Surah al-Ahzab is Madani.[[Al-Nahhas, in Ma'ani al-Qur'an al-Karim, p. 317, cites Ibn 'Abbas as saying: "It is Madani." Al-Suyuti, in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/558, also attributes this to Ibn al-Durays, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.]] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿O Prophet, fear Allah.﴾ It was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Abu al-A'war and 'Amr ibn Sufyan al-Sulami. They came to Medina and stayed with 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy [ibn Salul, the leader of the hypocrites] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "B".]] after the battle of Uhud. The Prophet ﷺ had granted them safe conduct so that they could speak with him. 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh and Tu'mah ibn Ubayriq accompanied them. They said to the Prophet ﷺ, while 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was with him: "Abandon the mention of our gods, al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, and say that they have intercession for whoever worships them, and we will leave you and your Lord alone." This grieved the Prophet ﷺ. 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit us to kill them." He said: "I have granted them safe conduct." 'Umar said: "Get out, under the curse and wrath of Allah!" The Prophet ﷺ then ordered 'Umar to expel them from Medina, and Allah the Exalted revealed:

﴿O Prophet, fear Allah.﴾ [[Al-Wahidi mentioned this in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 407, without a chain of transmission. Al-Qurtubi, 14/114, reported it in the weak form ("it is said") from al-Wahidi, al-Qushayri, al-Tha'labi, al-Mawardi and others. See also al-Farra', Ma'ani al-Qur'an 2/334.]] That is: persist in taqwa (God-consciousness), like a man who says to another who is standing: "Stand here", meaning: remain standing.

It is also said that the address is to the Prophet ﷺ while the intended meaning is the community (ummah).[[See al-Bahr al-Muhit 7/210, Zad al-Masir 6/348.]] Al-Dahhak said: its meaning is, "Fear Allah and do not break the covenant that is between you and them."

﴿And do not obey the disbelievers﴾ from the people of Mecca, meaning Abu Sufyan, 'Ikrimah and Abu al-A'war, ﴿and the hypocrites﴾ from the people of Medina, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'd and Tu'mah. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of His creation, before He created them, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He ordains for them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 33, verses 2–4:

﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do.﴾ Abu 'Amr recited "ya'maluna khabiran" and "ya'maluna basiran" with the *ya'* (third person) in both places. Others recited them with the *ta'* (second person).

﴿And rely upon Allah.﴾ Trust in Allah. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.﴾ As a Guardian over you. It was also said: as a Guarantor of your provision.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Allah has not made for any man two hearts within his chest.﴾ It was revealed concerning Abu Ma'mar Jamil ibn Ma'mar al-Fihri. He was an intelligent man who memorized what he heard, so the Quraysh said: "Abu Ma'mar would not have memorized these things unless he had two hearts." He used to say: "I have two hearts, and with each of them I understand better than the understanding of Muhammad." When Allah defeated the polytheists at the Battle of Badr, Abu Ma'mar fled among them. Abu Sufyan met him holding one of his sandals in his hand and the other on his foot. He said to him: "O Abu Ma'mar, what is the state of the people?" He said: "They have fled." He said: "Then what about one of your sandals being in your hand and the other on your foot?" Abu Ma'mar said: "I did not realize except that they were both on my foot." So they knew that day that, had he had two hearts, he would not have forgotten his sandal in his hand. [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in *Asbab al-Nuzul*, p. 407–408, without an isnad. See also: *al-Bahr al-Muhit*: 7/211; *Zad al-Masir*: 6/349.]]

Al-Zuhri and Muqatil said: this is a parable that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, struck for the one who makes his wife unlawful to himself through *zihar* (the pre-Islamic divorce formula of likening a wife to one's mother), and for the one who adopts the child of another. The meaning is: just as a man cannot have two hearts, so a woman cannot be the mother of one who makes *zihar* against her while she has two mothers, and a child cannot have two fathers. [[See: al-Tabari: 21/119, where he then said by way of preference: "The most correct of these sayings is the one who said: this is Allah's refutation of the one who said that a man has two hearts with which he understands, in the manner narrated from Ibn 'Abbas. It is permissible that this is Allah's refutation of the one who described the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with this, and that it is a refutation of the one who named the Qurashi whom he mentioned as 'the one with two hearts' from his own speech. Whichever of the two it was, it is Allah's negation concerning His creation of men being of that description." See also: al-Nahhas, *Ma'ani al-Qur'an al-Karim*, p. 318–320.]]

﴿Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce through zihar your mothers.﴾ The people of Syria and Kufa recited *"al-la'i"* here and in Surah al-Talaq with a *ya'* after the hamzah. Qalun, on the authority of Nafi', and Ya'qub recited it without a *ya'* after the hamzah. The others recited it with a softened hamzah. All of these are well-known dialectal forms. *"Tuzahiruna"* was recited by 'Asim with an alif, a *damma* on the *ta'*, and a *kasra* on the *ha'* lightened (*takhfif*). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited it with a *fatha* on the *ta'* and the *ha'*, lightened. Ibn 'Amir recited it with a *fatha* on both and a shaddah on the *za'*. The others recited it with a *fatha* on both, a shaddah on the *za'* and the *ha'*, without an alif between them.

The form of *zihar* is that a man says to his wife: "You are to me like the back of my mother." Allah, Exalted is He, says: He has not made your wives, whom you say this to in prohibition, to be like your mothers. Rather, it is a abominable speech and a falsehood. In it there is an expiation (*kaffarah*), which we will mention, God willing, in Surah al-Mujadalah.

﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons your sons.﴾ That is, those whom you have adopted. In it is the abrogation (*naskh*) of adoption. This is because a man in the pre-Islamic period would adopt a man and make him like a son born to him; people would call him by that name, and he would inherit his estate. The Prophet ﷺ had freed Zayd ibn Haritha ibn Sharahil al-Kalbi, and he had adopted him before the revelation. He also established a brotherhood between him and Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ married Zaynab bint Jahsh, who had been married to Zayd ibn Haritha, the hypocrites said: "Muhammad has married his son's wife, while he forbids the people from that." So Allah revealed this verse and abrogated adoption. [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in *Asbab al-Nuzul*, p. 408, without an isnad.]]

﴿That is your saying with your mouths.﴾ It has no reality. That is, their saying "Zayd ibn Muhammad ﷺ," and the claim of a lineage that has no reality. ﴿But Allah says the truth,﴾ that is, His saying is the truth. ﴿And He guides to the way.﴾ That is, He guides to the way of truth.

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir of Surah al-Ahzab, chapter "Call them by their fathers' names, that is more just in the sight of God," vol. 8, p. 517, and by Muslim in the Virtues of the Companions, chapter on the virtues of Zayd ibn Harithah, no. 2425, vol. 4, p. 1884.]].

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 6:

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾, meaning: more than they are to one another, in the enforceability of his judgment over them and the obligation of obeying him. Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ata' said: meaning, when the Prophet ﷺ calls them and their own selves call them to something, the obedience to the Prophet ﷺ takes precedence over their obedience to their own selves [[See: Zad al-Masir: 6 / 352.]]. Ibn Zayd said: the Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves in what he decides concerning them, just as you are closer to your slave in what you decide concerning him. It was also said: he is closer to them in urging them to jihad and in giving up their lives rather than him.

It was said: the Prophet ﷺ would go out to jihad, and a people would say: "We will go and ask permission from our fathers and our mothers," so the verse was revealed.

'Abd al-Wahid ibn 'Abd al-Maliki related to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us, Abu 'Amir related to us, Fulayh related to us, from Hilal ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Amra, from Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no believer except that I am closer to him in this world and the Hereafter." Recite, if you wish: ﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾. "Whichever believer dies and leaves property, let his male relatives inherit it; and whoever leaves a debt or dependants, let him come to me, for I am his guardian" [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Istiqrad, chapter: Prayer over one who leaves a debt, 5 / 61; and Muslim in al-Fara'id, chapter: Whoever leaves property, it belongs to his heirs, no. (1619), 3 / 1238, with similar meaning; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 8 / 324.]].

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and his wives are their mothers﴾. In the reading of Ubayy: "and his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them." They are the mothers of the believers in the honour owed to them and in the prohibition of marrying them forever, but not in looking at them or being alone with them, for that is forbidden with respect to them just as it is with respect to non-related men. God Most High said: ﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53]. Their daughters are not called sisters of the believers, nor are their brothers and sisters called maternal uncles and aunts of the believers [[See al-Qurtubi: 14 / 123.]].

Al-Shafi'i said: al-Zubayr married Asma' bint Abi Bakr, and she was the sister of the Mother of the Believers, yet he did not say: she is the maternal aunt of the believers [[See al-Qurtubi: 14 / 123.]].

They differed as to whether they were the mothers of all believing women. It was said: they were the mothers of the believing men and women alike.

It was also said: they were the mothers of the believing men only, not the women. Al-Sha'bi narrated from Masruq that a woman said to 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her: "She said: O Mother!" Then she said: "I am not a mother to you; I am only the mother of your men" [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6 / 567 to Ibn Sa'd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan; and see al-Kafi al-Shafi p. 132.]]. Thus, by this, the meaning of this motherhood became clear: the prohibition of marrying them.

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And those of kinship are closer to one another in the Book of Allah﴾. Meaning: in inheritance. Qatada said: the Muslims used to inherit from one another by emigration. Al-Kalbi said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ established brotherhood among the people, so he would pair two men, and when one of them died, the other would inherit from him to the exclusion of his male relatives, until this verse was revealed: ﴿And those of kinship are closer to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [[See: Ibn Kathir in al-Tafsir: 3 / 469; al-Qurtubi: 14 / 123–124.]] [76a] in the ruling of Allah, ﴿from among the believers﴾ whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had paired, ﴿and the emigrants﴾, meaning those with blood ties: some of them are closer to inheriting from one another than inheriting by faith and emigration. So this verse abrogated inheritance by brotherhood and emigration, and it became by kinship.

The words: ﴿except that you do kindness to your allies﴾. By "kindness" he meant the bequest [to those who support him among the contracting parties; this is because when Allah abrogated inheritance by the oath of alliance and emigration, He permitted a man to bequeath to whoever supports him whatever he wished from his third] [[What is between the brackets is missing from "B".]].

Mujahid said: by "kindness" he meant support and preserving the sanctity owed to the right of faith and emigration.

It was said: the verse intends the establishment of inheritance through faith and emigration, meaning: "those of kinship among the believers and the emigrants are closer to one another," that is, there is no inheritance between a Muslim and a disbeliever, nor between an emigrant and a non-emigrant, except that you do kindness to your allies, that is, except that you bequeath something to your relatives even if they are not of the people of faith and emigration. This is the view of Qatada, 'Ata' and 'Ikrima [[Al-Tabari mentioned these views: 21 / 124, then said, giving preference: "The most correct of the views in my judgment is that the meaning is: except that you do kindness to your allies whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ paired between you and them, from the emigrants and the Helpers, by way of bequest to them, support, and paying blood-money on their behalf, and the like, for all of that is kindness which Allah has enjoined upon His servants. I have chosen this view and said it is more correct than the view of those who said it refers to bequests to relatives who are polytheists, because a relative who is a polytheist, though he is of kin, is not a close ally, for polytheism severs the bond between the believer and the polytheist, and Allah has forbidden the believers to take them as allies by saying: 'Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies.' It is not permissible that He forbid them from taking them as allies and then describe them, glorified be His praise, as being allies."]].

﴿That was written in the Book as inscribed﴾, meaning: what I have mentioned, that those of kinship are closer to one another, was inscribed and written in the Preserved Tablet. Al-Qurazi said: it is in the Torah.

The Exalted said: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the Prophets their covenant﴾, to fulfil what they were entrusted with, and that some of them would confirm others and give glad tidings of one another.

Muqatil said: He took their covenant that they would worship Allah, call people to the worship of Allah, confirm one another, and give sincere counsel to their peoples. ﴿And [from] you, and [from] Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa son of Maryam﴾. These five were singled out from among the Prophets because they were the possessors of Scriptures and laws, and the Ulu al-'Azm (the Resolute Messengers). He mentioned the Prophet (ﷺ) first for what was narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadithi informed me; 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Ya'qub al-Muqri' informed us; Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Sa'idi informed us; Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Bakkar ibn Bilal informed us; my father informed us; Sa'id, that is Ibn Bashir, informed us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was the first of the Prophets in creation and the last of them in being sent forth."[[Recorded by al-Tabari (21/125). Ibn Kathir, in his Tafsir (3/470), attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim and said: "Sa'id ibn Bashir is weak in it. Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated it from Qatadah as a mursal report, and that is closer to correct. Some narrated it from Qatadah as a mawquf report. And Allah knows best."]]

Qatadah said: This is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And [mention] when We took from the Prophets their covenant, and from you, and from Nuh﴾, so He began with him (ﷺ) before them.

﴿And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾: a firm pledge to fulfil what they were entrusted with.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verses 8–9 (part 1 of 3):**

﴿That He may ask the truthful about their truthfulness﴾. He says: We took their covenant [﴿so that We may ask the truthful about their truthfulness﴾, meaning the prophets about their conveying] [[What is between the brackets is missing from "A".]] the message. The wisdom in asking them, although He knows that they are truthful, is the rebuke [[In "B": "denial"]] of those to whom they were sent.

It was also said: ﴿That He may ask the truthful﴾ about their deeds for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It was also said: ﴿That He may ask the truthful﴾ with their mouths about their truthfulness in their hearts.

﴿And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment﴾. The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you﴾. This was when the Muslims were besieged with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the days of the Trench (al-Khandaq), ﴿when there came to you armies﴾, meaning the confederates (al-Ahzab), who were Quraysh, Ghatafan, and the Jews of Banu Qurayza and al-Nadir. ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾, and it was the eastern wind (al-Saba). Ikrimah said: The south wind said to the north wind on the night of the confederates, "Let us go and help the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The north wind replied, "The heat does not travel at night." The wind that was sent upon them was the eastern wind (al-Saba) [[See: al-Qurtubi: 14/143–144.]].

Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Adam informed us, Shu'ba informed us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I have been supported by the eastern wind, and 'Ad were destroyed by the western wind" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Istisqa', chapter: The saying of the Prophet ﷺ, "I have been supported by the eastern wind," 2/52; and Muslim in al-Istisqa', chapter: On the eastern and western winds, no. (900), 2/617; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/387.
Al-Saba: a wind, and its regular direction is that it blows from the rising of the sun when night and day are equal.
Al-Daboor: the wind opposite to al-Saba. Al-Nawawi said: it is the western wind.]].

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And armies you did not see﴾, and they were the angels. The angels did not fight on that day, but Allah sent upon them, that night, a cold wind which uprooted the tent pegs, cut the ropes of the tents, extinguished the fires, overturned the cooking pots, and made the horses run wild among one another. The angels' takbir was loud on the sides of their camp, until the chief of every tribe would say, "O Banu so-and-so, come to me!" When they gathered around him, he would say, "Escape! Escape!" because of the terror Allah had cast into them. So they fled without fighting.

﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ruman, client of the family of al-Zubayr, narrated to me, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr and one whom I do not suspect, from Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, and from al-Zuhri, and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakra ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, and from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and from others of our scholars, the narrations of some of them entered into those of others: that a group of Jews, among them Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Kinana ibn al-Rabi' ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Hawdha ibn Qays, and Abu Ammar al-Wa'ili, along with a group from Banu al-Nadir and a group from Banu Wa'il, who were the ones who incited the confederates against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, went out until they came to Quraysh in Makkah. They called them to war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "We will be with you against him until we uproot him." Quraysh said to them, "O assembly of Jews, you are the people of the first Book and knowledge. Tell us, is our religion better, or is his religion?" They said, "Rather, your religion is better than his, and you are more entitled to the truth than they are." So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who believe in superstition and false deities?﴾ up to His saying ﴿And sufficient is Hell as a blazing fire﴾ (al-Nisa' 51–55).

When they had said that to Quraysh, what they said pleased them, and they became eager for what they had invited them to, namely the war against the Messenger of Allah. So they united for that. Then those men of the Jews went out until they came to Ghatafan of Qays Ghaylan, invited them to that, and informed them that they would be with them in it, and that Quraysh had already pledged to them to do so. So they answered them.

Quraysh went out, and its leader was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. Ghatafan went out, and its leader was Uyayna ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfa ibn Badr in Fazara, and al-Harith ibn Awf ibn Abi Haritha al-Murri among Banu Murra, and Mas'ud ibn Rukhayla ibn Nuwayra ibn Tarif with those of his people who followed him from Ashja' (76/b).

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of them and of what they had gathered against him, he dug the trench around Madinah.

The one who advised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to dig the trench was Salman al-Farisi, and it was the first battle Salman witnessed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was then a free man. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when we were in Persia and were besieged, we dug a trench around ourselves." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims worked on it until they perfected it [[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq in the Sirah, from Ibn Hisham: 3/214 and following; and al-Tabari recorded it: 21/129–131.]].

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isbahani informed us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tabari informed us, Hammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Atha narrated to us, Kathir ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Awf, my father narrated to me from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ marked out the trench in the year of the confederates, then he allotted forty cubits to every ten men. He said: The Emigrants and the Helpers disputed over Salman al-Farisi, who was a strong man. The Emigrants said, "Salman is one of us," and the Helpers said, "Salman is one of us." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House" [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 21/133–134; al-Hakim: 3/598, and he was silent about it; al-Dhahabi said: its chain is weak; and al-Tabarani: 6/261. See: Kashf al-Khafa' wa Muzil al-Ilbas: 1/558. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/130: al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Kathir ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, whom the majority have declared weak, though al-Tirmidhi graded his narration as good, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy.]].

Amr ibn Awf said: I, Salman, Hudhayfa, al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin al-Mazini, and six men from the Helpers were on forty cubits. We dug until, when we were beneath Dhu Nab, Allah brought forth in the bottom of the trench a white, hard rock which broke our iron tools and was hard upon us. We said, "O Salman, go up to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and inform him about this rock. Either he will divert us from it, for the diversion is near, or he will command us about it, for we do not wish to exceed his line." Salman went up to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was pitching a Turkish tent over himself, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a white, hard rock has emerged from the bottom of the trench, broken our iron tools, and is so hard upon us that little or much does not bite into it. So command us about it, for we do not wish to exceed your line." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ descended with Salman into the trench, and the nine men were on the side of the trench. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the pickaxe from Salman and struck it with a blow that split it, and a flash came from it that lit up what was between its two stony tracts (meaning Madinah), until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cried out "Allahu akbar" in a cry of conquest, and the Muslims cried out too. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck it a second time, and a flash came from it that lit up what was between its two stony tracts, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cried out in a cry of conquest, and the Muslims cried out too. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck it and broke it, and a flash came from it that lit up what was between its two stony tracts, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cried out in a cry of conquest, and the Muslims cried out too. He took Salman by the hand and ascended, and Salman said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, I have seen a thing the like of which I have never seen before." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to the people and said: "Did you see what Salman says?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "I struck my first blow, and the flash you saw appeared, and the palaces of al-Hira and the cities of Kisra were shown to me as if they were dogs' fangs. Jibril informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my second blow, and the flash you saw appeared, and the palaces of al-Hira from the land of the Romans were shown to me as if they were dogs' fangs. Jibril informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my third blow, and the flash you saw appeared, and the palaces of San'a' were shown to me as if they were dogs' fangs, and Jibril, peace be upon him, informed me that my community will prevail over them. So rejoice!" The Muslims rejoiced and said, "Praise be to Allah, a true promise. He promised us victory after siege." But the hypocrites said: "Do you not marvel at Muhammad? He promises you and gives you false hopes, and tells you that he sees from Yathrib the palaces of al-Hira and the cities of Kisra, and that they will be conquered for you, while you are digging the trench out of fear and cannot even go out to fight!" So the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us only delusion"﴾, and Allah revealed this story: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Owner of sovereignty"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 26] and the rest of the verse [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 21/134. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma': 6/131: al-Tabarani narrated it through two chains, in one of which is Hayy ibn Abd Allah, whom Ibn Ma'in declared trustworthy, though many declared him weak; and its remaining narrators are the narrators of the Sahih. See also: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 3/214–219.]].

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us, Mu'awiya ibn Amr informed us, Abu Ishaq informed us, from Humayd who said: I heard Anas say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the trench, and there were the Emigrants and the Helpers digging on a cold morning. They had no slaves to do that work for them. When he saw what they were suffering of fatigue and hunger, he said: "O Allah, indeed life is the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Helpers and the Emigrants." They replied to him: "We are those who pledged to Muhammad to fight jihad as long as we live forever." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter: The Battle of the Trench: 7/392; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/4.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi also informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Shu'ba informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: The Prophet ﷺ was carrying earth on the day of the Trench until it covered his belly, or dusted it, and he was saying:

By Allah, had it not been for Allah, we would not have been guided,
nor would we have given charity nor prayed.
So send down tranquility upon us,
and make our feet firm if we meet [the enemy].
Indeed, those who have transgressed against us,
whenever they desire strife, we refuse.

And he raised his voice with it: "We refuse, we refuse!" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter: The Battle of the Trench: 7/399; Muslim in al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, chapter: The Battle of the Confederates, no. (1803), 3/1430–1431; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/4–5.]]

We returned to the narration of Ibn Ishaq, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished with the trench, the Quraysh came and descended at Mujtama' al-Asyal, from Rumah, between al-Jurf and al-Ghaba [[In the Sirat Ibn Hisham: 3/220 it reads "Zughaba." Abu Dharr said: "Thus it occurs here with a fatha on the za', but "Raghaba" with a fatha on the ra' is the sound reading, and al-Waqshi also transmitted it that way."]] with ten thousand of their confederates (al-ahabish, allied tribes), and those who followed them from Banu Kinanah and the people of Tihamah. The Ghatafan and those who followed them from the people of Najd also came and descended at Dhanab Naqma, beside Uhud. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims went out until they placed their backs to Sal' with three thousand Muslims. There he pitched his camp, with the trench between him and the enemy. He ordered the women and children to be lifted up into the fortified towers (al-atam).

The enemy of Allah, Huyayy ibn Akhtab of Banu al-Nadir, went out until he came to Ka'b ibn Asad al-Qurazi, the holder of the pact and covenant of Banu Qurayzah. Ka'b had made a truce with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on behalf of his people and had made a covenant with him on this. When Ka'b heard of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, he closed his fortress against him. He asked permission to enter, but Ka'b refused to open to him. Huyayy called out: "O Ka'b, open for me!" Ka'b said: "Woe to you, O Huyayy, you are an ill-omened man, and I have made a covenant with Muhammad, so I will not break what is between me and him. I have seen from him nothing but fidelity and truthfulness." Huyayy said: "Woe to you, open for me, that I may speak with you." Ka'b said: "I will not do that." Huyayy said: "By Allah, if you close off to me, it is only out of concern that I might eat with you from your food." So the man was ashamed, and he opened to him. Huyayy said: "Woe to you, O Ka'b! I have brought you the might of the age and a surging sea. I have brought you Quraysh with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at Mujtama' al-Asyal from Rumah, and the Ghatafan with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at Dhanab Naqma beside Uhud. They have pledged to me and bound themselves to me that they will not depart until they uproot Muhammad and those with him."

Ka'b ibn Asad said to him: "By Allah, you have brought me the humiliation of the age, and a rainless cloud whose water has been spilled with thunder and lightning, but there is nothing in it. So leave me with Muhammad and what I am upon, for I have seen from Muhammad nothing but truthfulness and fidelity." Huyayy ibn Akhtab kept at Ka'b, twisting him by the forelock and the back, until he consented, on condition that Huyayy gave him a pledge and covenant from Allah: "If Quraysh and Ghatafan return without having struck Muhammad, I will enter with you into your fortress, so that what befalls you will befall me." Ka'b ibn Asad then broke his covenant and disowned what was between him and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

When the news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, of Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, who was then the chief of the Aws, and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, of Banu Sa'idah, who was then the chief of the Khazraj, and with them 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah, brother of Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and Khawwat ibn Jubayr, brother of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf. He said: "Go and see whether what has reached us about these people is true or not. If it is true, then speak to me in a way I will understand, and do not weaken the resolve of the people. If they are upholding the fidelity between us and them, then declare it openly to the people." So they went out until they reached them, and found them at the worst of what had been reported of them. They slandered the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "There is no pact between us and Muhammad, nor any covenant." Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah exchanged insults with them, and they insulted him in return, for he was a man of hot temper. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to him: "Leave off insulting them, for what lies between us and them is worse than insults." Then Sa'd and Sa'd and those with them came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, greeted him, and said: "'Adal and al-Qarah!" meaning the treachery of 'Adal and al-Qarah against the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the companions of al-Raji': Khubayb ibn 'Adi and his companions." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allahu Akbar! Rejoice, O assembly of Muslims!"

At that point the affliction grew severe and the fear intensified. The enemy came at them from above them and from below them, until the believers thought every kind of thought. Hypocrisy stirred up among some of the hypocrites, until Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, brother of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, said: "Muhammad used to promise us that we would eat the treasures of Khosrow and Caesar, while not one of us can go out to relieve himself. Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." And Aws ibn Qayzi, of Banu Harithah ibn Qayzi, said: "O Messenger of Allah, our houses are exposed to the enemy," and this was in the presence of a group of men from his people. "So give us permission, and we will return to our homes, for they lie outside Medina."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained, and the polytheists remained encamped against him for some twenty nights, close to a month. There was no fighting between the two sides except shooting with arrows and pebbles.

When the affliction grew severe upon the people, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn and al-Harith ibn 'Awf, who were the two leaders of the Ghatafan, and offered them a third of the produce of Medina, on condition that they would turn back with those who were with them from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions. A peace was agreed between him and them, until they wrote the document, but the witnessing had not yet taken place. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned this to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah and sought their counsel about it. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this something Allah has commanded you, which we must act upon? Or is it a matter you wish and so you do it? Or is it something you do for us?" He said: "No, rather it is something I do for you. By Allah, I do this only because I have seen the Arabs shoot at you from one bow and gang up on you from every side, so I wanted to break their strength away from you." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of Allah, we and these people were upon shirk with Allah and worship of idols, not worshipping Allah nor knowing Him, and they did not expect to eat a single date from Medina except as hospitality or by purchase. Now that Allah has honored us with Islam and strengthened us through you, shall we give them our wealth? We have no need of this. By Allah, we will give them nothing but the sword, until Allah judges between us and them." [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:] "Then the matter is yours." Sa'd took the document and erased what was written in it, then said: "Let them strive against us."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims remained, while their enemy besieged them, and there was no fighting between them, except that some horsemen of Quraysh, among them 'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd of Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Hubayrah ibn Abi Wahb, both of Makhzum, and Nawfal ibn 'Abd Allah, and Dirar ibn al-Khattab, and Mirdas, brother of Banu Muharib ibn Fihr, had armed themselves for battle. They rode out on their horses and passed by Banu Kinanah and said: "Prepare for war, O Banu Kinanah! Today you will know who the true horsemen are." Then they advanced toward the trench until they stopped at the trench. When they saw it they said: "By Allah, this is a stratagem that the Arabs have never used."

Then they sought a narrow spot in the trench and urged their horses, and the horses leapt across it. They roamed with them in the salt flats between the trench and Sal'. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib went out with a group of Muslims until they seized the gap through which they had driven their horses across. The horsemen came charging toward them. 'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd, who had fought at Badr, had been left lame by his wound, [so he did not attend Uhud]. On the day of the trench he came out marked with a distinguishing sign so that his position could be seen. When he and his horse stood still, 'Ali said to him: "O 'Amr, you used to pledge to Allah that whenever a man of Quraysh called you to one of two things, you would take one of them from him." He said: "Indeed." 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said to him: "I call you to Allah, to His Messenger, and to Islam." He said: "I have no need of that." He said: "Then I call you to single combat." He said: "Why, O nephew? By Allah, I do not wish to kill you." 'Ali said: "But by Allah, I wish to kill you." At that 'Amr grew furious, leapt down from his horse, hamstrung it, and struck its face. Then he turned upon 'Ali, and they grappled and fought, and 'Ali killed him. His horsemen then fled in defeat until they plunged into the trench in flight.

With 'Amr were killed two men: Munabbih ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Ubayd ibn al-Sabbaq ibn 'Abd al-Dar, who was struck by an arrow and died from it in Mecca; and Nawfal ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, who had plunged into the trench, became stuck in it, and they pelted him with stones. He said: "O assembly of Arabs, his killing is better than this!" 'Ali descended to him and killed him. The Muslims then gained possession of his body, and they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to sell them his body. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We have no need of his body or its price; do with it as you wish." So he left them free to deal with it.

'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, said: On the day of the trench we were in the fortress of Banu Harithah, which was among the most secure fortresses of Medina. The mother of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was with us in the fortress, and that was before the veil was prescribed for us. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh passed by wearing a short coat of mail, from which his entire forearm had come out, and in his hand was a spear, and he was saying:

"Wait a little, you will reach the battle that rages;
There is no harm in death when its term has come."

His mother said to him: "Hurry, my son, for by Allah you have fallen behind!" 'A'ishah said: I said to her: "O Umm Sa'd, by Allah, I wished that Sa'd's coat of mail were more complete than it is." She said: "And I feared for him where the arrow would strike him." She said: On that day Sa'd was struck by an arrow, and his main vein (al-akhal) was cut. It was shot by Khabbab ibn Qays ibn al-'Araqah, of Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy. When it struck him he said: "Take it, and I am the son of al-'Araqah!" Sa'd said: "May Allah make your face black in the Fire!" Then Sa'd said: "O Allah, if You have left any part of the war with Quraysh, then preserve me for it, for there is no people more beloved to me to fight than a people who harmed Your Messenger, denied him, and expelled him. And if You have ended the war between us and them, then make this a martyrdom for me, and do not let me die until my eyes are refreshed concerning Banu Qurayzah, who were his allies and clients in the pre-Islamic era." [See the full narration in the Sirat Ibn Hisham: 3/219–227.]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father Abbad, who said: Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib was in Fari', the fort of Hassan ibn Thabit. She said: Hassan was with us in it, along with the women and children. Safiyyah said: A Jewish man passed by us and began circling the fort, while Banu Qurayzah had gone to war. They had cut off what lay between us and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and there was no one between us and them to repel them for us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims were engaged in the throats of their enemy, unable to turn away from them toward us if someone came to us. She said: I said, "O Hassan, this Jew, as you see, is circling the fort. By Allah, I do not feel safe that he will point out our weak points to the Jews behind us, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions are preoccupied with us. So go down to him and kill him." He said, "May Allah forgive you, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib! By Allah, you know that I am not the one to do this." She said: When he said that to me and I saw nothing with him, I tightened my waist-wrap, then took a pole and went down from the fort to him, and I struck him with the pole until I killed him. When I had finished with him, I returned to the fort and said, "O Hassan, go down to him and strip him of his armor, for nothing prevented me from stripping him except that he was a man." He said, "I have no need of his spoils, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib."[[انظر: سيرة ابن هشام: ٣ / ٢٢٨-٢٣٠.]] (See: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 3/228–230.)

They said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions remained in the state that Allah Most High described: fear and hardship, because of the massing of their enemy and their coming at them from above them and from below them.

Then Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud ibn Amir of Ghatafan came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have embraced Islam, and my people do not know of my Islam, so command me with whatever you wish." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "You are just one man among us, so sow discord against them if you are able, for war is deception." Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud went out until he came to Banu Qurayzah, and he had been their boon companion in the pre-Islamic period. He said to them: "O Banu Qurayzah, you know my affection for you and the special bond between me and you." They said: "You have spoken truly; you are not suspected by us." He said to them: "Quraysh and Ghatafan have come to fight Muhammad, and you have backed them against him. Quraysh and Ghatafan are not in the same situation as you. This land is your land; your wealth, your children and your women are in it, and you cannot move away from it to another place. Quraysh and Ghatafan, however, their wealth, their children and their women are far away. If they see a raid and booty they can take, they will take it; if it is otherwise, they will return to their lands and leave you alone with the man, and the man is in your land, and you have no power against him if he is alone with you. So do not fight alongside these people until you take from them hostages from their nobles, who will remain in your hands as a guarantee for you that they will fight alongside you against Muhammad, until you engage him." They said: "You have given sound and sincere counsel."

Then he went out until he came to Quraysh, and he said to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those of the men of Quraysh with him: "O assembly of Quraysh, you know my affection for you and my estrangement from Muhammad. A matter has reached me, and I saw it as a duty upon me to convey it to you as sincere advice, so keep it secret from me." They said, "We will." He said: "You know that the Jews have regretted what they did between them and Muhammad, and they have sent to him: 'We have regretted what we did.' Would it please you that we take from the two tribes, Quraysh and Ghatafan, men of their nobles, and give them to you, so that you may strike their necks, and then we will be with you against those who remain of them?" He sent back to them: "Yes." So if the Jews send to you seeking hostages from your men, do not give them a single man from you."

Then he went out until he came to Ghatafan and said: "O assembly of Ghatafan, you are my origin, my clan, and the people dearest to me, and I do not think you suspect me." They said, "You have spoken truly." He said, "Then keep it secret from me." They said, "We will." Then he said to them the same as he had said to Quraysh, and warned them as he had warned them.

When it was the night of Saturday in Shawwal in the fifth year, and among what [Nu'aym] had done for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Sufyan and the chiefs of Ghatafan sent to Banu Qurayzah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl with a group of Quraysh and Ghatafan, and they said to them: "We are not a people who remain in one place; the hoof and the hoofed beast have perished. So go out to fight, so that we may engage Muhammad and finish with what is between us and him." Banu Qurayzah said to them: "Today is Saturday, a day on which we do no work at all, and some of us previously committed an offense on it, and what befell them is not hidden from you. And we are not, in addition to that, going to fight alongside you until you give us hostages from your men, who will remain in our hands as a guarantee for us until we engage Muhammad, for we fear that if the war overwhelms you and the fighting becomes severe for you, you will set out for your lands and leave us, with the man in our land, and we have no power against Muhammad." When the messengers returned to them with what Banu Qurayzah had said, Quraysh and Ghatafan said: "By Allah, you know that what Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud told you is true." So they sent to Banu Qurayzah: "By Allah, we will not give you a single man from our men. If you want to fight, then come out and fight." Banu Qurayzah said, when the messengers reached them with this: "What Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud mentioned to you is true. These people only want to fight. If they find an opportunity they will seize it, and if it is otherwise they will flee to their lands and leave you alone with the man in your land." So they sent to Quraysh and Ghatafan: "By Allah, we will not fight alongside you until you give us hostages." They refused them, and Allah caused discord between them. And Allah sent upon them a wind during cold, bitter winter nights, which overturned their cooking pots and cast down their vessels.

When the news of what had divided them reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he called Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and sent him to them to see what the people were doing at night.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others related from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, both of them saying: A young man from the people of Kufa said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: "O Abu Abd Allah, did you see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and keep his company?" He said, "Yes, nephew." He said: "How did you use to act?" He said: "By Allah, we used to strive hard." The young man said: "By Allah, if we had reached him we would not have let him walk on the earth; we would have carried him on our necks and served him, and we would have done this and that." Hudhayfah said: "Nephew, by Allah, I saw myself on the night of the Confederates with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'Who will stand up and go to these people and bring us news of them? Allah will admit him to Paradise.' None of us stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed during a part of the night, then turned to us and said the same. The people were silent, and none of us stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed during a part of the night, then turned to us and said: 'Who is the man who will stand up and look at what the people are doing, on condition that he will be my companion in Paradise?' None of the men stood up, from the intensity of fear, the intensity of hunger and the intensity of cold. When no one stood up, he called me, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said, 'O Hudhayfah!' I had no choice but to rise to him when he called me, so I said, 'At your service, O Messenger of Allah,' and I stood up until I came to him, and my sides were trembling. He wiped my head and face, then said: 'Go to these people until you bring me news of them, and do not do anything until you return to me.' Then he said, 'O Allah, protect him from before him, behind him, from his right, from his left, from above him and from below him.' So I took my arrow, and I girded my weapons, then set off walking toward them as if I were walking in a bathhouse. I went and entered among the people, and Allah had sent upon them a wind and hosts of Allah, doing to them what it did. It left them no cooking pot, no fire and no structure. Abu Sufyan was sitting warming himself by the fire. I took an arrow and placed it on the belly of my bow, and I intended to shoot him, and had I shot him I would have hit him. But I remembered the Prophet's (ﷺ) words: 'Do not do anything until you return to me,' so I returned the arrow to my quiver." When Abu Sufyan saw what the wind and the hosts of Allah were doing to them, leaving them no cooking pot, no fire and no structure, he stood up and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, let each one of you take the hand of the man beside him and see who he is." I took the hand of the man beside me and said, "Who are you?" He said, "Subhan Allah! Do you not know me? I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so." He was a man from Hawazin.

Then Abu Sufyan said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, you have not reached a place to remain. The horses and the camels have perished, Banu Qurayzah have broken their word to us, and we have received from them what we dislike, and we have encountered this wind, as you see. So depart, for I am departing." Then he went to his camel, which was tethered, and sat upon it, then struck it, and it leaped with him on three legs. He did not release its tether until it was standing. Ghatafan heard what Quraysh had done, so they turned back to their lands.

He said: I returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as if I were walking in a bathhouse, and I came to him while he was standing and praying. When he finished the prayer of salutation, I informed him of the news, and he laughed until his canine teeth showed in the darkness of the night. He said: When I had informed him and finished, I felt a chill, and the warmth left me.

The Prophet (ﷺ) drew me close to him, made me sleep at his feet, cast the edge of his garment over me, and pressed my chest against the soles of his feet. I did not cease sleeping until morning. When I woke up, he said: "Get up, O sleeper!"[[أخرجه مسلم في الجهاد باب: غزو الأحزاب برقم (١٧٨٨) : ٣ / ١٤١٤-١٤١٥.]] (Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Jihad, chapter: The Battle of the Confederates, no. 1788: 3/1414–1415.)

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verses 8–9 (part 1 of 3):**

﴿That He may ask the truthful about their truthfulness﴾. He says: We took their covenant [﴿so that We may ask the truthful about their truthfulness﴾, meaning the prophets about their conveying] [[What is between the brackets is missing from "A".]] the message. The wisdom in asking them, although He knows that they are truthful, is the rebuke [[In "B": "denial"]] of those to whom they were sent.

It was also said: ﴿That He may ask the truthful﴾ about their deeds for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It was also said: ﴿That He may ask the truthful﴾ with their mouths about their truthfulness in their hearts.

﴿And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment﴾. The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you﴾. This was when the Muslims were besieged with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ during the days of the Trench (al-Khandaq), ﴿when there came to you armies﴾, meaning the confederates (al-Ahzab), who were Quraysh, Ghatafan, and the Jews of Banu Qurayza and al-Nadir. ﴿So We sent upon them a wind﴾, and it was the eastern wind (al-Saba). Ikrimah said: The south wind said to the north wind on the night of the confederates, "Let us go and help the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." The north wind replied, "The heat does not travel at night." The wind that was sent upon them was the eastern wind (al-Saba) [[See: al-Qurtubi: 14/143–144.]].

Al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Adam informed us, Shu'ba informed us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "I have been supported by the eastern wind, and 'Ad were destroyed by the western wind" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Istisqa', chapter: The saying of the Prophet ﷺ, "I have been supported by the eastern wind," 2/52; and Muslim in al-Istisqa', chapter: On the eastern and western winds, no. (900), 2/617; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/387.
Al-Saba: a wind, and its regular direction is that it blows from the rising of the sun when night and day are equal.
Al-Daboor: the wind opposite to al-Saba. Al-Nawawi said: it is the western wind.]].

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And armies you did not see﴾, and they were the angels. The angels did not fight on that day, but Allah sent upon them, that night, a cold wind which uprooted the tent pegs, cut the ropes of the tents, extinguished the fires, overturned the cooking pots, and made the horses run wild among one another. The angels' takbir was loud on the sides of their camp, until the chief of every tribe would say, "O Banu so-and-so, come to me!" When they gathered around him, he would say, "Escape! Escape!" because of the terror Allah had cast into them. So they fled without fighting.

﴿And Allah is ever Seeing of what you do﴾. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yazid ibn Ruman, client of the family of al-Zubayr, narrated to me, from Urwa ibn al-Zubayr and one whom I do not suspect, from Abd Allah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, and from al-Zuhri, and Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakra ibn Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Hazm, and from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and from others of our scholars, the narrations of some of them entered into those of others: that a group of Jews, among them Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Kinana ibn al-Rabi' ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Hawdha ibn Qays, and Abu Ammar al-Wa'ili, along with a group from Banu al-Nadir and a group from Banu Wa'il, who were the ones who incited the confederates against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, went out until they came to Quraysh in Makkah. They called them to war against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "We will be with you against him until we uproot him." Quraysh said to them, "O assembly of Jews, you are the people of the first Book and knowledge. Tell us, is our religion better, or is his religion?" They said, "Rather, your religion is better than his, and you are more entitled to the truth than they are." So Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who believe in superstition and false deities?﴾ up to His saying ﴿And sufficient is Hell as a blazing fire﴾ (al-Nisa' 51–55).

When they had said that to Quraysh, what they said pleased them, and they became eager for what they had invited them to, namely the war against the Messenger of Allah. So they united for that. Then those men of the Jews went out until they came to Ghatafan of Qays Ghaylan, invited them to that, and informed them that they would be with them in it, and that Quraysh had already pledged to them to do so. So they answered them.

Quraysh went out, and its leader was Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. Ghatafan went out, and its leader was Uyayna ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfa ibn Badr in Fazara, and al-Harith ibn Awf ibn Abi Haritha al-Murri among Banu Murra, and Mas'ud ibn Rukhayla ibn Nuwayra ibn Tarif with those of his people who followed him from Ashja' (76/b).

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard of them and of what they had gathered against him, he dug the trench around Madinah.

The one who advised the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to dig the trench was Salman al-Farisi, and it was the first battle Salman witnessed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was then a free man. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when we were in Persia and were besieged, we dug a trench around ourselves." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims worked on it until they perfected it [[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq in the Sirah, from Ibn Hisham: 3/214 and following; and al-Tabari recorded it: 21/129–131.]].

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isbahani informed us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Tabari informed us, Hammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Atha narrated to us, Kathir ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Awf, my father narrated to me from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ marked out the trench in the year of the confederates, then he allotted forty cubits to every ten men. He said: The Emigrants and the Helpers disputed over Salman al-Farisi, who was a strong man. The Emigrants said, "Salman is one of us," and the Helpers said, "Salman is one of us." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House" [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 21/133–134; al-Hakim: 3/598, and he was silent about it; al-Dhahabi said: its chain is weak; and al-Tabarani: 6/261. See: Kashf al-Khafa' wa Muzil al-Ilbas: 1/558. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/130: al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Kathir ibn Abd Allah al-Muzani, whom the majority have declared weak, though al-Tirmidhi graded his narration as good, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy.]].

Amr ibn Awf said: I, Salman, Hudhayfa, al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin al-Mazini, and six men from the Helpers were on forty cubits. We dug until, when we were beneath Dhu Nab, Allah brought forth in the bottom of the trench a white, hard rock which broke our iron tools and was hard upon us. We said, "O Salman, go up to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and inform him about this rock. Either he will divert us from it, for the diversion is near, or he will command us about it, for we do not wish to exceed his line." Salman went up to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who was pitching a Turkish tent over himself, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a white, hard rock has emerged from the bottom of the trench, broken our iron tools, and is so hard upon us that little or much does not bite into it. So command us about it, for we do not wish to exceed your line." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ descended with Salman into the trench, and the nine men were on the side of the trench. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took the pickaxe from Salman and struck it with a blow that split it, and a flash came from it that lit up what was between its two stony tracts (meaning Madinah), until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cried out "Allahu akbar" in a cry of conquest, and the Muslims cried out too. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck it a second time, and a flash came from it that lit up what was between its two stony tracts, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cried out in a cry of conquest, and the Muslims cried out too. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck it and broke it, and a flash came from it that lit up what was between its two stony tracts, until it was as if a lamp were in the middle of a dark house. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ cried out in a cry of conquest, and the Muslims cried out too. He took Salman by the hand and ascended, and Salman said: "May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, I have seen a thing the like of which I have never seen before." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to the people and said: "Did you see what Salman says?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "I struck my first blow, and the flash you saw appeared, and the palaces of al-Hira and the cities of Kisra were shown to me as if they were dogs' fangs. Jibril informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my second blow, and the flash you saw appeared, and the palaces of al-Hira from the land of the Romans were shown to me as if they were dogs' fangs. Jibril informed me that my community will prevail over them. Then I struck my third blow, and the flash you saw appeared, and the palaces of San'a' were shown to me as if they were dogs' fangs, and Jibril, peace be upon him, informed me that my community will prevail over them. So rejoice!" The Muslims rejoiced and said, "Praise be to Allah, a true promise. He promised us victory after siege." But the hypocrites said: "Do you not marvel at Muhammad? He promises you and gives you false hopes, and tells you that he sees from Yathrib the palaces of al-Hira and the cities of Kisra, and that they will be conquered for you, while you are digging the trench out of fear and cannot even go out to fight!" So the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, "Allah and His Messenger promised us only delusion"﴾, and Allah revealed this story: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Owner of sovereignty"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 26] and the rest of the verse [[Recorded by al-Tabari: 21/134. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma': 6/131: al-Tabarani narrated it through two chains, in one of which is Hayy ibn Abd Allah, whom Ibn Ma'in declared trustworthy, though many declared him weak; and its remaining narrators are the narrators of the Sahih. See also: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 3/214–219.]].

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us, Mu'awiya ibn Amr informed us, Abu Ishaq informed us, from Humayd who said: I heard Anas say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the trench, and there were the Emigrants and the Helpers digging on a cold morning. They had no slaves to do that work for them. When he saw what they were suffering of fatigue and hunger, he said: "O Allah, indeed life is the life of the Hereafter, so forgive the Helpers and the Emigrants." They replied to him: "We are those who pledged to Muhammad to fight jihad as long as we live forever." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter: The Battle of the Trench: 7/392; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/4.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi also informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim informed us, Shu'ba informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: The Prophet ﷺ was carrying earth on the day of the Trench until it covered his belly, or dusted it, and he was saying:

By Allah, had it not been for Allah, we would not have been guided,
nor would we have given charity nor prayed.
So send down tranquility upon us,
and make our feet firm if we meet [the enemy].
Indeed, those who have transgressed against us,
whenever they desire strife, we refuse.

And he raised his voice with it: "We refuse, we refuse!" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter: The Battle of the Trench: 7/399; Muslim in al-Jihad wa al-Siyar, chapter: The Battle of the Confederates, no. (1803), 3/1430–1431; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/4–5.]]

We returned to the narration of Ibn Ishaq, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished with the trench, the Quraysh came and descended at Mujtama' al-Asyal, from Rumah, between al-Jurf and al-Ghaba [[In the Sirat Ibn Hisham: 3/220 it reads "Zughaba." Abu Dharr said: "Thus it occurs here with a fatha on the za', but "Raghaba" with a fatha on the ra' is the sound reading, and al-Waqshi also transmitted it that way."]] with ten thousand of their confederates (al-ahabish, allied tribes), and those who followed them from Banu Kinanah and the people of Tihamah. The Ghatafan and those who followed them from the people of Najd also came and descended at Dhanab Naqma, beside Uhud. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims went out until they placed their backs to Sal' with three thousand Muslims. There he pitched his camp, with the trench between him and the enemy. He ordered the women and children to be lifted up into the fortified towers (al-atam).

The enemy of Allah, Huyayy ibn Akhtab of Banu al-Nadir, went out until he came to Ka'b ibn Asad al-Qurazi, the holder of the pact and covenant of Banu Qurayzah. Ka'b had made a truce with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on behalf of his people and had made a covenant with him on this. When Ka'b heard of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, he closed his fortress against him. He asked permission to enter, but Ka'b refused to open to him. Huyayy called out: "O Ka'b, open for me!" Ka'b said: "Woe to you, O Huyayy, you are an ill-omened man, and I have made a covenant with Muhammad, so I will not break what is between me and him. I have seen from him nothing but fidelity and truthfulness." Huyayy said: "Woe to you, open for me, that I may speak with you." Ka'b said: "I will not do that." Huyayy said: "By Allah, if you close off to me, it is only out of concern that I might eat with you from your food." So the man was ashamed, and he opened to him. Huyayy said: "Woe to you, O Ka'b! I have brought you the might of the age and a surging sea. I have brought you Quraysh with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at Mujtama' al-Asyal from Rumah, and the Ghatafan with their leaders and chiefs, until I have settled them at Dhanab Naqma beside Uhud. They have pledged to me and bound themselves to me that they will not depart until they uproot Muhammad and those with him."

Ka'b ibn Asad said to him: "By Allah, you have brought me the humiliation of the age, and a rainless cloud whose water has been spilled with thunder and lightning, but there is nothing in it. So leave me with Muhammad and what I am upon, for I have seen from Muhammad nothing but truthfulness and fidelity." Huyayy ibn Akhtab kept at Ka'b, twisting him by the forelock and the back, until he consented, on condition that Huyayy gave him a pledge and covenant from Allah: "If Quraysh and Ghatafan return without having struck Muhammad, I will enter with you into your fortress, so that what befalls you will befall me." Ka'b ibn Asad then broke his covenant and disowned what was between him and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

When the news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, of Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, who was then the chief of the Aws, and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, of Banu Sa'idah, who was then the chief of the Khazraj, and with them 'Abd Allah ibn Rawahah, brother of Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, and Khawwat ibn Jubayr, brother of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf. He said: "Go and see whether what has reached us about these people is true or not. If it is true, then speak to me in a way I will understand, and do not weaken the resolve of the people. If they are upholding the fidelity between us and them, then declare it openly to the people." So they went out until they reached them, and found them at the worst of what had been reported of them. They slandered the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "There is no pact between us and Muhammad, nor any covenant." Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah exchanged insults with them, and they insulted him in return, for he was a man of hot temper. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to him: "Leave off insulting them, for what lies between us and them is worse than insults." Then Sa'd and Sa'd and those with them came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, greeted him, and said: "'Adal and al-Qarah!" meaning the treachery of 'Adal and al-Qarah against the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the companions of al-Raji': Khubayb ibn 'Adi and his companions." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allahu Akbar! Rejoice, O assembly of Muslims!"

At that point the affliction grew severe and the fear intensified. The enemy came at them from above them and from below them, until the believers thought every kind of thought. Hypocrisy stirred up among some of the hypocrites, until Mu'attib ibn Qushayr, brother of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, said: "Muhammad used to promise us that we would eat the treasures of Khosrow and Caesar, while not one of us can go out to relieve himself. Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion." And Aws ibn Qayzi, of Banu Harithah ibn Qayzi, said: "O Messenger of Allah, our houses are exposed to the enemy," and this was in the presence of a group of men from his people. "So give us permission, and we will return to our homes, for they lie outside Medina."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained, and the polytheists remained encamped against him for some twenty nights, close to a month. There was no fighting between the two sides except shooting with arrows and pebbles.

When the affliction grew severe upon the people, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent to 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn and al-Harith ibn 'Awf, who were the two leaders of the Ghatafan, and offered them a third of the produce of Medina, on condition that they would turn back with those who were with them from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his companions. A peace was agreed between him and them, until they wrote the document, but the witnessing had not yet taken place. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned this to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah and sought their counsel about it. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this something Allah has commanded you, which we must act upon? Or is it a matter you wish and so you do it? Or is it something you do for us?" He said: "No, rather it is something I do for you. By Allah, I do this only because I have seen the Arabs shoot at you from one bow and gang up on you from every side, so I wanted to break their strength away from you." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of Allah, we and these people were upon shirk with Allah and worship of idols, not worshipping Allah nor knowing Him, and they did not expect to eat a single date from Medina except as hospitality or by purchase. Now that Allah has honored us with Islam and strengthened us through you, shall we give them our wealth? We have no need of this. By Allah, we will give them nothing but the sword, until Allah judges between us and them." [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:] "Then the matter is yours." Sa'd took the document and erased what was written in it, then said: "Let them strive against us."

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the Muslims remained, while their enemy besieged them, and there was no fighting between them, except that some horsemen of Quraysh, among them 'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd of Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Hubayrah ibn Abi Wahb, both of Makhzum, and Nawfal ibn 'Abd Allah, and Dirar ibn al-Khattab, and Mirdas, brother of Banu Muharib ibn Fihr, had armed themselves for battle. They rode out on their horses and passed by Banu Kinanah and said: "Prepare for war, O Banu Kinanah! Today you will know who the true horsemen are." Then they advanced toward the trench until they stopped at the trench. When they saw it they said: "By Allah, this is a stratagem that the Arabs have never used."

Then they sought a narrow spot in the trench and urged their horses, and the horses leapt across it. They roamed with them in the salt flats between the trench and Sal'. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib went out with a group of Muslims until they seized the gap through which they had driven their horses across. The horsemen came charging toward them. 'Amr ibn 'Abd Wudd, who had fought at Badr, had been left lame by his wound, [so he did not attend Uhud]. On the day of the trench he came out marked with a distinguishing sign so that his position could be seen. When he and his horse stood still, 'Ali said to him: "O 'Amr, you used to pledge to Allah that whenever a man of Quraysh called you to one of two things, you would take one of them from him." He said: "Indeed." 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said to him: "I call you to Allah, to His Messenger, and to Islam." He said: "I have no need of that." He said: "Then I call you to single combat." He said: "Why, O nephew? By Allah, I do not wish to kill you." 'Ali said: "But by Allah, I wish to kill you." At that 'Amr grew furious, leapt down from his horse, hamstrung it, and struck its face. Then he turned upon 'Ali, and they grappled and fought, and 'Ali killed him. His horsemen then fled in defeat until they plunged into the trench in flight.

With 'Amr were killed two men: Munabbih ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Ubayd ibn al-Sabbaq ibn 'Abd al-Dar, who was struck by an arrow and died from it in Mecca; and Nawfal ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, who had plunged into the trench, became stuck in it, and they pelted him with stones. He said: "O assembly of Arabs, his killing is better than this!" 'Ali descended to him and killed him. The Muslims then gained possession of his body, and they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to sell them his body. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We have no need of his body or its price; do with it as you wish." So he left them free to deal with it.

'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, said: On the day of the trench we were in the fortress of Banu Harithah, which was among the most secure fortresses of Medina. The mother of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was with us in the fortress, and that was before the veil was prescribed for us. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh passed by wearing a short coat of mail, from which his entire forearm had come out, and in his hand was a spear, and he was saying:

"Wait a little, you will reach the battle that rages;
There is no harm in death when its term has come."

His mother said to him: "Hurry, my son, for by Allah you have fallen behind!" 'A'ishah said: I said to her: "O Umm Sa'd, by Allah, I wished that Sa'd's coat of mail were more complete than it is." She said: "And I feared for him where the arrow would strike him." She said: On that day Sa'd was struck by an arrow, and his main vein (al-akhal) was cut. It was shot by Khabbab ibn Qays ibn al-'Araqah, of Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy. When it struck him he said: "Take it, and I am the son of al-'Araqah!" Sa'd said: "May Allah make your face black in the Fire!" Then Sa'd said: "O Allah, if You have left any part of the war with Quraysh, then preserve me for it, for there is no people more beloved to me to fight than a people who harmed Your Messenger, denied him, and expelled him. And if You have ended the war between us and them, then make this a martyrdom for me, and do not let me die until my eyes are refreshed concerning Banu Qurayzah, who were his allies and clients in the pre-Islamic era." [See the full narration in the Sirat Ibn Hisham: 3/219–227.]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father Abbad, who said: Safiyyah bint Abd al-Muttalib was in Fari', the fort of Hassan ibn Thabit. She said: Hassan was with us in it, along with the women and children. Safiyyah said: A Jewish man passed by us and began circling the fort, while Banu Qurayzah had gone to war. They had cut off what lay between us and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and there was no one between us and them to repel them for us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims were engaged in the throats of their enemy, unable to turn away from them toward us if someone came to us. She said: I said, "O Hassan, this Jew, as you see, is circling the fort. By Allah, I do not feel safe that he will point out our weak points to the Jews behind us, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions are preoccupied with us. So go down to him and kill him." He said, "May Allah forgive you, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib! By Allah, you know that I am not the one to do this." She said: When he said that to me and I saw nothing with him, I tightened my waist-wrap, then took a pole and went down from the fort to him, and I struck him with the pole until I killed him. When I had finished with him, I returned to the fort and said, "O Hassan, go down to him and strip him of his armor, for nothing prevented me from stripping him except that he was a man." He said, "I have no need of his spoils, daughter of Abd al-Muttalib."[[انظر: سيرة ابن هشام: ٣ / ٢٢٨-٢٣٠.]] (See: Sirat Ibn Hisham: 3/228–230.)

They said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions remained in the state that Allah Most High described: fear and hardship, because of the massing of their enemy and their coming at them from above them and from below them.

Then Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud ibn Amir of Ghatafan came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have embraced Islam, and my people do not know of my Islam, so command me with whatever you wish." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "You are just one man among us, so sow discord against them if you are able, for war is deception." Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud went out until he came to Banu Qurayzah, and he had been their boon companion in the pre-Islamic period. He said to them: "O Banu Qurayzah, you know my affection for you and the special bond between me and you." They said: "You have spoken truly; you are not suspected by us." He said to them: "Quraysh and Ghatafan have come to fight Muhammad, and you have backed them against him. Quraysh and Ghatafan are not in the same situation as you. This land is your land; your wealth, your children and your women are in it, and you cannot move away from it to another place. Quraysh and Ghatafan, however, their wealth, their children and their women are far away. If they see a raid and booty they can take, they will take it; if it is otherwise, they will return to their lands and leave you alone with the man, and the man is in your land, and you have no power against him if he is alone with you. So do not fight alongside these people until you take from them hostages from their nobles, who will remain in your hands as a guarantee for you that they will fight alongside you against Muhammad, until you engage him." They said: "You have given sound and sincere counsel."

Then he went out until he came to Quraysh, and he said to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those of the men of Quraysh with him: "O assembly of Quraysh, you know my affection for you and my estrangement from Muhammad. A matter has reached me, and I saw it as a duty upon me to convey it to you as sincere advice, so keep it secret from me." They said, "We will." He said: "You know that the Jews have regretted what they did between them and Muhammad, and they have sent to him: 'We have regretted what we did.' Would it please you that we take from the two tribes, Quraysh and Ghatafan, men of their nobles, and give them to you, so that you may strike their necks, and then we will be with you against those who remain of them?" He sent back to them: "Yes." So if the Jews send to you seeking hostages from your men, do not give them a single man from you."

Then he went out until he came to Ghatafan and said: "O assembly of Ghatafan, you are my origin, my clan, and the people dearest to me, and I do not think you suspect me." They said, "You have spoken truly." He said, "Then keep it secret from me." They said, "We will." Then he said to them the same as he had said to Quraysh, and warned them as he had warned them.

When it was the night of Saturday in Shawwal in the fifth year, and among what [Nu'aym] had done for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Sufyan and the chiefs of Ghatafan sent to Banu Qurayzah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl with a group of Quraysh and Ghatafan, and they said to them: "We are not a people who remain in one place; the hoof and the hoofed beast have perished. So go out to fight, so that we may engage Muhammad and finish with what is between us and him." Banu Qurayzah said to them: "Today is Saturday, a day on which we do no work at all, and some of us previously committed an offense on it, and what befell them is not hidden from you.
