And we are not, in addition to that, going to fight alongside you until you give us hostages from your men, who will remain in our hands as a guarantee for us until we engage Muhammad, for we fear that if the war overwhelms you and the fighting becomes severe for you, you will set out for your lands and leave us, with the man in our land, and we have no power against Muhammad." When the messengers returned to them with what Banu Qurayzah had said, Quraysh and Ghatafan said: "By Allah, you know that what Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud told you is true." So they sent to Banu Qurayzah: "By Allah, we will not give you a single man from our men. If you want to fight, then come out and fight." Banu Qurayzah said, when the messengers reached them with this: "What Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud mentioned to you is true. These people only want to fight. If they find an opportunity they will seize it, and if it is otherwise they will flee to their lands and leave you alone with the man in your land." So they sent to Quraysh and Ghatafan: "By Allah, we will not fight alongside you until you give us hostages." They refused them, and Allah caused discord between them. And Allah sent upon them a wind during cold, bitter winter nights, which overturned their cooking pots and cast down their vessels.

When the news of what had divided them reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he called Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and sent him to them to see what the people were doing at night.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and others related from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, both of them saying: A young man from the people of Kufa said to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman: "O Abu Abd Allah, did you see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and keep his company?" He said, "Yes, nephew." He said: "How did you use to act?" He said: "By Allah, we used to strive hard." The young man said: "By Allah, if we had reached him we would not have let him walk on the earth; we would have carried him on our necks and served him, and we would have done this and that." Hudhayfah said: "Nephew, by Allah, I saw myself on the night of the Confederates with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'Who will stand up and go to these people and bring us news of them? Allah will admit him to Paradise.' None of us stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed during a part of the night, then turned to us and said the same. The people were silent, and none of us stood up. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed during a part of the night, then turned to us and said: 'Who is the man who will stand up and look at what the people are doing, on condition that he will be my companion in Paradise?' None of the men stood up, from the intensity of fear, the intensity of hunger and the intensity of cold. When no one stood up, he called me, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and said, 'O Hudhayfah!' I had no choice but to rise to him when he called me, so I said, 'At your service, O Messenger of Allah,' and I stood up until I came to him, and my sides were trembling. He wiped my head and face, then said: 'Go to these people until you bring me news of them, and do not do anything until you return to me.' Then he said, 'O Allah, protect him from before him, behind him, from his right, from his left, from above him and from below him.' So I took my arrow, and I girded my weapons, then set off walking toward them as if I were walking in a bathhouse. I went and entered among the people, and Allah had sent upon them a wind and hosts of Allah, doing to them what it did. It left them no cooking pot, no fire and no structure. Abu Sufyan was sitting warming himself by the fire. I took an arrow and placed it on the belly of my bow, and I intended to shoot him, and had I shot him I would have hit him. But I remembered the Prophet's (ﷺ) words: 'Do not do anything until you return to me,' so I returned the arrow to my quiver." When Abu Sufyan saw what the wind and the hosts of Allah were doing to them, leaving them no cooking pot, no fire and no structure, he stood up and said: "O assembly of Quraysh, let each one of you take the hand of the man beside him and see who he is." I took the hand of the man beside me and said, "Who are you?" He said, "Subhan Allah! Do you not know me? I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so." He was a man from Hawazin.

Then Abu Sufyan said: "O assembly of Quraysh, by Allah, you have not reached a place to remain. The horses and the camels have perished, Banu Qurayzah have broken their word to us, and we have received from them what we dislike, and we have encountered this wind, as you see. So depart, for I am departing." Then he went to his camel, which was tethered, and sat upon it, then struck it, and it leaped with him on three legs. He did not release its tether until it was standing. Ghatafan heard what Quraysh had done, so they turned back to their lands.

He said: I returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as if I were walking in a bathhouse, and I came to him while he was standing and praying. When he finished the prayer of salutation, I informed him of the news, and he laughed until his canine teeth showed in the darkness of the night. He said: When I had informed him and finished, I felt a chill, and the warmth left me.

The Prophet (ﷺ) drew me close to him, made me sleep at his feet, cast the edge of his garment over me, and pressed my chest against the soles of his feet. I did not cease sleeping until morning. When I woke up, he said: "Get up, O sleeper!"[[أخرجه مسلم في الجهاد باب: غزو الأحزاب برقم (١٧٨٨) : ٣ / ١٤١٤-١٤١٥.]] (Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Jihad, chapter: The Battle of the Confederates, no. 1788: 3/1414–1415.)

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 10–11:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾, i.e., from above the valley, from the direction of the east, and they were Asad and Ghatafan, led by Malik ibn ʿAwf al-Nasri and ʿUyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari with a thousand from Ghatafan, and with them Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid al-Asadi among Banu Asad, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab among the Jews of Banu Qurayza. ﴿And from below you﴾ means from the bottom of the valley, from the direction of the west, and they were Quraysh and Kinana, led by Abu Sufyan ibn Harb among Quraysh and those who followed him, and Abu al-Aʿwar ʿAmr ibn Sufyan al-Sulami from the direction of the trench (al-Khandaq).

What set off the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Khandaq), it is said, was the expulsion by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of Banu al-Nadir from their homes.

﴿And when the eyes shifted﴾ meaning they inclined and stared fixedly from terror. It is also said: they turned away from everything, so they did not look at their enemy. ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾, meaning they moved from their places until they reached the windpipes from fright. Al-Hanjara is the hollow of the trachea (al-hulqum). This is a figurative expression, used to describe the intensity of fear. Al-Farra' said: its meaning is that they became cowardly, and the way of a coward when his fear intensifies is that his lungs swell; when the lungs swell they lift the heart up to the throat, and for this reason it is said of a coward: "his lung has swelled."

﴿And you thought about Allah with various thoughts﴾, i.e., the thoughts differed: the hypocrites thought that Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, would be annihilated, while the believers thought that victory and triumph would be theirs.

The people of Medina, the people of Syria and Abu Bakr read "al-Zununa", "al-Rasula" and "al-Sabila" with the alif affirmed both in connected and pause recitation, because it is written thus in the codices (al-masahif). The people of Basra and Hamza read without the alif in both states, according to the original form. The others read with the alif in pause but not in connection, to match the verse-endings (ru'us al-ayy).

﴿There the believers were tested﴾, i.e., at that time the believers were tried by the siege and the fighting, so that the sincere could be distinguished from the hypocrite. ﴿And they were shaken with a severe shaking﴾, meaning they were moved with a violent movement.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 12–14:

﴿And when the hypocrites say﴾ — Mu'attib ibn Qushayr; and it is said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions — ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ — doubt and weakness of belief — ﴿"Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."﴾ This is the saying of the people of hypocrisy: "Muhammad promises us the conquest of the palaces of Syria and Persia, while one of us cannot even venture beyond his saddle-bag. By Allah, this is nothing but delusion!"

﴿And when a faction of them said﴾ — that is, of the hypocrites, and they were Aws ibn Qayzi and his companions — ﴿"O people of Yathrib"﴾ — meaning Madinah. Abu Ubaydah said: "Yathrib" is the name of a land, and the city of the Messenger (ﷺ) is in one part of it.

It is related in some reports that the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade that Madinah be called Yathrib, and said: "It is Taba (good)," as if he disliked this term. [[Muslim related in al-Jihad (2/1007) from the hadith of Jabir ibn Samurah, raised to the Prophet: "Indeed Allah named it Taba." Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi related it in his Musnad, p. 104, from Shu'bah from Simak with the wording: "They used to call Madinah Yathrib, so the Prophet (ﷺ) named it Taybah." It was also recorded by Abu Awanah. See: Fath al-Bari: 4/88-89.]]

﴿"There is no staying place for you"﴾ — the majority read it with a fatha on the mim, meaning: there is no place for you to alight and remain in. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and Hafs read it with a damma on the mim, meaning: there is no staying (iqamah) for you. ﴿"So return"﴾ — to your dwellings, away from following Muhammad (ﷺ); it is also said: away from fighting, to your homes.

﴿And a party of them seek permission from the Prophet﴾ — and they are Banu Harithah and Banu Salamah — ﴿saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed (awrah)"﴾ — that is, empty and vulnerable, and they are on the side facing the enemy, and we fear thieves for them. Abu Raja al-Utaridi read "awirah" with a kasra on the waw, meaning: their walls are low, so it is easy for thieves to enter them. Allah refuted them, saying: ﴿"And they were not exposed; they only intended to flee."﴾ — that is, they did not intend anything but fleeing.

﴿And if they had been entered from its surroundings﴾ — that is, if the city had been entered upon them from its sides and quarters, meaning these armies that intended to fight them, who are the confederates — ﴿from its sides﴾ — the plural of qutr (region) — ﴿then they were asked for sedition﴾ — that is, shirk.

﴿They would have given it﴾ — they would have granted it. The people of the Hijaz read "la-atawha" with a short alif, meaning: they would have come to it, done it, and turned back from Islam. ﴿And they would not have delayed in it﴾ — that is, they would not have held back from the sedition ﴿except briefly﴾ — and they would have hastened to answer the call to shirk, giving themselves willingly to it. This is the saying of most of the exegetes.

Al-Hasan and al-Farra said: they would not have remained in Madinah after granting disbelief except briefly, until they perished. [[Mentioned by al-Farra in Ma'ani al-Qur'an: 2/337.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 12–14:

﴿And when the hypocrites say﴾ — Mu'attib ibn Qushayr; and it is said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions — ﴿and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ — doubt and weakness of belief — ﴿"Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion."﴾ This is the saying of the people of hypocrisy: "Muhammad promises us the conquest of the palaces of Syria and Persia, while one of us cannot even venture beyond his saddle-bag. By Allah, this is nothing but delusion!"

﴿And when a faction of them said﴾ — that is, of the hypocrites, and they were Aws ibn Qayzi and his companions — ﴿"O people of Yathrib"﴾ — meaning Madinah. Abu Ubaydah said: "Yathrib" is the name of a land, and the city of the Messenger (ﷺ) is in one part of it.

It is related in some reports that the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade that Madinah be called Yathrib, and said: "It is Taba (good)," as if he disliked this term. [[Muslim related in al-Jihad (2/1007) from the hadith of Jabir ibn Samurah, raised to the Prophet: "Indeed Allah named it Taba." Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi related it in his Musnad, p. 104, from Shu'bah from Simak with the wording: "They used to call Madinah Yathrib, so the Prophet (ﷺ) named it Taybah." It was also recorded by Abu Awanah. See: Fath al-Bari: 4/88-89.]]

﴿"There is no staying place for you"﴾ — the majority read it with a fatha on the mim, meaning: there is no place for you to alight and remain in. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and Hafs read it with a damma on the mim, meaning: there is no staying (iqamah) for you. ﴿"So return"﴾ — to your dwellings, away from following Muhammad (ﷺ); it is also said: away from fighting, to your homes.

﴿And a party of them seek permission from the Prophet﴾ — and they are Banu Harithah and Banu Salamah — ﴿saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed (awrah)"﴾ — that is, empty and vulnerable, and they are on the side facing the enemy, and we fear thieves for them. Abu Raja al-Utaridi read "awirah" with a kasra on the waw, meaning: their walls are low, so it is easy for thieves to enter them. Allah refuted them, saying: ﴿"And they were not exposed; they only intended to flee."﴾ — that is, they did not intend anything but fleeing.

﴿And if they had been entered from its surroundings﴾ — that is, if the city had been entered upon them from its sides and quarters, meaning these armies that intended to fight them, who are the confederates — ﴿from its sides﴾ — the plural of qutr (region) — ﴿then they were asked for sedition﴾ — that is, shirk.

﴿They would have given it﴾ — they would have granted it. The people of the Hijaz read "la-atawha" with a short alif, meaning: they would have come to it, done it, and turned back from Islam. ﴿And they would not have delayed in it﴾ — that is, they would not have held back from the sedition ﴿except briefly﴾ — and they would have hastened to answer the call to shirk, giving themselves willingly to it. This is the saying of most of the exegetes.

Al-Hasan and al-Farra said: they would not have remained in Madinah after granting disbelief except briefly, until they perished. [[Mentioned by al-Farra in Ma'ani al-Qur'an: 2/337.]]

﴿And they had already made a covenant with Allah before, that they would not turn their backs﴾ — that is, before the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Khandaq). ﴿They would not turn their backs﴾ — from their enemy, meaning they would not flee.

Yazid ibn Ruman said: They were the Banu Harithah. On the day of Uhud they intended to lose heart along with the Banu Salamah, but when what was revealed about them was revealed, they made a covenant with Allah that they would not return to such a thing.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 21/137.]]

Qatadah said: They were people who had been absent from the Battle of Badr [and had seen what Allah gave the people of Badr of honour and virtue]. [What is between the brackets is missing from manuscript "A".] They said: "If Allah makes us witness a battle, we will certainly fight." Then Allah brought them that situation.[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 21/137. See also Zad al-Masir: 6/363; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/219.]]

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: They were seventy men who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the night of al-'Aqabah. They said: "Stipulate for your Lord and for yourself whatever you wish." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves, your wives and your children from." They said: "If we do that, what will we have, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "For you is victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter." They said: "We have done that." That is their covenant.[[Mentioned by al-Qurtubi: 14/150. See also Zad al-Masir: 6/363; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/219.]]

This view is not acceptable, because those who pledged allegiance on the night of al-'Aqabah were seventy men, among whom there was no doubter and no one who would say such a thing. Rather, the verse concerns a people who made a covenant with Allah that they would fight and not flee, but they broke the covenant.

﴿And the covenant of Allah will be questioned﴾ — about it.

﴿Say﴾ to them, ﴿Flight will never benefit you if you flee from death or killing﴾ which has been prescribed for you, because whoever's term has come dies or is killed. ﴿And then you will not be given enjoyment except for a little﴾ — that is, after fleeing you will not be given enjoyment except for the duration of your appointed terms, and that is brief.

﴿Say: "Who is it that can protect you from God if He intends harm for you," meaning: who can prevent you from His punishment; "or intends mercy for you," meaning victory? ﴾ "And they will not find for themselves, besides God, any ally," meaning: any close friend who can benefit them, "nor any helper," meaning: any supporter who can defend them.

﴿God certainly knows those among you who hinder others﴾, meaning: those who discourage people from following the Messenger of God (ﷺ), ﴿and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us,"﴾ meaning: return to us and leave Muhammad, do not fight alongside him, for we fear destruction for you.

Qatada said: These were some of the hypocrites who used to discourage the Helpers of the Prophet (ﷺ) and say to their brothers: "Muhammad and his companions are merely a mouthful of food. If they were meat, Abu Sufyan and his companions would devour them. Leave the man, for he is doomed." [Reported by al-Tabari: 21/139.]

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning the hypocrites, because the Jews sent to the hypocrites and said: "What drives you to kill yourselves at the hands of Abu Sufyan and those with him? If they gain power over you this time, they will spare none of you. We pity you. You are our brothers and neighbours, so come to us." Then Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions turned to the believers, obstructing them and frightening them with Abu Sufyan and those with him, saying: "If they gain power over you, they will spare none of you. What do you hope for from Muhammad? There is no good in him. He will only kill us here. Let us go to our brothers," meaning the Jews. But the believers' words in response to the hypocrites only increased their faith and their seeking of reward. [See: Zad al-Masir: 6/365.]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And they do not come to the battle﴾ [79a] ﴿except a little,﴾ meaning: out of show and reputation (riya' wa sum'ah), without seeking reward. Had that little been for God's sake, it would have been much.

﴿Stingy towards you,﴾ meaning: withholding from spending in the way of God and from giving help. Qatada said: stingy at the time of the spoils of war (ghanimah). God described them with stinginess and cowardice, saying: ﴿So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling﴾ in their heads out of fear and cowardice, ﴿like one who faints from the approach of death,﴾ meaning: like the rolling of one overcome by death, because whoever is near death, when its signs overwhelm him, loses his reason and his gaze becomes fixed so that he does not blink. ﴿But when fear departs, they lash you﴾ with words, meaning: they harm you and assail you in a time of safety, ﴿with sharp tongues,﴾ meaning: piercing ones. It is the plural of "hadid." It is said of an eloquent orator of sharp tongue: "mislaq," "misla'," "sallaq," and "salla'." Ibn Abbas said: "Salaqukum" means: they attacked you and took you to task with blame and backbiting. Qatada said: They stretched out their tongues against you at the time of dividing the spoils of war, saying: "Give us, for we fought alongside you, so you have no more right to the spoils than we do." [See: Zad al-Masir: 6/366.] So at the time of the spoils they are the most grasping of people, and at the time of battle they are the most cowardly of people. ﴿Stingy over the good,﴾ meaning: at the time of the spoils they are miserly toward the believers. ﴿Those have not believed, so God has nullified their deeds.﴾ Muqatil said: God nullified their jihad. ﴿And that is ever easy for God.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verses 22–23:

Then He described the state of the believers when they met the confederates, saying: ﴿When the believers saw the confederates, they said﴾, submitting to the command of God and affirming His promise: ﴿This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger have spoken truly﴾. God's promise to them is what is mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah: "Did you think that you would enter Paradise without there having come to you the like of those who passed away before you?" up to His words: "Surely the help of God is near" [al-Baqarah 2:214]. So the verse implies that the believers would face the same kind of trial. When they saw the confederates and the hardship that befell them, they said: "This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger have spoken truly." ﴿And it only increased them in faith and submission﴾ [i.e., affirmation of God and submission to the command of God].

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God﴾, meaning: they fulfilled what they pledged to God and kept it. ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾, meaning: he finished his nadhr (vow) and fulfilled his pledge, so he remained steadfast in jihad until he was martyred. The word nahb means "vow," and it also means "death." Muqatil said: "fulfilled his nahb" means his term (ajal), so he was killed while being faithful to the pledge [meaning Hamzah and his companions]. It was also said: "fulfilled his nahb" means he exerted his utmost effort in fulfilling the pledge, from the Arabs' saying: "So-and-so covered the journey (nahaba) in his travel for a whole day and night," when he pressed on without stopping. ﴿And among them is he who waits﴾ for martyrdom.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow" refers to those who were martyred at the Battle of Badr and Uhud [in Ibn Hisham: "fulfilled his nahb" means he finished his work and returned to his Lord, like those who were martyred at Badr and Uhud]. "And among them is he who waits" means: those among the believers who remained after these, waiting for one of two outcomes: either martyrdom or victory [see Sirat Ibn Hisham: 3/248–249]. ﴿And they did not change [their covenant] in the least﴾.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliһi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Khuza'i informed us: Abd al-A'la informed us, from Humayd, who said: I asked Anas. [And] Amr ibn Zurarah narrated to me: Ziyad informed us: Humayd al-Tawil narrated to me, from Anas, who said: My paternal uncle Anas ibn al-Nadr was absent from the battle of Badr, and he said: "O Messenger of God, I was absent from the first battle in which you fought the polytheists. If God lets me witness a battle against the polytheists, God will surely see what I do." When the day of Uhud came and the Muslims were routed, he said: "O God, I apologize to You for what these people have done"—meaning his companions—"and I disavow to You what these people have done"—meaning the polytheists. Then he advanced and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh met him. He said: "O Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, by the Lord of al-Nadr, I smell the fragrance of Paradise from beyond Uhud." Sa'd said: "I was not able, O Messenger of God, to do what he did." Anas said: "We found on him more than eighty wounds from sword strikes, spear thrusts, or arrow shots. We found him killed, and the polytheists had mutilated him, so no one recognized him except his sister by his fingertips." Anas said: "We used to think, or we used to see, that this verse was revealed concerning him and those like him: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God﴾ to the end of the verse [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Jihad, chapter on God's saying, Mighty and Majestic: "Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is he who waits, and they did not change in the least": 6/21; and Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter: The Assurance of Paradise for the Martyr, no. (1903): 3/1512.]].

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: Muhammad ibn Hammad informed us: Mu'awiyah informed us, from al-A'mash, from Sufyan, from Shaqiq, from Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, who said: We emigrated with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in the way of God, seeking the face of God, so our reward became due from God. Some of us passed away without having consumed any of their reward. Among them was Mus'ab ibn Umayr, who was killed on the day of Uhud, and nothing was found to shroud him in except a striped cloak (namirah). When we placed it over his head, his feet would show, and when we placed it over his feet, his head would show. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Place it over his head, and put idhkhir grass over his feet." He also said: "And whoever has his fruit ripened for him, he is gathering it." Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verses 22–23:

Then He described the state of the believers when they met the confederates, saying: ﴿When the believers saw the confederates, they said﴾, submitting to the command of God and affirming His promise: ﴿This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger have spoken truly﴾. God's promise to them is what is mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah: "Did you think that you would enter Paradise without there having come to you the like of those who passed away before you?" up to His words: "Surely the help of God is near" [al-Baqarah 2:214]. So the verse implies that the believers would face the same kind of trial. When they saw the confederates and the hardship that befell them, they said: "This is what God and His Messenger promised us, and God and His Messenger have spoken truly." ﴿And it only increased them in faith and submission﴾ [i.e., affirmation of God and submission to the command of God].

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God﴾, meaning: they fulfilled what they pledged to God and kept it. ﴿Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow﴾, meaning: he finished his nadhr (vow) and fulfilled his pledge, so he remained steadfast in jihad until he was martyred. The word nahb means "vow," and it also means "death." Muqatil said: "fulfilled his nahb" means his term (ajal), so he was killed while being faithful to the pledge [meaning Hamzah and his companions]. It was also said: "fulfilled his nahb" means he exerted his utmost effort in fulfilling the pledge, from the Arabs' saying: "So-and-so covered the journey (nahaba) in his travel for a whole day and night," when he pressed on without stopping. ﴿And among them is he who waits﴾ for martyrdom.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow" refers to those who were martyred at the Battle of Badr and Uhud [in Ibn Hisham: "fulfilled his nahb" means he finished his work and returned to his Lord, like those who were martyred at Badr and Uhud]. "And among them is he who waits" means: those among the believers who remained after these, waiting for one of two outcomes: either martyrdom or victory [see Sirat Ibn Hisham: 3/248–249]. ﴿And they did not change [their covenant] in the least﴾.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliһi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Khuza'i informed us: Abd al-A'la informed us, from Humayd, who said: I asked Anas. [And] Amr ibn Zurarah narrated to me: Ziyad informed us: Humayd al-Tawil narrated to me, from Anas, who said: My paternal uncle Anas ibn al-Nadr was absent from the battle of Badr, and he said: "O Messenger of God, I was absent from the first battle in which you fought the polytheists. If God lets me witness a battle against the polytheists, God will surely see what I do." When the day of Uhud came and the Muslims were routed, he said: "O God, I apologize to You for what these people have done"—meaning his companions—"and I disavow to You what these people have done"—meaning the polytheists. Then he advanced and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh met him. He said: "O Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, by the Lord of al-Nadr, I smell the fragrance of Paradise from beyond Uhud." Sa'd said: "I was not able, O Messenger of God, to do what he did." Anas said: "We found on him more than eighty wounds from sword strikes, spear thrusts, or arrow shots. We found him killed, and the polytheists had mutilated him, so no one recognized him except his sister by his fingertips."
