**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verses 24–26 (part 1 of 3):**

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So that Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness﴾, meaning the reward of their truthfulness. Their truthfulness is their fulfilment of the covenant. ﴿And punish the hypocrites if He wills, or turn to them in forgiveness﴾, so that He guides them to faith. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved﴾, from Quraysh and Ghatafan, ﴿in their rage﴾, not healing their hearts by attaining what they wanted. ﴿They gained no good﴾, meaning no victory. ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting﴾, by means of the angels and the wind. ﴿And Allah is ever Strong and Mighty﴾ [strong in His dominion, mighty] [[What is between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]] in His retribution.

﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them﴾, meaning those who aided the confederates of Quraysh and Ghatafan against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, and they were the Banu Qurayzah. ﴿From their fortresses﴾, meaning their strongholds and refuges. Its singular is ṣayṣiyah, and from it is said of the horn [of an animal] and of the spur of a cock and of the weaver's comb that it is a ṣayṣiyah. [From this root comes the term for the horn, the spur of the rooster, and the weaver's comb, ṣayṣiyah.] [[What is between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]]

The reason for this is that when morning came on the night in which the confederates withdrew, returning to their lands, and the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers departed from the Trench to Medina and laid down their weapons, at noon Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), wrapped in a turban of brocade, riding a mule with a saddle [[al-rihalah: the saddle.]] and a silk covering, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was washing his head, having washed one side of it. [Jibril] said: "Have you laid down the weapons, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." Jibril said: "May Allah pardon you. The angels have not laid down their weapons for forty nights, and I have only just now returned from pursuing the people."

It is also narrated that dust was on the face of Jibril, peace be upon him, and on his horse, so the Prophet (ﷺ) began wiping the dust from his face and from his horse. [Jibril] said: "Allah commands you to march against Banu Qurayzah, so advance [[Go forth against them. To nahd (rise up) against an enemy means to stand firm before them and begin fighting them.]] against them. Indeed, I have cut their bowstrings, opened their gates, and left them in turmoil and confusion." [[See al-Bukhari: 7/407; Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/10–11.]] So the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered a caller, who proclaimed: "Whoever is listening and obedient, let him not pray the afternoon prayer except at Banu Qurayzah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, ahead with his banner, and the people hastened toward it. ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, advanced until he drew near the fortresses, and he heard from them a vile remark about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He turned back and met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the road and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you should not approach these vile people." [The Prophet] said: "Why? Do you think you heard harm from them toward me?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "If they had seen me, they would not have said anything of that sort."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drew near their fortresses, he said: "O brothers of the apes and the swine! Has Allah disgraced you and brought down His vengeance upon you?" They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, you were never ignorant."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by his companions at al-Sawrayn [[A place near Medina.]] before he reached Banu Qurayzah, and said: "Has anyone passed by you?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah. Dihyah ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi passed by us on a white mule with a saddle and a silk brocade covering." He, peace be upon him, said: "That was Jibril. He was sent to Banu Qurayzah to shake their fortresses and to cast terror into their hearts."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Banu Qurayzah, he stopped at one of their wells, in an area of their property. People caught up with him, and men came to him after the late night prayer [[Al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah: the night prayer, meaning the final evening prayer.]] and they had not yet prayed the afternoon prayer, because of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "None of you should pray the afternoon prayer except at Banu Qurayzah." So they prayed the afternoon prayer there after the late night prayer. Allah did not reproach them for that, nor did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rebuke them for it. [The narrator] said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them for twenty-five nights, until the siege exhausted them, and Allah cast terror into their hearts.

Huyayy ibn Akhtab had entered upon Banu Qurayzah in their fortress when Quraysh and Ghatafan withdrew from them, in fulfilment of his pledge to Kaʿb ibn Asad, which he had made to him.

When they were certain that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not leave them until he fought them, Ka'b ibn Asad said: "O assembly of Jews, you can see the situation that has come upon you. I am offering you three options, so take whichever of them you wish." They said, "And what are they?" He said: "We follow this man and believe him. By Allah, it has become clear to you that he is a prophet sent by God, and that he is the one you find described in your Book. Then you will be secure for your homes, your property, your sons and your women." They said: "We will never abandon the judgment of the Torah (al-Tawrat) or exchange it for anything else." He said: "If you refuse this, then come, let us kill our sons and our women, then go out to Muhammad as men with drawn swords, leaving behind us no burden that concerns us, until Allah judges between us and Muhammad. If we perish, we will perish and leave behind nothing we fear for. And if we prevail, then by my life, we will take women and sons (again)." They said: "We would kill these poor people? What good is life after them?" He said: "If you refuse this, then tonight is the night of Saturday (al-Sabt), and it may be that Muhammad and his companions feel secure on it, so go down (to attack them), perhaps we may strike Muhammad and his companions by surprise." They said: "Shall we desecrate our Sabbath and innovate in it what those before us did not innovate? Do you not know what befell those who did so, of transformation (into apes and swine)?" He said: "No man among you has spent a single night since his mother bore him in the age being resolute?" Then they sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "Send to us Abu Lubaba ibn Abd al-Mundhir, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, who were allies of the Aws, so that we may consult him about our affair." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to them. When they saw him, the men stood up to him, the women and children greeted him weeping before his face, and he was moved with pity for them. They said: "O Abu Lubaba, do you think we should submit to the judgment of Muhammad?" He said: "Yes." [They said: "What will he do to us if we submit?"] (The words in brackets are omitted in manuscript "A".) He pointed with his hand to his throat, meaning slaughter. Abu Lubaba said: "By Allah, my feet had not moved from their place before I knew that I had betrayed Allah and His Messenger." Then Abu Lubaba set off on his way and did not go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he tied himself to one of the pillars of the mosque, and said: "I will not move from my place until Allah accepts my repentance for what I have done." He pledged to Allah that he would never set foot on the land of Bani Qurayza again, and that Allah would never see him in a land where he had betrayed Allah and His Messenger. When news of him reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he was late (in returning), he said: "If he had come to me, I would have asked forgiveness for him. But since he has done what he has done, I will not release him from his place until Allah accepts his repentance." Then Allah the Exalted sent down the repentance of Abu Lubaba upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in the house of Umm Salama. Umm Salama said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughing, so I said: 'What makes you laugh, O Messenger of Allah? May Allah make your teeth laugh?' He said: 'Repentance has been accepted for Abu Lubaba.' I said: 'Shall I not give him the good news of that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, if you wish.' So she stood at the door of her chamber, and that was before the veil was imposed upon them, and she said: 'O Abu Lubaba, rejoice, for Allah has accepted your repentance.'" He said: "The people rushed to him to release him, but he said: 'No, by Allah, not until the Messenger of Allah himself releases me with his hand.' When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by him going out to the dawn prayer, he released him." Then he said: "Tha'laba ibn Sha'ba, Usayd ibn Sha'ba, and Usayd ibn Ubayd, and they are a group from the Banu Hudhayl, who are neither of Qurayza nor of al-Nadir, their lineage being above that, they are cousins of the people (of Qurayza), embraced Islam on that night in which Bani Qurayza descended upon the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." On that night Amr ibn Sa'da al-Qurazi went out and passed by the guard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who that night was Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansari. When he saw him, he said: "Who is this?" He said: "Amr ibn Sa'da." Amr had refused to join Bani Qurayza in their treachery against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he had said: "I will never betray Muhammad." When Muhammad ibn Maslama recognized him, he said: "O Allah, do not deprive me of the slips of the noble," and then he let him go. So he went out on his way and spent that night in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Medina, then departed, and no one knows where he went in the land of Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was told of his situation, and he said: "That is a man whom Allah has saved by his fidelity." [(Narrated by al-Tabari, 21/152; see also Ibn Hisham, 3/238-239.)] Some people claim that he had been bound with a rope among those of Bani Qurayza who were bound when they descended upon the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in the morning his rope was found lying loose, and no one knew where he had gone, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that statement about him. And Allah knows best. When morning came, they descended upon the judgment of the Messenger of Allah. Then the Aws rose up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are our clients (mawali) rather than of the Khazraj, and you did with the clients of the Khazraj yesterday what you know." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had earlier besieged Bani Qaynuqa', who were allies of the Khazraj, and they descended upon his judgment, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul asked him to spare them, and he granted them to him. When the Aws spoke to him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Are you not content, O assembly of the Aws, that a man from among you should judge among you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then the matter is left to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh had been placed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the tent of a Muslim woman called Rufayda, in his mosque, and she used to treat the wounded and would devote herself to serving whoever among the Muslims was in need. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to his people when the arrow struck him at the Trench: "Place him in the tent of Rufayda until I visit him soon." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him as judge over Bani Qurayza, his people came to him and carried him on a donkey over which they had spread a leather cushion, and he was a large man. Then they came with him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "O Abu Amr, be good to your clients, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only appointed you so that you would be good to them." When they pressed him much, he said: "The time has come for Sa'd that in the cause of Allah he should not fear the blame of any blamer." Some of those from his people who had been with him returned to the house of Bani al-Ashhal and lamented for them the men of Bani Qurayza, before Sa'd ibn Mu'adh reached them, because of his word that he had heard from him. When Sa'd reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "Rise up to your chief and bring him down." They rose to him and said: "O Abu Amr, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has appointed you over your clients to judge over them." Sa'd said: "Will you pledge to me the covenant and compact of Allah that the judgment regarding them is what I decide?" They said: "Yes." He said: "And upon whoever is here in this direction, where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is," while he turned away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ out of reverence for him. [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes."] (The words in brackets are omitted in manuscript "A".) Sa'd said: "Then I judge concerning them that the men be killed, the property be divided, and the children and women be taken captive." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Sa'd: "You have judged concerning them with the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens." [(Narrated by al-Tabari, 21/153; and the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs with the wording: "You have judged concerning them with the judgment of the King"; the author narrated it with this wording in Sharh al-Sunna, 11/91-92. See also al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 133; Ibn Hishlam, 3/239-240, who narrated it from Alqama ibn Waqqas al-Laythi as a mursal report.)] Then they were brought down, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ detained them in the house of Bint al-Harith, a woman from Bani al-Najjar. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the market of Medina, which is its market today, and dug trenches there. Then he sent for them, and their necks were struck in those trenches, being brought out to him in groups. Among them were the enemy of Allah Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn Asad, the chief of the people. They numbered six hundred or seven hundred, and the one who gave the highest number said they were between eight hundred and nine hundred. Some of them said to Ka'b ibn Asad, while they were being led to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in groups: "O Ka'b, what do you think will be done with us?" Ka'b said: "Will you not understand at every stage? Do you not see that the summoner does not call back, and that whoever among you is taken away does not return? By Allah, it is death." That continued until the Prophet ﷺ had finished with them. Huyayy ibn Akhtab, the enemy of Allah, came to him wearing a garment of apple-colored cloth, which had been slashed on every side at the width of a fingertip, so that it would not be stripped from him whole, his hands bound to his neck with a rope. When he looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "As for me, by Allah, I did not blame myself for my enmity toward you, but whoever forsakes Allah will be forsaken." Then he turned to the people and said: "O people, there is no harm in the command of Allah: it is a Book, a decree, and a slaughter written upon the Children of Israel." Then he sat down and his neck was struck.

Urwa ibn al-Zubayr narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "None of the women of Bani Qurayza was killed except one woman." She said: "By Allah, she was with me, conversing with me and laughing greatly, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was killing their men with swords, when a caller called out her name: 'Where is so-and-so?' She said: 'I am here.' I said: 'Woe to you, what is wrong with you?' She said: 'I am being killed.' I said: 'Why?' She said: 'Because of a deed I committed.'" She said: "So she was taken away and her neck was struck." Aisha used to say: "I cannot forget her wonder: her good spirits and her great laughter, though she knew she was going to be killed." Al-Waqidi said: "The name of that woman was Shababa, the wife of al-Hakam al-Qurazi. She had killed Khallad ibn Suwayd, dropping a millstone on him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned her and her neck was struck in retaliation for Khallad ibn Suwayd." [(Narrated by al-Tabari, 21/153-154; and Ibn Ishaq, 3/242.)] He said: "Ali and al-Zubayr were striking the necks of Bani Qurayza, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting there."

Al-Baghawi's *Ma'alim al-Tanzil* (Commentary on Surah 33, verses 24–26), part 3 of 3:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from al-Zuhri that al-Zubayr ibn Bata al-Qurazi, who was known by the kunya Abu Abd al-Rahman, had shown favor to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas in the pre-Islamic period, on the day of Bu'ath. He had captured him, shaved his forelock, and then released him. On the day of Qurayzah, Thabit came to him, and al-Zubayr was an elderly man. He said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, do you recognize me?" He replied: "Would someone like you fail to recognize someone like me?" Thabit said: "I wish to repay you for the favor you did me." He replied: "Indeed, the noble repays the noble." Then Thabit went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, al-Zubayr once did me a favor, and I owe him a debt. I wish to repay him for it, so grant me his life." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "He is yours." So Thabit went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has granted me your life." He said: "An elderly man with no family and no children, what will he do with life?" Thabit then went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, what about his family and his property?" He said: "They are yours." So Thabit went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has given me your wife and your children, so they are yours." He said: "A household in the Hijaz (the region of western Arabia) without property, how will they survive like that?" Thabit then went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, what about his property?" He said: "It is yours." So Thabit went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has given me your property, so it is yours." Al-Zubayr said: "O Thabit, what did God do to the one whose face was a Chinese mirror in which the maidens of the tribe of Ka'b ibn Asad would see themselves?" Thabit said: "He was killed." He said: "And what became of the lord of the settled and the nomadic, Huyayy ibn Akhtab?" Thabit said: "He was killed." He said: "And what became of our vanguard when we charged, and our defender when we retreated, Azal ibn Shamu'il?" Thabit said: "He was killed." He said: "And what became of the two assemblies, meaning the Banu Ka'b ibn Qurayzah and the Banu Amr ibn Qurayzah?" Thabit said: "They departed and were killed." He said: "Then I ask you, by the favor I did you, O Thabit, to join me with my people. By God, there is no good in life after these men. I am not patient for even the span of a bucket's drawing of water until I meet my beloved." So Thabit brought him forward and struck his neck. When Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) heard his words, "until I meet my beloved," he said: "By God, he will meet them in the Fire of Hell, abiding in it forever and eternally." [[See: Ibn Hisham: 3 / 242–243.]]

It is said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had ordered the killing of anyone among them who had reached puberty. [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 2 / 76–77, from Atiyyah ibn Sa'd al-Qurazi.]] Then he divided the property, women, and children of the Banu Qurayzah among the Muslims. On that day the shares for horses and the shares for men were established, and he set aside the one-fifth from them. A cavalryman received three shares: two for the horse and one for the rider. A foot soldier who had no horse received one share. There were thirty-six horses, and this was the first spoils in which the two shares for horses were applied. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Sa'd ibn Zayd al-Ansari, a brother of the Banu Abd al-Ashhal, with some of the captives from the Banu Qurayzah to Najd, where he bought horses and weapons with them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had chosen for himself from their women Rayhanah bint Amr ibn Khanafah, one of the women of the Banu Amr ibn Qurayzah. She remained with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) until he died, while she was in his possession. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was keen to marry her and to place the veil upon her, but she said: "O Messenger of God, rather keep me in your possession, for that is lighter on me and on you." So he left her. When he had taken her captive, she had disliked Islam and refused anything but Judaism. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) set her aside and was troubled in himself by this matter of hers. While he was with his companions, he heard the sound of two sandals behind him and said: "Surely this is Tha'labah ibn Sha'bah bringing me the good news of Rayhanah's conversion to Islam." He came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, Rayhanah has embraced Islam." This delighted him. [[See: Ibn Hisham: 3 / 242–243.]]

When the affair of the Banu Qurayzah was concluded, the wound of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh burst open. This happened because, after he had given his judgment concerning the Banu Qurayzah, he supplicated, saying: "O God, You know that there was no people more beloved to me to fight than a people who denied Your Messenger. O God, if You have left any of the war against Quraysh upon Your Messenger, then keep me alive for it. But if You have ended the war between him and them, then take my soul to You." His wound then burst open, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought him back to his tent, which had been pitched for him in the mosque. A'ishah said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, and Umar attended him. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I could recognize Umar's weeping from Abu Bakr's, while I was in my chamber." She said: "They were as God the Exalted described: ﴿compassionate among themselves﴾ [al-Fath: 29]." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 6 / 141–142.]] The conquest of the Banu Qurayzah took place at the end of Dhu al-Qa'dah in the fifth year after the Hijrah (migration to Medina).

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us, Yahya ibn Adam informed us, Isra'il informed us, I heard Abu Ishaq say: I heard Sulayman ibn Surad say: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say, when he had driven the confederates away from him: "Now we shall attack them, and they will not attack us; we shall march against them." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi: chapter on the Battle of the Trench, 7 / 405; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14 / 7–8.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Miliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Qutaybah informed us, al-Layth informed us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: "There is no god but God alone; He made His army mighty, gave victory to His servant, and defeated the confederates alone; there is nothing after Him." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi: chapter on the Battle of the Trench, 7 / 406; Muslim in al-Dhikr wal-Du'a wal-Tawbah wal-Istighfar, chapter: seeking refuge from the evil of what one has done and from the evil of what one has not done, no. 2724, 4 / 2089, from Qutaybah; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14 / 8.]]

God the Exalted said regarding the story of the Banu Qurayzah: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported them from their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts. A group you killed, and a group you took captive.﴾ The first group are the men. It is said they numbered six hundred. The second group, ﴿a group you took captive﴾, are the women and the offspring. It is said they numbered seven hundred and fifty, and it is also said nine hundred. [[See the full narrative in Ibn Hisham's Sirah: 3 / 233–243.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verses 24–26 (part 1 of 3):**

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So that Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness﴾, meaning the reward of their truthfulness. Their truthfulness is their fulfilment of the covenant. ﴿And punish the hypocrites if He wills, or turn to them in forgiveness﴾, so that He guides them to faith. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved﴾, from Quraysh and Ghatafan, ﴿in their rage﴾, not healing their hearts by attaining what they wanted. ﴿They gained no good﴾, meaning no victory. ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting﴾, by means of the angels and the wind. ﴿And Allah is ever Strong and Mighty﴾ [strong in His dominion, mighty] [[What is between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]] in His retribution.

﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them﴾, meaning those who aided the confederates of Quraysh and Ghatafan against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, and they were the Banu Qurayzah. ﴿From their fortresses﴾, meaning their strongholds and refuges. Its singular is ṣayṣiyah, and from it is said of the horn [of an animal] and of the spur of a cock and of the weaver's comb that it is a ṣayṣiyah. [From this root comes the term for the horn, the spur of the rooster, and the weaver's comb, ṣayṣiyah.] [[What is between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]]

The reason for this is that when morning came on the night in which the confederates withdrew, returning to their lands, and the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers departed from the Trench to Medina and laid down their weapons, at noon Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), wrapped in a turban of brocade, riding a mule with a saddle [[al-rihalah: the saddle.]] and a silk covering, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was washing his head, having washed one side of it. [Jibril] said: "Have you laid down the weapons, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." Jibril said: "May Allah pardon you. The angels have not laid down their weapons for forty nights, and I have only just now returned from pursuing the people."

It is also narrated that dust was on the face of Jibril, peace be upon him, and on his horse, so the Prophet (ﷺ) began wiping the dust from his face and from his horse. [Jibril] said: "Allah commands you to march against Banu Qurayzah, so advance [[Go forth against them. To nahd (rise up) against an enemy means to stand firm before them and begin fighting them.]] against them. Indeed, I have cut their bowstrings, opened their gates, and left them in turmoil and confusion." [[See al-Bukhari: 7/407; Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/10–11.]] So the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered a caller, who proclaimed: "Whoever is listening and obedient, let him not pray the afternoon prayer except at Banu Qurayzah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, ahead with his banner, and the people hastened toward it. ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, advanced until he drew near the fortresses, and he heard from them a vile remark about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He turned back and met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the road and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you should not approach these vile people." [The Prophet] said: "Why? Do you think you heard harm from them toward me?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "If they had seen me, they would not have said anything of that sort."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drew near their fortresses, he said: "O brothers of the apes and the swine! Has Allah disgraced you and brought down His vengeance upon you?" They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, you were never ignorant."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by his companions at al-Sawrayn [[A place near Medina.]] before he reached Banu Qurayzah, and said: "Has anyone passed by you?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah. Dihyah ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi passed by us on a white mule with a saddle and a silk brocade covering." He, peace be upon him, said: "That was Jibril. He was sent to Banu Qurayzah to shake their fortresses and to cast terror into their hearts."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Banu Qurayzah, he stopped at one of their wells, in an area of their property. People caught up with him, and men came to him after the late night prayer [[Al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah: the night prayer, meaning the final evening prayer.]] and they had not yet prayed the afternoon prayer, because of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "None of you should pray the afternoon prayer except at Banu Qurayzah." So they prayed the afternoon prayer there after the late night prayer. Allah did not reproach them for that, nor did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rebuke them for it. [The narrator] said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them for twenty-five nights, until the siege exhausted them, and Allah cast terror into their hearts.

Huyayy ibn Akhtab had entered upon Banu Qurayzah in their fortress when Quraysh and Ghatafan withdrew from them, in fulfilment of his pledge to Kaʿb ibn Asad, which he had made to him.

When they were certain that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not leave them until he fought them, Ka'b ibn Asad said: "O assembly of Jews, you can see the situation that has come upon you. I am offering you three options, so take whichever of them you wish." They said, "And what are they?" He said: "We follow this man and believe him. By Allah, it has become clear to you that he is a prophet sent by God, and that he is the one you find described in your Book. Then you will be secure for your homes, your property, your sons and your women." They said: "We will never abandon the judgment of the Torah (al-Tawrat) or exchange it for anything else." He said: "If you refuse this, then come, let us kill our sons and our women, then go out to Muhammad as men with drawn swords, leaving behind us no burden that concerns us, until Allah judges between us and Muhammad. If we perish, we will perish and leave behind nothing we fear for. And if we prevail, then by my life, we will take women and sons (again)." They said: "We would kill these poor people? What good is life after them?" He said: "If you refuse this, then tonight is the night of Saturday (al-Sabt), and it may be that Muhammad and his companions feel secure on it, so go down (to attack them), perhaps we may strike Muhammad and his companions by surprise." They said: "Shall we desecrate our Sabbath and innovate in it what those before us did not innovate? Do you not know what befell those who did so, of transformation (into apes and swine)?" He said: "No man among you has spent a single night since his mother bore him in the age being resolute?" Then they sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "Send to us Abu Lubaba ibn Abd al-Mundhir, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, who were allies of the Aws, so that we may consult him about our affair." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to them. When they saw him, the men stood up to him, the women and children greeted him weeping before his face, and he was moved with pity for them. They said: "O Abu Lubaba, do you think we should submit to the judgment of Muhammad?" He said: "Yes." [They said: "What will he do to us if we submit?"] (The words in brackets are omitted in manuscript "A".) He pointed with his hand to his throat, meaning slaughter. Abu Lubaba said: "By Allah, my feet had not moved from their place before I knew that I had betrayed Allah and His Messenger." Then Abu Lubaba set off on his way and did not go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he tied himself to one of the pillars of the mosque, and said: "I will not move from my place until Allah accepts my repentance for what I have done." He pledged to Allah that he would never set foot on the land of Bani Qurayza again, and that Allah would never see him in a land where he had betrayed Allah and His Messenger. When news of him reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he was late (in returning), he said: "If he had come to me, I would have asked forgiveness for him. But since he has done what he has done, I will not release him from his place until Allah accepts his repentance." Then Allah the Exalted sent down the repentance of Abu Lubaba upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in the house of Umm Salama. Umm Salama said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughing, so I said: 'What makes you laugh, O Messenger of Allah? May Allah make your teeth laugh?' He said: 'Repentance has been accepted for Abu Lubaba.' I said: 'Shall I not give him the good news of that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, if you wish.' So she stood at the door of her chamber, and that was before the veil was imposed upon them, and she said: 'O Abu Lubaba, rejoice, for Allah has accepted your repentance.'" He said: "The people rushed to him to release him, but he said: 'No, by Allah, not until the Messenger of Allah himself releases me with his hand.' When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by him going out to the dawn prayer, he released him." Then he said: "Tha'laba ibn Sha'ba, Usayd ibn Sha'ba, and Usayd ibn Ubayd, and they are a group from the Banu Hudhayl, who are neither of Qurayza nor of al-Nadir, their lineage being above that, they are cousins of the people (of Qurayza), embraced Islam on that night in which Bani Qurayza descended upon the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." On that night Amr ibn Sa'da al-Qurazi went out and passed by the guard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who that night was Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansari. When he saw him, he said: "Who is this?" He said: "Amr ibn Sa'da." Amr had refused to join Bani Qurayza in their treachery against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he had said: "I will never betray Muhammad." When Muhammad ibn Maslama recognized him, he said: "O Allah, do not deprive me of the slips of the noble," and then he let him go. So he went out on his way and spent that night in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Medina, then departed, and no one knows where he went in the land of Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was told of his situation, and he said: "That is a man whom Allah has saved by his fidelity." [(Narrated by al-Tabari, 21/152; see also Ibn Hisham, 3/238-239.)] Some people claim that he had been bound with a rope among those of Bani Qurayza who were bound when they descended upon the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in the morning his rope was found lying loose, and no one knew where he had gone, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that statement about him. And Allah knows best. When morning came, they descended upon the judgment of the Messenger of Allah. Then the Aws rose up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are our clients (mawali) rather than of the Khazraj, and you did with the clients of the Khazraj yesterday what you know." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had earlier besieged Bani Qaynuqa', who were allies of the Khazraj, and they descended upon his judgment, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul asked him to spare them, and he granted them to him. When the Aws spoke to him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Are you not content, O assembly of the Aws, that a man from among you should judge among you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then the matter is left to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh had been placed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the tent of a Muslim woman called Rufayda, in his mosque, and she used to treat the wounded and would devote herself to serving whoever among the Muslims was in need. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to his people when the arrow struck him at the Trench: "Place him in the tent of Rufayda until I visit him soon." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him as judge over Bani Qurayza, his people came to him and carried him on a donkey over which they had spread a leather cushion, and he was a large man. Then they came with him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "O Abu Amr, be good to your clients, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only appointed you so that you would be good to them." When they pressed him much, he said: "The time has come for Sa'd that in the cause of Allah he should not fear the blame of any blamer." Some of those from his people who had been with him returned to the house of Bani al-Ashhal and lamented for them the men of Bani Qurayza, before Sa'd ibn Mu'adh reached them, because of his word that he had heard from him. When Sa'd reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "Rise up to your chief and bring him down." They rose to him and said: "O Abu Amr, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has appointed you over your clients to judge over them." Sa'd said: "Will you pledge to me the covenant and compact of Allah that the judgment regarding them is what I decide?" They said: "Yes." He said: "And upon whoever is here in this direction, where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is," while he turned away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ out of reverence for him. [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes."] (The words in brackets are omitted in manuscript "A".) Sa'd said: "Then I judge concerning them that the men be killed, the property be divided, and the children and women be taken captive." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Sa'd: "You have judged concerning them with the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens." [(Narrated by al-Tabari, 21/153; and the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs with the wording: "You have judged concerning them with the judgment of the King"; the author narrated it with this wording in Sharh al-Sunna, 11/91-92. See also al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 133; Ibn Hishlam, 3/239-240, who narrated it from Alqama ibn Waqqas al-Laythi as a mursal report.)] Then they were brought down, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ detained them in the house of Bint al-Harith, a woman from Bani al-Najjar. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the market of Medina, which is its market today, and dug trenches there. Then he sent for them, and their necks were struck in those trenches, being brought out to him in groups. Among them were the enemy of Allah Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn Asad, the chief of the people. They numbered six hundred or seven hundred, and the one who gave the highest number said they were between eight hundred and nine hundred. Some of them said to Ka'b ibn Asad, while they were being led to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in groups: "O Ka'b, what do you think will be done with us?" Ka'b said: "Will you not understand at every stage? Do you not see that the summoner does not call back, and that whoever among you is taken away does not return? By Allah, it is death." That continued until the Prophet ﷺ had finished with them. Huyayy ibn Akhtab, the enemy of Allah, came to him wearing a garment of apple-colored cloth, which had been slashed on every side at the width of a fingertip, so that it would not be stripped from him whole, his hands bound to his neck with a rope. When he looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "As for me, by Allah, I did not blame myself for my enmity toward you, but whoever forsakes Allah will be forsaken." Then he turned to the people and said: "O people, there is no harm in the command of Allah: it is a Book, a decree, and a slaughter written upon the Children of Israel." Then he sat down and his neck was struck.

Urwa ibn al-Zubayr narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "None of the women of Bani Qurayza was killed except one woman." She said: "By Allah, she was with me, conversing with me and laughing greatly, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was killing their men with swords, when a caller called out her name: 'Where is so-and-so?' She said: 'I am here.' I said: 'Woe to you, what is wrong with you?' She said: 'I am being killed.' I said: 'Why?' She said: 'Because of a deed I committed.'" She said: "So she was taken away and her neck was struck." Aisha used to say: "I cannot forget her wonder: her good spirits and her great laughter, though she knew she was going to be killed." Al-Waqidi said: "The name of that woman was Shababa, the wife of al-Hakam al-Qurazi. She had killed Khallad ibn Suwayd, dropping a millstone on him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned her and her neck was struck in retaliation for Khallad ibn Suwayd." [(Narrated by al-Tabari, 21/153-154; and Ibn Ishaq, 3/242.)] He said: "Ali and al-Zubayr were striking the necks of Bani Qurayza, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting there."

Al-Baghawi's *Ma'alim al-Tanzil* (Commentary on Surah 33, verses 24–26), part 3 of 3:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from al-Zuhri that al-Zubayr ibn Bata al-Qurazi, who was known by the kunya Abu Abd al-Rahman, had shown favor to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas in the pre-Islamic period, on the day of Bu'ath. He had captured him, shaved his forelock, and then released him. On the day of Qurayzah, Thabit came to him, and al-Zubayr was an elderly man. He said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, do you recognize me?" He replied: "Would someone like you fail to recognize someone like me?" Thabit said: "I wish to repay you for the favor you did me." He replied: "Indeed, the noble repays the noble." Then Thabit went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, al-Zubayr once did me a favor, and I owe him a debt. I wish to repay him for it, so grant me his life." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "He is yours." So Thabit went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has granted me your life." He said: "An elderly man with no family and no children, what will he do with life?" Thabit then went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, what about his family and his property?" He said: "They are yours." So Thabit went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has given me your wife and your children, so they are yours." He said: "A household in the Hijaz (the region of western Arabia) without property, how will they survive like that?" Thabit then went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, what about his property?" He said: "It is yours." So Thabit went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has given me your property, so it is yours." Al-Zubayr said: "O Thabit, what did God do to the one whose face was a Chinese mirror in which the maidens of the tribe of Ka'b ibn Asad would see themselves?" Thabit said: "He was killed." He said: "And what became of the lord of the settled and the nomadic, Huyayy ibn Akhtab?" Thabit said: "He was killed." He said: "And what became of our vanguard when we charged, and our defender when we retreated, Azal ibn Shamu'il?" Thabit said: "He was killed." He said: "And what became of the two assemblies, meaning the Banu Ka'b ibn Qurayzah and the Banu Amr ibn Qurayzah?" Thabit said: "They departed and were killed." He said: "Then I ask you, by the favor I did you, O Thabit, to join me with my people. By God, there is no good in life after these men. I am not patient for even the span of a bucket's drawing of water until I meet my beloved." So Thabit brought him forward and struck his neck. When Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) heard his words, "until I meet my beloved," he said: "By God, he will meet them in the Fire of Hell, abiding in it forever and eternally." [[See: Ibn Hisham: 3 / 242–243.]]

It is said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had ordered the killing of anyone among them who had reached puberty. [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 2 / 76–77, from Atiyyah ibn Sa'd al-Qurazi.]] Then he divided the property, women, and children of the Banu Qurayzah among the Muslims. On that day the shares for horses and the shares for men were established, and he set aside the one-fifth from them. A cavalryman received three shares: two for the horse and one for the rider. A foot soldier who had no horse received one share. There were thirty-six horses, and this was the first spoils in which the two shares for horses were applied. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Sa'd ibn Zayd al-Ansari, a brother of the Banu Abd al-Ashhal, with some of the captives from the Banu Qurayzah to Najd, where he bought horses and weapons with them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had chosen for himself from their women Rayhanah bint Amr ibn Khanafah, one of the women of the Banu Amr ibn Qurayzah. She remained with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) until he died, while she was in his possession. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was keen to marry her and to place the veil upon her, but she said: "O Messenger of God, rather keep me in your possession, for that is lighter on me and on you." So he left her. When he had taken her captive, she had disliked Islam and refused anything but Judaism. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) set her aside and was troubled in himself by this matter of hers. While he was with his companions, he heard the sound of two sandals behind him and said: "Surely this is Tha'labah ibn Sha'bah bringing me the good news of Rayhanah's conversion to Islam." He came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, Rayhanah has embraced Islam." This delighted him. [[See: Ibn Hisham: 3 / 242–243.]]

When the affair of the Banu Qurayzah was concluded, the wound of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh burst open. This happened because, after he had given his judgment concerning the Banu Qurayzah, he supplicated, saying: "O God, You know that there was no people more beloved to me to fight than a people who denied Your Messenger. O God, if You have left any of the war against Quraysh upon Your Messenger, then keep me alive for it. But if You have ended the war between him and them, then take my soul to You." His wound then burst open, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought him back to his tent, which had been pitched for him in the mosque. A'ishah said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, and Umar attended him. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I could recognize Umar's weeping from Abu Bakr's, while I was in my chamber." She said: "They were as God the Exalted described: ﴿compassionate among themselves﴾ [al-Fath: 29]." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 6 / 141–142.]] The conquest of the Banu Qurayzah took place at the end of Dhu al-Qa'dah in the fifth year after the Hijrah (migration to Medina).

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad informed us, Yahya ibn Adam informed us, Isra'il informed us, I heard Abu Ishaq say: I heard Sulayman ibn Surad say: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say, when he had driven the confederates away from him: "Now we shall attack them, and they will not attack us; we shall march against them." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi: chapter on the Battle of the Trench, 7 / 405; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14 / 7–8.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Miliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Qutaybah informed us, al-Layth informed us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: "There is no god but God alone; He made His army mighty, gave victory to His servant, and defeated the confederates alone; there is nothing after Him." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi: chapter on the Battle of the Trench, 7 / 406; Muslim in al-Dhikr wal-Du'a wal-Tawbah wal-Istighfar, chapter: seeking refuge from the evil of what one has done and from the evil of what one has not done, no. 2724, 4 / 2089, from Qutaybah; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14 / 8.]]

God the Exalted said regarding the story of the Banu Qurayzah: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported them from their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts. A group you killed, and a group you took captive.﴾ The first group are the men. It is said they numbered six hundred. The second group, ﴿a group you took captive﴾, are the women and the offspring. It is said they numbered seven hundred and fifty, and it is also said nine hundred. [[See the full narrative in Ibn Hisham's Sirah: 3 / 233–243.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verses 24–26 (part 1 of 3):**

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So that Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness﴾, meaning the reward of their truthfulness. Their truthfulness is their fulfilment of the covenant. ﴿And punish the hypocrites if He wills, or turn to them in forgiveness﴾, so that He guides them to faith. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved﴾, from Quraysh and Ghatafan, ﴿in their rage﴾, not healing their hearts by attaining what they wanted. ﴿They gained no good﴾, meaning no victory. ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting﴾, by means of the angels and the wind. ﴿And Allah is ever Strong and Mighty﴾ [strong in His dominion, mighty] [[What is between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]] in His retribution.

﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them﴾, meaning those who aided the confederates of Quraysh and Ghatafan against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims, and they were the Banu Qurayzah. ﴿From their fortresses﴾, meaning their strongholds and refuges. Its singular is ṣayṣiyah, and from it is said of the horn [of an animal] and of the spur of a cock and of the weaver's comb that it is a ṣayṣiyah. [From this root comes the term for the horn, the spur of the rooster, and the weaver's comb, ṣayṣiyah.] [[What is between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]]

The reason for this is that when morning came on the night in which the confederates withdrew, returning to their lands, and the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers departed from the Trench to Medina and laid down their weapons, at noon Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), wrapped in a turban of brocade, riding a mule with a saddle [[al-rihalah: the saddle.]] and a silk covering, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was washing his head, having washed one side of it. [Jibril] said: "Have you laid down the weapons, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." Jibril said: "May Allah pardon you. The angels have not laid down their weapons for forty nights, and I have only just now returned from pursuing the people."

It is also narrated that dust was on the face of Jibril, peace be upon him, and on his horse, so the Prophet (ﷺ) began wiping the dust from his face and from his horse. [Jibril] said: "Allah commands you to march against Banu Qurayzah, so advance [[Go forth against them. To nahd (rise up) against an enemy means to stand firm before them and begin fighting them.]] against them. Indeed, I have cut their bowstrings, opened their gates, and left them in turmoil and confusion." [[See al-Bukhari: 7/407; Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/10–11.]] So the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered a caller, who proclaimed: "Whoever is listening and obedient, let him not pray the afternoon prayer except at Banu Qurayzah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, ahead with his banner, and the people hastened toward it. ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, advanced until he drew near the fortresses, and he heard from them a vile remark about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He turned back and met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the road and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you should not approach these vile people." [The Prophet] said: "Why? Do you think you heard harm from them toward me?" He said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "If they had seen me, they would not have said anything of that sort."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drew near their fortresses, he said: "O brothers of the apes and the swine! Has Allah disgraced you and brought down His vengeance upon you?" They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, you were never ignorant."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by his companions at al-Sawrayn [[A place near Medina.]] before he reached Banu Qurayzah, and said: "Has anyone passed by you?" They said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah. Dihyah ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi passed by us on a white mule with a saddle and a silk brocade covering." He, peace be upon him, said: "That was Jibril. He was sent to Banu Qurayzah to shake their fortresses and to cast terror into their hearts."

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Banu Qurayzah, he stopped at one of their wells, in an area of their property. People caught up with him, and men came to him after the late night prayer [[Al-ʿishāʾ al-ākhirah: the night prayer, meaning the final evening prayer.]] and they had not yet prayed the afternoon prayer, because of the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "None of you should pray the afternoon prayer except at Banu Qurayzah." So they prayed the afternoon prayer there after the late night prayer. Allah did not reproach them for that, nor did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rebuke them for it. [The narrator] said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them for twenty-five nights, until the siege exhausted them, and Allah cast terror into their hearts.

Huyayy ibn Akhtab had entered upon Banu Qurayzah in their fortress when Quraysh and Ghatafan withdrew from them, in fulfilment of his pledge to Kaʿb ibn Asad, which he had made to him.

When they were certain that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not leave them until he fought them, Ka'b ibn Asad said: "O assembly of Jews, you can see the situation that has come upon you. I am offering you three options, so take whichever of them you wish." They said, "And what are they?" He said: "We follow this man and believe him. By Allah, it has become clear to you that he is a prophet sent by God, and that he is the one you find described in your Book. Then you will be secure for your homes, your property, your sons and your women." They said: "We will never abandon the judgment of the Torah (al-Tawrat) or exchange it for anything else." He said: "If you refuse this, then come, let us kill our sons and our women, then go out to Muhammad as men with drawn swords, leaving behind us no burden that concerns us, until Allah judges between us and Muhammad. If we perish, we will perish and leave behind nothing we fear for. And if we prevail, then by my life, we will take women and sons (again)." They said: "We would kill these poor people? What good is life after them?" He said: "If you refuse this, then tonight is the night of Saturday (al-Sabt), and it may be that Muhammad and his companions feel secure on it, so go down (to attack them), perhaps we may strike Muhammad and his companions by surprise." They said: "Shall we desecrate our Sabbath and innovate in it what those before us did not innovate? Do you not know what befell those who did so, of transformation (into apes and swine)?" He said: "No man among you has spent a single night since his mother bore him in the age being resolute?" Then they sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "Send to us Abu Lubaba ibn Abd al-Mundhir, brother of the Banu Amr ibn Awf, who were allies of the Aws, so that we may consult him about our affair." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent him to them. When they saw him, the men stood up to him, the women and children greeted him weeping before his face, and he was moved with pity for them. They said: "O Abu Lubaba, do you think we should submit to the judgment of Muhammad?" He said: "Yes." [They said: "What will he do to us if we submit?"] (The words in brackets are omitted in manuscript "A".) He pointed with his hand to his throat, meaning slaughter. Abu Lubaba said: "By Allah, my feet had not moved from their place before I knew that I had betrayed Allah and His Messenger." Then Abu Lubaba set off on his way and did not go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until he tied himself to one of the pillars of the mosque, and said: "I will not move from my place until Allah accepts my repentance for what I have done." He pledged to Allah that he would never set foot on the land of Bani Qurayza again, and that Allah would never see him in a land where he had betrayed Allah and His Messenger. When news of him reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he was late (in returning), he said: "If he had come to me, I would have asked forgiveness for him. But since he has done what he has done, I will not release him from his place until Allah accepts his repentance." Then Allah the Exalted sent down the repentance of Abu Lubaba upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in the house of Umm Salama. Umm Salama said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughing, so I said: 'What makes you laugh, O Messenger of Allah? May Allah make your teeth laugh?' He said: 'Repentance has been accepted for Abu Lubaba.' I said: 'Shall I not give him the good news of that, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Yes, if you wish.' So she stood at the door of her chamber, and that was before the veil was imposed upon them, and she said: 'O Abu Lubaba, rejoice, for Allah has accepted your repentance.'" He said: "The people rushed to him to release him, but he said: 'No, by Allah, not until the Messenger of Allah himself releases me with his hand.' When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by him going out to the dawn prayer, he released him." Then he said: "Tha'laba ibn Sha'ba, Usayd ibn Sha'ba, and Usayd ibn Ubayd, and they are a group from the Banu Hudhayl, who are neither of Qurayza nor of al-Nadir, their lineage being above that, they are cousins of the people (of Qurayza), embraced Islam on that night in which Bani Qurayza descended upon the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." On that night Amr ibn Sa'da al-Qurazi went out and passed by the guard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who that night was Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansari. When he saw him, he said: "Who is this?" He said: "Amr ibn Sa'da." Amr had refused to join Bani Qurayza in their treachery against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he had said: "I will never betray Muhammad." When Muhammad ibn Maslama recognized him, he said: "O Allah, do not deprive me of the slips of the noble," and then he let him go. So he went out on his way and spent that night in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Medina, then departed, and no one knows where he went in the land of Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was told of his situation, and he said: "That is a man whom Allah has saved by his fidelity." [(Narrated by al-Tabari, 21/152; see also Ibn Hisham, 3/238-239.)] Some people claim that he had been bound with a rope among those of Bani Qurayza who were bound when they descended upon the judgment of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and in the morning his rope was found lying loose, and no one knew where he had gone, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said that statement about him. And Allah knows best. When morning came, they descended upon the judgment of the Messenger of Allah. Then the Aws rose up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are our clients (mawali) rather than of the Khazraj, and you did with the clients of the Khazraj yesterday what you know." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had earlier besieged Bani Qaynuqa', who were allies of the Khazraj, and they descended upon his judgment, and Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul asked him to spare them, and he granted them to him. When the Aws spoke to him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Are you not content, O assembly of the Aws, that a man from among you should judge among you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then the matter is left to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh had been placed by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the tent of a Muslim woman called Rufayda, in his mosque, and she used to treat the wounded and would devote herself to serving whoever among the Muslims was in need. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to his people when the arrow struck him at the Trench: "Place him in the tent of Rufayda until I visit him soon." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ appointed him as judge over Bani Qurayza, his people came to him and carried him on a donkey over which they had spread a leather cushion, and he was a large man. Then they came with him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying: "O Abu Amr, be good to your clients, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ only appointed you so that you would be good to them." When they pressed him much, he said: "The time has come for Sa'd that in the cause of Allah he should not fear the blame of any blamer." Some of those from his people who had been with him returned to the house of Bani al-Ashhal and lamented for them the men of Bani Qurayza, before Sa'd ibn Mu'adh reached them, because of his word that he had heard from him. When Sa'd reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "Rise up to your chief and bring him down." They rose to him and said: "O Abu Amr, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has appointed you over your clients to judge over them." Sa'd said: "Will you pledge to me the covenant and compact of Allah that the judgment regarding them is what I decide?" They said: "Yes." He said: "And upon whoever is here in this direction, where the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is," while he turned away from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ out of reverence for him. [The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Yes."] (The words in brackets are omitted in manuscript "A".) Sa'd said: "Then I judge concerning them that the men be killed, the property be divided, and the children and women be taken captive." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Sa'd: "You have judged concerning them with the judgment of Allah from above the seven heavens." [(Narrated by al-Tabari, 21/153; and the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs with the wording: "You have judged concerning them with the judgment of the King"; the author narrated it with this wording in Sharh al-Sunna, 11/91-92. See also al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 133; Ibn Hishlam, 3/239-240, who narrated it from Alqama ibn Waqqas al-Laythi as a mursal report.)] Then they were brought down, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ detained them in the house of Bint al-Harith, a woman from Bani al-Najjar. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to the market of Medina, which is its market today, and dug trenches there. Then he sent for them, and their necks were struck in those trenches, being brought out to him in groups. Among them were the enemy of Allah Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn Asad, the chief of the people. They numbered six hundred or seven hundred, and the one who gave the highest number said they were between eight hundred and nine hundred. Some of them said to Ka'b ibn Asad, while they were being led to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in groups: "O Ka'b, what do you think will be done with us?" Ka'b said: "Will you not understand at every stage? Do you not see that the summoner does not call back, and that whoever among you is taken away does not return? By Allah, it is death." That continued until the Prophet ﷺ had finished with them. Huyayy ibn Akhtab, the enemy of Allah, came to him wearing a garment of apple-colored cloth, which had been slashed on every side at the width of a fingertip, so that it would not be stripped from him whole, his hands bound to his neck with a rope. When he looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he said: "As for me, by Allah, I did not blame myself for my enmity toward you, but whoever forsakes Allah will be forsaken." Then he turned to the people and said: "O people, there is no harm in the command of Allah: it is a Book, a decree, and a slaughter written upon the Children of Israel." Then he sat down and his neck was struck.

Urwa ibn al-Zubayr narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "None of the women of Bani Qurayza was killed except one woman." She said: "By Allah, she was with me, conversing with me and laughing greatly, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was killing their men with swords, when a caller called out her name: 'Where is so-and-so?' She said: 'I am here.' I said: 'Woe to you, what is wrong with you?' She said: 'I am being killed.' I said: 'Why?' She said: 'Because of a deed I committed.'" She said: "So she was taken away and her neck was struck." Aisha used to say: "I cannot forget her wonder: her good spirits and her great laughter, though she knew she was going to be killed." Al-Waqidi said: "The name of that woman was Shababa, the wife of al-Hakam al-Qurazi. She had killed Khallad ibn Suwayd, dropping a millstone on him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned her and her neck was struck in retaliation for Khallad ibn Suwayd." [(Narrated by al-Tabari, 21/153-154; and Ibn Ishaq, 3/242.)] He said: "Ali and al-Zubayr were striking the necks of Bani Qurayza, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting there."

Al-Baghawi's *Ma'alim al-Tanzil* (Commentary on Surah 33, verses 24–26), part 3 of 3:

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated from al-Zuhri that al-Zubayr ibn Bata al-Qurazi, who was known by the kunya Abu Abd al-Rahman, had shown favor to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas in the pre-Islamic period, on the day of Bu'ath. He had captured him, shaved his forelock, and then released him. On the day of Qurayzah, Thabit came to him, and al-Zubayr was an elderly man. He said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, do you recognize me?" He replied: "Would someone like you fail to recognize someone like me?" Thabit said: "I wish to repay you for the favor you did me." He replied: "Indeed, the noble repays the noble." Then Thabit went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, al-Zubayr once did me a favor, and I owe him a debt. I wish to repay him for it, so grant me his life." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "He is yours." So Thabit went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has granted me your life." He said: "An elderly man with no family and no children, what will he do with life?" Thabit then went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, what about his family and his property?" He said: "They are yours." So Thabit went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has given me your wife and your children, so they are yours." He said: "A household in the Hijaz (the region of western Arabia) without property, how will they survive like that?" Thabit then went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, what about his property?" He said: "It is yours." So Thabit went to him and said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) has given me your property, so it is yours." Al-Zubayr said: "O Thabit, what did God do to the one whose face was a Chinese mirror in which the maidens of the tribe of Ka'b ibn Asad would see themselves?" Thabit said: "He was killed." He said: "And what became of the lord of the settled and the nomadic, Huyayy ibn Akhtab?" Thabit said: "He was killed." He said: "And what became of our vanguard when we charged, and our defender when we retreated, Azal ibn Shamu'il?" Thabit said: "He was killed." He said: "And what became of the two assemblies, meaning the Banu Ka'b ibn Qurayzah and the Banu Amr ibn Qurayzah?" Thabit said: "They departed and were killed." He said: "Then I ask you, by the favor I did you, O Thabit, to join me with my people. By God, there is no good in life after these men. I am not patient for even the span of a bucket's drawing of water until I meet my beloved." So Thabit brought him forward and struck his neck. When Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may God be pleased with him) heard his words, "until I meet my beloved," he said: "By God, he will meet them in the Fire of Hell, abiding in it forever and eternally." [[See: Ibn Hisham: 3 / 242–243.]]

It is said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had ordered the killing of anyone among them who had reached puberty. [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 2 / 76–77, from Atiyyah ibn Sa'd al-Qurazi.]] Then he divided the property, women, and children of the Banu Qurayzah among the Muslims. On that day the shares for horses and the shares for men were established, and he set aside the one-fifth from them. A cavalryman received three shares: two for the horse and one for the rider. A foot soldier who had no horse received one share. There were thirty-six horses, and this was the first spoils in which the two shares for horses were applied. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent Sa'd ibn Zayd al-Ansari, a brother of the Banu Abd al-Ashhal, with some of the captives from the Banu Qurayzah to Najd, where he bought horses and weapons with them. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) had chosen for himself from their women Rayhanah bint Amr ibn Khanafah, one of the women of the Banu Amr ibn Qurayzah. She remained with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) until he died, while she was in his possession. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was keen to marry her and to place the veil upon her, but she said: "O Messenger of God, rather keep me in your possession, for that is lighter on me and on you." So he left her. When he had taken her captive, she had disliked Islam and refused anything but Judaism. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) set her aside and was troubled in himself by this matter of hers. While he was with his companions, he heard the sound of two sandals behind him and said: "Surely this is Tha'labah ibn Sha'bah bringing me the good news of Rayhanah's conversion to Islam." He came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, Rayhanah has embraced Islam." This delighted him. [[See: Ibn Hisham: 3 / 242–243.]]

When the affair of the Banu Qurayzah was concluded, the wound of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh burst open. This happened because, after he had given his judgment concerning the Banu Qurayzah, he supplicated, saying: "O God, You know that there was no people more beloved to me to fight than a people who denied Your Messenger. O God, if You have left any of the war against Quraysh upon Your Messenger, then keep me alive for it. But if You have ended the war between him and them, then take my soul to You." His wound then burst open, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) brought him back to his tent, which had been pitched for him in the mosque. A'ishah said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, and Umar attended him. By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, I could recognize Umar's weeping from Abu Bakr's, while I was in my chamber." She said: "They were as God the Exalted described: ﴿compassionate among themselves﴾ [al-Fath: 29]." [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad: 6 / 141–142.]] The conquest of the Banu Qurayzah took place at the end of Dhu al-Qa'dah in the fifth year after the Hijrah (migration to Medina).

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi: chapter on the Battle of the Trench, 7 / 405; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14 / 7–8.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Miliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Qutaybah informed us, al-Layth informed us, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: "There is no god but God alone; He made His army mighty, gave victory to His servant, and defeated the confederates alone; there is nothing after Him." God the Exalted said regarding the story of the Banu Qurayzah: ﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Book who supported them from their fortresses, and cast terror into their hearts. A group you killed, and a group you took captive.﴾ The first group are the men. It is said they numbered six hundred. The second group, ﴿a group you took captive﴾, are the women and the offspring. It is said they numbered seven hundred and fifty, and it is also said nine hundred. [[See the full narrative in Ibn Hisham's Sirah: 3 / 233–243.]]

﴿And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, and a land you had not yet trod.﴾ Ibn Zayd and Muqatil said: it means Khaybar. Qatadah said: "We were told that it is Makkah." Al-Hasan said: "Persia and Rome." Ikrimah said: "Every land that will be conquered until the Day of Resurrection." [[See al-Bahr al-Muhit 7/225.]]

﴿And Allah is ever Competent over all things.﴾

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a graceful release.﴾ The provision (mut'at al-talaq, the gift given upon divorce). ﴿But if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.﴾

The occasion of revelation of this verse: the wives of the Prophet ﷺ asked him for some worldly goods and requested an increase in maintenance, and they harmed him through jealousy of one another. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ deserted them, and he swore that he would not approach them for a month, and he did not go out to his companions. They said: "What is the matter with him?" They were saying: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has divorced his wives." Umar said: "I will surely find out his condition for you." He said: I entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, have you divorced them?" He said: "No." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I entered the mosque and the Muslims were saying: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has divorced his wives.' Shall I go down and inform them that you have not divorced them?" He said: "Yes, if you wish." So I stood at the door of the mosque and called out at the top of my voice: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ has not divorced his wives." Then this verse was revealed: "When there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it; but if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those who [can] draw conclusions from it would have known it" [al-Nisa': 83]. I was one of those who drew the conclusion from that matter. Then Allah revealed the verse of choice (ayat al-takhyir, the verse giving choice). Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 30:

His saying, Exalted and Mighty is He: ﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits an evident immorality﴾ — with a manifest disobedience. It has been said: it is like His saying, Exalted and Mighty is He: "If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be nullified" [Az-Zumar: 65], not that any of them actually committed an immorality. Ibn Abbas said: what is meant by "immorality" (fahisha) is nushuz (defiance of a husband, ill conduct toward him) and bad character.

﴿Her punishment will be doubled for her, twofold﴾. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read "nuda'if" with a nun, with kasra on the ayn and its shadda, and "al-adhab" in the accusative. The others read it with a ya and a fatha on the ayn, and "al-adhab" in the nominative. Abu Ja'far and the people of Basra also read it with a shadda. Abu Amr put a shadda on this word alone, because of His saying "twofold" (di'fayn). The others read "yudaaf" with an alif and a fatha on the ayn, and "al-adhab" in the nominative. Both are dialectal forms, like "ba''ada" and "ba'ada" (both meaning "to make distant"). Abu Amr and Abu Ubayda said: "da''aftu al-shay'" means that you made it double, and "da'afta" (with alif) means that you made it multiples of itself.

﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾. Muqatil said: her punishment is easy for Allah, and the doubling of their punishment for disobedience, because of their nobility, is like the doubling of the punishment of a free woman compared with a slave woman, and the doubling of their reward because of the elevation of their rank. In this is an indication that they are the most noble women of the worlds.

﴿And whoever is obedient﴾ means submits, ﴿among you to Allah and His Messenger﴾. Ya'qub recited "man ta'ti minkunna, wa taqnut" (whoever of you comes, and is obedient) with the *ta'* in both places. The majority (al-'amma) recited with the *ya'* because *man* (whoever) is a particle standing in place of a noun, used to refer to the singular, the plural, the masculine and the feminine. ﴿And does righteous deeds, We will give her her reward twice﴾ means double the reward of others. Muqatil said: for every good deed, twenty good deeds.

Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited "ya'mal, yu'tiha" (with the *ya'* in both places), taking it as a continuation of His words "wa man ya'ti, wa yaqnut." The others recited with the *ta'*. ﴿And We have prepared for her a noble provision﴾, meaning a good provision, namely Paradise.

﴿O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other of the women﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He means, your standing with Me is not like the standing of other righteous women. You are more honoured by Me, and your reward is greater with Me. He did not say "like one of," because *ahad* (any one) is general and suits the singular, the dual, the plural, the masculine and the feminine. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We make no distinction between any of His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 285], and He said: "So there is none of you who could keep him away" [al-Haqqah: 47].

﴿If you fear Allah﴾, and so obey Him, ﴿then do not be soft in speech﴾, meaning do not be gentle in speech to men, and do not soften your words, ﴿lest one in whose heart is a disease should be moved with desire﴾, meaning immorality and lust. It was also said it means hypocrisy. The meaning is: do not say a statement by which a hypocrite or an immoral man may find a way to hope for you.

A woman is recommended to be firm in her speech when addressing strangers, in order to cut off their desires.

﴿And speak a known word﴾, meaning, for the sake of the religion and Islam, plainly and clearly, without softness.
