﴿وَقَرْنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ﴾ The people of Medina and 'Asim read "وَقَرَنَ" with a fatha on the qaf. Others read it with a kasra. Whoever reads it with a fatha on the qaf, its meaning is "uqrarna," that is, "remain in your houses" (الْزَمْنَ بُيُوتَكُنَّ). This comes from their saying: "qarartu bil-makan aqarru qararan" (I stayed in the place). It is said: "qarartu aqarru" and "qarartu aqirru," and both are dialectal forms. The first "r," which is the middle radical of the verb, was dropped because of the heaviness of the doubled consonant, and its vowel was transferred to the qaf, as they say: "fi zalaltu, zaltu" (in "zalaltu," the "l" was dropped and its vowel moved to the preceding letter). Allah the Exalted says: ﴿فَظَلْتُمْ تَفَكَّهُونَ﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 65], and "﴿ظَلْتَ عَلَيْهِ عَاكِفًا﴾" [Ta-Ha: 97].

Whoever reads it with a kasra on the qaf, it is said that it comes from "qarartu aqarru," meaning "uqrarna" (with a kasra on the "r"). The first "r" was dropped and its vowel transferred to the qaf, as we have mentioned. It is also said, and this is the most correct view, that it is an imperative from "al-waqar" (dignity and tranquillity), like their saying from "al-wa'd" (promise): "idna" (ʿidna), and from "al-wasl" (joining): "silna" (ṣilna). That means: be people of dignity and calm, from their saying: "waqara fulan yaqiru wuquran" when a man became calm and settled.

﴿وَلَا تَبَرَّجْنَ﴾ Mujahid and Qatadah said: "at-tabarruj" is coquetry and affected softness of manner (التَّكَسُّرُ وَالتَّغَنُّجُ). Ibn Abi Najih said: it is strutting (التَّبَخْتُرُ). It is also said: it is displaying adornment and showing one's beauty to men. ﴿تَبَرُّجَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ الْأُولَى﴾ [They differed concerning "the first Jahiliyyah" (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance)]. [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "A".]]

Al-Sha'bi said: it is the period between Jesus and Muhammad (ﷺ). [[See: al-Tabari 22/4; al-Bahr al-Muhit 7/231.]]

Abu al-'Aliyah said: it was in the time of Dawud and Sulayman, peace be upon them. A woman would wear a shirt of pearls, unsewn at the sides, so that her body could be seen through it. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit 7/231.]]

Al-Kalbi said: that was in the time of Nimrod the tyrant. A woman would make a coat of pearls, wear it, walk in the middle of the road with nothing on her other than it, and present herself to men. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit 7/230.]]

It is related from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said: the first Jahiliyyah was between Nuh and Idris, and it lasted a thousand years. Two tribes of the descendants of Adam existed: one of them lived in the plain and the other lived in the mountain. The men of the mountain were handsome, but the women were plain. The women of the plain were handsome, but the men were plain. Iblis came to a man from the people of the plain and hired himself out to him, serving him. He made an instrument similar to what shepherds play, and he produced a sound the people had never heard the like of. This reached those around them, who came to them to listen. They made a festival which they gathered for once a year. The women displayed themselves to the men and the men adorned themselves for the women. A man from the people of the mountain attacked them during that festival, saw the women and their beauty, and went to his companions and told them about it. [So they moved to them] [[Addition from "B".]] and settled among them, and indecency spread among them. [[See: al-Tabari 22/4.]] This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿وَلَا تَبَرَّجْنَ تَبَرُّجَ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ الْأُولَى﴾.

Qatadah said: it is what came before Islam. [[See: al-Tabari 22/4-5; al-Durr al-Manthur 6/601.]]

It is also said: "al-Jahiliyyah al-Ula" (the first Jahiliyyah) is what we have mentioned, and "al-Jahiliyyah al-Ukhra" (the later Jahiliyyah) is a people who will do the like of their deeds at the end of time.

It is also said: the first may be mentioned even when there is no second, as in His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّهُ أَهْلَكَ عَادًا الْأُولَى﴾ [al-Najm: 50], though there was no second 'Ad.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿وَأَقِمْنَ الصَّلَاةَ وَآتِينَ الزَّكَاةَ وَأَطِعْنَ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ﴾. By "ar-rijs" (impurity) he meant the sin from which Allah forbade the women, as Muqatil said. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means the work of Satan and what does not please Allah. Qatadah said: it means evil. Mujahid said: ar-rijs is doubt.

By "Ahl al-Bayt" (the People of the House) he meant the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), because they are in his house. This is the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, and he recited His saying: ﴿وَاذْكُرْنَ مَا يُتْلَى فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Ahzab: 34]. This is also the view of 'Ikrimah and Muqatil.

Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and a group of the Successors (al-Tabi'un, the generation after the Companions), among them Mujahid, Qatadah and others, held that they are 'Ali, Fatimah, al-Hasan and al-Husayn. [[See: Zad al-Masir 6/381.]]

Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi told us: Abu Muhammad 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Ansari informed us: Abu Muhammad Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'idi informed us: Abu Hammam al-Walid ibn Shuja' informed us: Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Za'idah informed us: my father informed us, from Mus'ab ibn Shaybah, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah al-Hajabiyyah, from 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one morning wearing a black cloak of hair (mirt murahhal min sha'r aswad). He sat down, and Fatimah came, and he let her in under it. [Then 'Ali came, and he let him in under it.] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "A".]] Then al-Hasan came and he let him in under it, then al-Husayn came and he let him in under it. Then he said: ﴿إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمْ تَطْهِيرًا﴾. [[Narrated by Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter: The Virtue of the People of the House, no. 2424, 4/1883; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 14/116.]]

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Humaydi informed us: 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us: Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us: al-Hasan ibn Mukarram told us: 'Uthman ibn 'Umar informed us: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar told us, from Sharik ibn Abi Namir, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Umm Salamah, who said: It was revealed in my house: ﴿إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمُ الرِّجْسَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ﴾. She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Fatimah, 'Ali, al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and said: "These are my Ahl al-Bayt." I said: O Messenger of Allah, am I not one of the Ahl al-Bayt? He said: "Yes, if Allah wills." [[Narrated by al-Hakim 3/146, without the words (She said: I said: O Messenger of Allah, am I not one of the Ahl al-Bayt? He said: Yes, if Allah wills). It is in al-Musnad 6/492 by another route with similar wording, and its chain is weak. See also: Ibn Kathir 3/485-486; Sharh al-Sunnah 14/117. He (al-Hakim) said: this hadith has a sound chain.]]

Zayd ibn Arqam said: The Ahl al-Bayt of the Prophet (ﷺ) are those for whom charity is forbidden after him: the family of 'Ali, the family of 'Aqil, the family of Ja'far, and the family of 'Abbas. [[Narrated by Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter: On the virtues of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, no. 2408, 4/1873.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verses 34–35:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, words: ﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of Allah﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿and the wisdom﴾. Qatadah said: meaning the Sunnah. Muqatil said: the rulings of the Qur'an and its admonitions.

﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle, Acquainted﴾, meaning: Subtle toward His allies, Acquainted with all His creation.

His, the Mighty and Majestic, words: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women﴾, to the end of the verse. The reason for this is that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah mentions men in the Qur'an and does not mention women with goodness, so there is no good in us by which we are mentioned. We fear that Allah will not accept any obedience from us." So Allah revealed this verse [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 22/10, and its chain contains Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said of him in al-Taqrib: "in him is weakness" (fihi lin), and al-Suyuti added its attribution to al-Tabarani. See: Zad al-Masir: 6/383 with the editor's footnote; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/233.]].

Muqatil said: Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah and Nusaybah [[In "B": Unaysah.]] bint Ka'b al-Ansariyyah said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Why is it that our Lord mentions men and does not mention women in anything of His Book? We fear that there is no good in them?" So this verse was revealed [[See the narrations from Umm Salamah in al-Tabari: 22/10.]].

It is also narrated that Asma' bint Umays returned from Abyssinia with her husband Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. She entered upon the wives of the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Has anything of the Qur'an been revealed about us?" They said: "No." So she came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed women are in loss and ruin." He said: "And why is that?" She said: "Because they are not mentioned with goodness as men are mentioned." So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, and the believing men and believing women, and the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi, p. 413, and the author of Zad al-Masir: 6/384.]]﴾, meaning the obedient, ﴿and the truthful men and truthful women﴾, being truthful in their faith and in what grieves them and what pleases them, ﴿and the patient men and patient women﴾, patient in what Allah has commanded, ﴿and the humble men and humble women﴾, meaning the humble, ﴿and the charitable men and charitable women﴾ in what Allah has provided them, ﴿and the fasting men and fasting women, and the men and women who guard their chastity﴾ from what is not lawful, ﴿and the men and women who remember Allah often﴾. Mujahid said: A servant is not among those who remember Allah often until he remembers Allah standing, sitting, and lying on his side [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/609 to Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]].

We have also been related that the Prophet ﷺ said: "The mufarridun have gone ahead." They said: "And who are the mufarridun, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Those who remember Allah often, men and women" [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Remembrance, Supplication, Repentance and Seeking Forgiveness, chapter: Encouragement to the remembrance of Allah the Exalted, no. (2676), 4/2062.]].

Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: Whoever entrusts his affair to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is included in His saying: "Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women." Whoever testifies that Allah is his Lord and Muhammad is His Messenger, and whose heart does not contradict his tongue, is included in His saying: "and the believing men and believing women." Whoever obeys Allah in the obligatory duties and the Messenger in the Sunnah is included in His saying: "and the devoutly obedient men and devoutly obedient women." Whoever guards his speech from lying is included in His saying: "and the truthful men and truthful women." Whoever is patient in obedience, in refraining from disobedience, and in calamity, is included in His saying: "and the patient men and patient women." Whoever prays and does not know who is on his right and his left is included in His saying: "and the humble men and humble women." Whoever gives charity of a dirham every week is included in His saying: "and the charitable men and charitable women." Whoever fasts in every month the White Days: the thirteenth, the fourteenth, and the fifteenth, is included in His saying: "and the fasting men and fasting women." Whoever guards his chastity from what is not lawful is included in His saying: "and the men and women who guard their chastity." Whoever prays the five prayers with their rights is included in His saying: "and the men and women who remember Allah often."

﴿Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward﴾

**The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 33, verse 36:**

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair.﴾

The verse was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyya, her brother Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, and their mother Umayyah bint Abd al-Muttalib, the paternal aunt of the Prophet (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed marriage to Zaynab on behalf of his mawla (freedman, client) Zayd ibn Harithah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had bought Zayd in the Jahiliyyah at the market of Ukaz, then freed him and adopted him. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to Zaynab, she agreed, thinking that he was proposing to her for himself. When she learned that he was proposing her for Zayd, she refused and said: "I am the daughter of your paternal aunt, O Messenger of Allah, so I will not accept him for myself." She was fair, beautiful, and had a sharp temper. Her brother likewise disliked this. So Allah, may He be exalted and glorified, revealed: ﴿It is not for a believing man﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 22/11, and al-Wahidi mentioned it in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 610.]] meaning Abd Allah ibn Jahsh, ﴿or a believing woman﴾ meaning his sister Zaynab, ﴿when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter﴾, i.e., when Allah and His Messenger intend a matter, which is the marriage of Zaynab to Zayd, ﴿to have any choice in their affair.﴾

The people of Kufa read ﴿أَنْ يَكُونَ﴾ with a ya (yakuna, masculine verb form), because a separation intervenes between the feminine noun and the verb. The others read it with a ta (takuna), because al-Khiyarah (choice) is feminine. Al-Khiyarah means al-ikhtiyar (choosing).

The meaning is: that they should want something other than what Allah wants, or refrain from what Allah and His Messenger have commanded.

﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.﴾ He has erred with an evident error. When they heard this, they were content with it and submitted. Zaynab placed her affair in the hands of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and her brother did likewise. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her to Zayd. He consummated the marriage with her, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave her as mahr (bridal gift) ten dinars, sixty dirhams, a khimar (headscarf), a dir' (coat of mail or shirt), an izar (lower garment), a milhafa (wrap), fifty mudd (a unit of dry measure) of food, and thirty sa' (a unit of dry measure) of dates.

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 33, verse 37:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And [remember] when you said to him on whom Allah bestowed favour and you bestowed favour, "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah,"﴾ and the rest of the verse. It was revealed concerning Zaynab.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir, chapter: "And you hid within yourself that which Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him" (8/523).]] The reason is that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Zaynab to Zayd, she remained with him for a time. Then one day the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Zayd on some business and saw Zaynab standing, wearing a shift and a head-covering. She was fair, beautiful, and of the most perfect form among the women of Quraysh. She entered his heart and he was pleased by her beauty, so he said, "Glory be to Allah, Turner of hearts," and he departed. When Zayd came, she told him about this. Zayd perceived the matter, and his aversion to her was instilled in him at that moment.[[This narration, although many exegetes related it, has been rejected by the verifying scholars. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (8/524): "Other reports have come down, which Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabari narrated and many exegetes transmitted, and one should not occupy oneself with them. What I have cited is the one relied upon." This is a testimony of worth. He, may Allah have mercy on him, had earlier mentioned narrations on this subject and commented on them, saying: "Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this story through al-Suddi, presenting it in a clear and good form, with the wording: 'We have been told that this verse was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh. Her mother was Umayma bint Abd al-Muttalib, aunt of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to marry her to Zayd ibn Haritha, his freedman, but she disliked that. Then she agreed to what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arranged, so he married her to him. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed His Prophet (ﷺ) afterwards that she would be among his wives, so he was shy to order her divorce. Between Zayd and Zaynab there continued to be what occurs between people. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told him to keep his wife to himself and to fear Allah. He feared that people would criticize him and say, "He married his son's wife," for he had adopted Zayd.' And he has from the route of Ali ibn Zayd, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali, who said: 'Allah informed His Prophet (ﷺ) that Zaynab would be among his wives before he married her. When Zayd came to him complaining about her, he said to him: "Fear Allah and keep your wife to yourself." Allah said: "I had informed you that I would marry her to you," and "you hid within yourself that which Allah is to disclose."'" Then: Allah knows best, may Allah protect you: 1. The narrations on this story are weak in their chains. 2. They conflict with the infallibility (ʿisma) of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his station. 3. If what the prayer and peace of Allah be upon him concealed was his love for her, Allah would have disclosed it, as al-Baghawi mentioned, but Allah disclosed only that he would marry her. 4. It was he (ﷺ) who proposed her to Zayd ibn Haritha, and she was the daughter of his paternal aunt, and he had seen her since she was a child until she grew up. So how would love for her have entered his heart? And how could this love enter his heart after she became married to his freedman? If you wish to expand, consult: al-Shifa of Qadi Iyad (2/878–880); Hayat Muhammad by Muhammad Husayn Haykal (pp. 322–326); al-Isra'iliyyat wal-Mawdu'at fi Kutub al-Tafsir by Muhammad Abu Shahba (pp. 452–458); Ruh al-Ma'ani of al-Alusi (22/24–25); al-Bahr al-Muhit (7/234–235); Fi Zilal al-Qur'an (5/2865–2869); and Dr. Zahir Awad al-Alma'i's book: "Ma' al-Mufassirin wal-Mustashriqin fi Zawaj al-Nabi (ﷺ) bi-Zaynab bint Jahsh."]] So he came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "I want to separate from my companion." He said, "What is the matter with you? Has something about her made you doubt?" He said, "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I have seen nothing from her but good. But she exalts herself over me because of her nobility, and she harms me with her tongue." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, "Keep your wife to yourself," meaning Zaynab bint Jahsh, "and fear Allah" concerning her. Then Zayd divorced her.[[See al-Bahr al-Muhit (7/234).]] This is the meaning of His words, Mighty and Majestic:

﴿And [remember] when you said to him on whom Allah bestowed favour﴾ by Islam, ﴿and you bestowed favour﴾ by manumission, and he was Zayd ibn Haritha, ﴿"Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah"﴾ regarding her, and do not separate from her, ﴿and you hid within yourself that which Allah is to disclose﴾, that is, you concealed within yourself what Allah would make manifest. That is, there was in his heart that if he divorced her, he would marry her.

Ibn Abbas said: it was her love. Qatada said: he wished that he had divorced her.

﴿and you feared the people﴾. Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said: you felt shy before them.

It was also said: you feared the blame of the people, that they would say, "He ordered a man to divorce his wife and then married her."[[See Zad al-Masir (6/387).]]

﴿while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾. Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, and Aisha said: No verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that was harder for him than this verse.[[See al-Tabari (22/13), and see the following note.]]

It is related from Masruq, who said: Aisha said: "If the Prophet (ﷺ) had concealed anything of what was revealed to him, he would have concealed this verse: 'And you hid within yourself that which Allah is to disclose.'"[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the chapter on Surat al-Ahzab (9/71–72), who said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Also by al-Tabari (22/13). See also al-Bukhari in Tawhid, chapter: "And His Throne was upon the water" (13/404), but from Anas; and Muslim in Iman, chapter: "The meaning of Allah's words, 'He certainly saw him in another descent'; and did the Prophet (ﷺ) see his Lord on the night of the Isra'?" no. 177, (1/160).]]

Sufyan ibn Uyayna narrated from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin asked me what al-Hasan says about His words: "And you hid within yourself that which Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him." I said: He says that when Zayd came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Prophet of Allah, I want to divorce Zaynab," it pleased him, and he said, "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah." Ali ibn al-Husayn said: "It is not so. Allah had informed him that she would be among his wives and that Zayd would divorce her. When Zayd came and said, 'I want to divorce her,' he said to him, 'Keep your wife to yourself,' so Allah rebuked him and said: 'Why did you say, "Keep your wife to yourself," when I had informed you that she would be among your wives?'"[[See Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (3/492).]]

This is the more preferable and more fitting view for the state of the prophets, and it agrees with the recitation, because Allah knew that He would disclose and make manifest what he concealed, and He disclosed nothing but her marriage to him, so He said: "We married her to you." If what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concealed had been his love for her or his intention to divorce her, he would have disclosed that, because it is not permissible for Him to inform that He will make it manifest and then conceal it without making it manifest. This shows that he was rebuked only for concealing what Allah had informed him: that she would be his wife. He concealed it out of shame, lest he say to Zayd, "The one who is under you and in your marriage will be my wife." This is a good and acceptable view. Even if the other view, that he concealed his love for her or his marriage to her should he divorce her, is held, it does not detract from the state of the prophets, because a servant is not blamed for what arises in his heart regarding such matters, so long as he does not intend sin, since affection and the inclination of the soul are part of human nature.

His words: ﴿"Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah"﴾ are a command to what is right, and it is a fear that carries no sin.

His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ do not mean that he did not fear Allah previously, for he (peace be upon him) said: "I am the most fearful of you of Allah and the most mindful of Him." Rather, when he mentioned fear of the people, He mentioned that Allah has more right to be feared in all circumstances and all matters.

His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So when Zayd had no further need of her﴾, that is, no longer had a need of her in marriage, ﴿We married her to you﴾. He mentioned "had no further need" so that it would be known that the wife of the adopted son becomes lawful after consummation.

Anas said: Zaynab used to boast over the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), saying: "Your families married you off, but Allah married me from above the seven heavens."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tawhid, chapter: "And His Throne was upon the water" (13/403–404).]]

Al-Sha'bi said: Zaynab used to say to the Prophet (ﷺ): "I take pride in three things over which none of your wives can boast: my grandfather and your grandfather are one; Allah married me to you in the heavens; and the envoy was Gabriel (peace be upon him)."[[Narrated by al-Tabari (22/14). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath (13/412): al-Tabari and Abu al-Qasim al-Tahawi in Kitab al-Hujja wal-Tibyan narrated it from the mursal report of al-Sha'bi.]]

Ismail ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Muhammad informed us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us, Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us: Muhammad ibn Hatim ibn Maymun narrated to me, Bahz informed us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughira informed us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: When the waiting period of Zaynab ended, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Zayd, "Mention her to me." He said: So Zayd went until he came to her, and she was kneading her dough. He said: When I saw her, she became great in my chest, so that I could not look at her, because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had mentioned her. So I turned my back to her and retreated backwards, and I said: "O Zaynab, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has sent to mention you."

She said: "I will do nothing until I consult my Lord." She stood up to her place of prayer, and the Qur'an was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and entered upon her without permission.

He said: "We saw that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fed us bread and meat until the day extended, [so the people went out] [[Omitted in manuscript 'A'.]] and some men remained talking in the house after the meal. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, and I followed him. He began to go around the apartments of his wives, greeting them, and they said, 'O Messenger of Allah, how did you find your family?' He said: I do not know whether I informed him that the people had left, or he informed me."

He said: So he went until he entered the house, and I went to enter with him, but he let the curtain fall between me and him, and the veil was revealed.[[Narrated by Muslim in Nikah, chapter: "The marriage of Zaynab bint Jahsh and the revelation of the veil," no. 1428 (2/1048).]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Sulayman ibn Harb informed us, Hammad informed us, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) never gave a wedding feast for any of his wives as he gave for Zaynab; he held a feast with a sheep.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Nikah, chapter: "The wedding feast with a sheep" (9/232); Muslim in Nikah, chapter: "The marriage of Zaynab bint Jahsh and the revelation of the veil," no. 1428 (2/1049); and the author in Sharh al-Sunna (9/137).]]

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us, Muhammad ibn Hisham ibn Mulas al-Namari informed us, Marwan al-Fazari informed us, Humayd informed us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) held a wedding feast when he consummated his marriage with Zaynab bint Jahsh, and he fed the Muslims bread and meat.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir (Surat al-Ahzab) (8/528), and the author in Sharh al-Sunna (9/137).]]

His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿so that there may be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when those adopted sons have no further need of them﴾, that is, no sin, and "al-Ad'iya" (the adopted sons) is the plural of "al-Da'iy," which means the adopted son. He says: "We married you to Zaynab, and she was the wife of Zayd, whom you adopted," so that it would be known that the wife of an adopted son is lawful for the one who adopted him, [even if the adopted son had consummated the marriage with her] [[What is between the brackets is omitted in manuscript 'A'.]], unlike the wife of a biological son, who is not lawful for the father.

﴿And the command of Allah is always executed﴾, that is, the decree of Allah is enacted and His ruling is effective, and He had decreed concerning Zaynab that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would marry her.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿There is no blame upon the Prophet concerning that which Allah has ordained for him﴾, i.e., concerning that which Allah has made lawful for him. ﴿The way of Allah﴾, i.e., like the way of Allah, [it is] in the accusative by removal of the preposition. It was also said that it is in the accusative as an incitement (al-ighra'), meaning: adhere to the way of Allah. ﴿Among those who passed away before﴾, i.e., among the earlier prophets, that He would not hold them to account for what He had made lawful for them.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: He meant Dawud (David), when he combined between himself and the woman he desired; likewise, He combined between Muhammad ﷺ and Zaynab.

It was also said: by "the way" He referred to marriage, for it is from the way of the prophets, peace be upon them.

It was also said: [He referred] to the multiplicity of wives, like Dawud and Sulayman, peace be upon them both. [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit (The Surrounding Sea), 7/235-236, where it is stated that the Jews criticized him, i.e., the Prophet ﷺ, for his many marriages and multiplicity of wives, so Allah refuted them by His saying: "the way of Allah."]]

﴿And the command of Allah is a decree decreed﴾, i.e., a determined judgment, existing and past.

﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah﴾ [meaning: the way of Allah concerning the prophets, those who convey the messages of Allah]. [[The text between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]] ﴿and fear Him, and fear no one except Allah﴾: they do not fear the talk of people or their blame concerning what Allah has made lawful for them and enjoined upon them. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾: Guardian of the deeds of His creatures and their Reckoner.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Zaynab, the people said: "Muhammad has married his son's wife." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾ [[See al-Tabari: 22/16.]], meaning Zayd ibn Harithah. That is, he is not the father of any of your men whom he did not beget, so that marriage to his wife would be forbidden to him after she had been divorced from him.

If it is said: Did he not have sons: al-Qasim, al-Tayyib, al-Tahir, and Ibrahim? And likewise al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said of al-Hasan: "This son of mine is a master"?

It is said: These were children; they had not yet become men.

The correct view is what we have said: he intended "the father of any one of your men" [[See: Masa'il al-Razi wa Ajwibatuha min Gharaib Ayat al-Tanzil, p. 282.]].

﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾: Allah sealed prophethood with him. Asim read "khatam" with a fatha on the ta', as a noun, meaning the last of them. The others read it with a kasra on the ta', as an active participle, because he sealed the prophets with himself, so he is their seal.

Ibn Abbas said: He means: if I had not sealed the prophets with him, I would have made for him a son who would be a prophet after him [[See: Zad al-Masir: 6/393.]].

It is related from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, that when Allah decreed that there would be no prophet after him, He did not give him a male child who would reach manhood. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni informed us: Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad al-Khudhashahi informed us: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us: Abkar al-Jurbadhi informed us: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Yazid, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah, who said: Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My example and the example of the prophets is like a palace whose building was made beautiful, except that a place for one brick was left. People went around it, marveling at the beauty of its construction, but they were not pleased except with the place of that brick. I filled the place of that brick. The building was sealed with me, and the messengers were sealed with me." [[Related by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/201. Al-Bukhari (6/558) related from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My example and the example of the prophets before me is like a man who built a house, made it beautiful and perfect, except for the place of one brick in a corner. People began to go around it, marveling at it and saying: 'Why was this brick not placed?' He said: 'I am the brick, and I am the Seal of the Prophets.'" Muslim (4/1719) related from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My example and the example of the prophets before me is like a man who built a building, made it beautiful and perfect, except for the place of one brick in one of its corners. People went around it, marveling at it and saying: 'Why was this brick not placed?' He said: 'I am the brick, and I am the Seal of the Prophets.'"]]

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Samad al-Jawzajani informed us: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Khuza'i informed us: al-Haytham ibn Kulayb al-Shashi informed us: Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Makhzumi, and more than one other, said: Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser), by whom Allah erases disbelief; I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer), at whose feet people will be gathered; I am al-'Aqib (the Last), and al-'Aqib is the one after whom there is no prophet." [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in al-Adab, chapter: What has come concerning the names of the Prophet (ﷺ): 8/128-130, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Al-Bukhari related it in al-Manaqib, chapter: What has come concerning the names of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): 6/554, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/211.]]

﴿Those who convey the messages of Allah﴾ [meaning: the way of Allah concerning the prophets, those who convey the messages of Allah]. [[The text between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "b".]] ﴿and fear Him, and fear no one except Allah﴾: they do not fear the talk of people or their blame concerning what Allah has made lawful for them and enjoined upon them. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾: Guardian of the deeds of His creatures and their Reckoner.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 41:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah, exalted is He, did not prescribe any obligation (fari'ah) without setting for it a known limit, then He excused its people in cases of excuse, except for dhikr (remembrance of Allah), for He did not set for it a limit at which it ends, and He did not excuse anyone from abandoning it except one whose intellect has been overcome [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 22/17, and Ibn Kathir: 3/496.]] and He commanded them to it in all circumstances, saying: "So remember Allah standing, sitting, and on your sides" [al-Nisa: 103]. And He said: ﴿Remember Allah with much remembrance﴾, that is: by night and by day, on land and at sea, in health and in sickness, and in secret and in public. Mujahid said: Much remembrance is that you do not forget Him at all.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 42–44:

﴿And glorify Him﴾ i.e., pray to Him, ﴿at dawn and in the afternoon﴾ meaning: the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ) and the afternoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr). Al-Kalbi said: "wa-aṣīlan" refers to the noon prayer (ṣalāt al-ẓuhr), the afternoon prayer (ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr), and the two night prayers (al-ʿishāʾayn).

Mujahid said: it means: say "Subḥān Allāh" (Glory be to God), "al-Ḥamdu lillāh" (Praise be to God), "Lā ilāha illā Allāh" (There is no god but God), "Allāhu akbar" (God is greatest), and "Lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-Llāh" (There is no power and no strength except through God). Thus he used tasbīh to express its counterparts.

It is also said: what is meant by His words "much remembrance" (dhikran kathīran) are these words, which the one in a state of purity, the one in major impurity (junub), and the one in minor impurity (muḥdith) may say. [[See: al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ: 7 / 237; Zād al-Masīr: 6 / 397-398.]]

﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels﴾. So the blessing (ṣalāh) from God is mercy, and from the angels it is seeking forgiveness for the believers.

Al-Suddi said: The Children of Israel said to Musa: "Does our Lord pray?" This statement weighed heavily on Musa, so God revealed to him: "Tell them: I do pray, and My prayer is My mercy, and My mercy has encompassed everything." [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6 / 622.]]

It is also said: the blessing of God upon the servant is the spreading of a good remembrance of him among His servants. It is also said: it is praise of him.

Anas said: When the verse "Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet" was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of God, God has not honoured you with any dignity except that He has given us a share in it." So God revealed this verse. [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6 / 622 to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

His words: ﴿to bring you out from darkness into light﴾ i.e., from the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith, meaning: by His mercy, His guidance, and the angels' supplication for you, He brought you out from the darkness of disbelief into the light, ﴿and He is ever merciful to the believers﴾. ﴿Their greeting﴾ i.e., the greeting of the believers, ﴿on the day they meet Him﴾ i.e., they see God, ﴿will be "Peace"﴾ i.e., God will greet them with peace, and will keep them safe from all calamities.

It is reported from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib that he said: "Their greeting on the day they meet Him" means: they meet the Angel of Death, who does not seize the soul of a believer without greeting him with peace.  [[Narrated by al-Hakim: 2 / 351-352, who said: "Authentic." I (al-Dhahabi) say: ʿAbdullah, Ibn ʿAdi said: "his hadith is obscure"; and Muhammad, Ibn Hibban said: "he is not to be used as evidence." Al-Suyuti also cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6 / 623 to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman.]]

And it is reported from Ibn Masʿud that he said: When the Angel of Death comes to seize the soul of the believer, he says: "Your Lord sends you His greetings of peace." [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6 / 623 to al-Marwazi in al-Janaʾiz, Ibn Abi al-Dunya and Abu al-Shaykh; also mentioned by the author of al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ: 7 / 237.]]

It is also said: the angels will greet them and give them glad tidings when they come forth from their graves. [[See: al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ: 7 / 237.]] ﴿And He has prepared for them a generous reward﴾, i.e., Paradise.

His words: ﴿to bring you out from darkness into light﴾ i.e., from the darkness of disbelief into the light of faith, meaning: by His mercy, His guidance, and the angels' supplication for you, He brought you out from the darkness of disbelief into the light, ﴿and He is ever merciful to the believers﴾. ﴿Their greeting﴾ i.e., the greeting of the believers, ﴿on the day they meet Him﴾ i.e., they see God, ﴿will be "Peace"﴾ i.e., God will greet them with peace, and will keep them safe from all calamities.

It is reported from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib that he said: "Their greeting on the day they meet Him" means: they meet the Angel of Death, who does not seize the soul of a believer without greeting him with peace.  [[Narrated by al-Hakim: 2 / 351-352, who said: "Authentic." I (al-Dhahabi) say: ʿAbdullah, Ibn ʿAdi said: "his hadith is obscure"; and Muhammad, Ibn Hibban said: "he is not to be used as evidence." Al-Suyuti also cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6 / 623 to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman.]]

And it is reported from Ibn Masʿud that he said: When the Angel of Death comes to seize the soul of the believer, he says: "Your Lord sends you His greetings of peace." [[Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6 / 623 to al-Marwazi in al-Janaʾiz, Ibn Abi al-Dunya and Abu al-Shaykh; also mentioned by the author of al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ: 7 / 237.]]

It is also said: the angels will greet them and give them glad tidings when they come forth from their graves. [[See: al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ: 7 / 237.]] ﴿And He has prepared for them a generous reward﴾, i.e., Paradise.

**Allah the Exalted said:** ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner﴾. That is, a witness to the messengers that they conveyed (the message), a bringer of good news to those who believe of Paradise, and a warner to those who deny Our signs of the Fire.

﴿And as one who calls to Allah﴾ to His oneness and obedience, ﴿by His permission﴾ by His command, ﴿and as a shining lamp﴾. He called him a lamp because he is guided by him, just as a lamp is used for light in darkness.

﴿And give good news to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾.

﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾. We have mentioned its explanation at the beginning of the surah. ﴿And disregard their harm﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: be patient with their harm. Al-Zajjaj said: do not repay them for it. This verse is abrogated (mansukh) by the verse of fighting. [83/b]

﴿And put your trust in Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾, meaning as Guardian.

**Allah the Exalted said:** ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾. In this is evidence that a divorce before marriage does not take effect, because Allah the Exalted linked divorce to marriage. So even if a man says to a non-related woman, "If I marry you, you are divorced," or says, "Every woman I marry is divorced," and then he marries her, the divorce does not take effect. This is the view of 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Jabir, Mu'adh, and 'A'ishah, and it is the position of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Urwah, Shurayh, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Qasim, Tawus, al-Hasan, 'Ikrimah, 'Ata', Sulayman ibn Yasar, Mujahid, al-Sha'bi, Qatadah, and most of the people of knowledge, may Allah be pleased with them all. It is also the view of al-Shafi'i.

It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that the divorce does take effect. This is the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and the Ashab al-Ra'y (the People of Opinion, i.e., the Hanafis).

Rabi'ah, Malik, and al-Awza'i said: if he specifies a particular woman, it takes effect; if he generalizes, it does not take effect.

'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "They lied about Ibn Mas'ud. If he said it, it was a slip by a scholar regarding a man who says, 'If I marry so-and-so, she is divorced.' Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when you marry believing women and then divorce them﴾, and He did not say, 'When you divorce them and then marry them.'"[[See: Ahkam al-Qur'an by al-Jassas: 5/232–236.]]

Therefore the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not thoroughly search for these sound chains, and Allah knows best. The hadith has other routes from a number of Companions which strengthen it. See its detailed takhrij in: Nasb al-Rayah: 3/230–233; Talkhis al-Habir: 3/210–212; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 6/173–174 and 7/152–153.]]

**His saying, may He be exalted:** ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whose bridal payments (ujur) you have given﴾, meaning their dowries (muhur). ﴿And those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has granted you as spoils﴾, that is, what Allah returned to you from the disbelievers by way of captives, so that you own the like of Safiyyah and Juwayriyyah. Maria was among those whom his right hand possessed, and she bore him Ibrahim. ﴿And the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts﴾, meaning the women of Quraysh. ﴿And the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts﴾, meaning the women of Banu Zuhrah. ﴿Who migrated with you﴾ to Madinah. So whoever of them did not migrate with him, it is not permissible for him to marry her.

Abu Salih narrated from Umm Hani that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, he proposed to me, and Allah revealed this verse. I was not lawful to him, because I had not been among the emigrant women, and I was among the Tulaqa' (those freed at the conquest). Then the condition of migration in the permission was abrogated (naskh, abrogation).[1]

﴿And a believing woman, if she gives herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to marry her, exclusively for you, not for the believers﴾. That is: We have made lawful for you a believing woman who gives herself to you without a dowry. As for a woman who is not a believer, she is not lawful to him if she gives herself to him.

The scholars differed over whether it was lawful for the Prophet (ﷺ) to marry a Jewish or Christian woman with a dowry.

A group held that it was not lawful for him to do so, based on His saying: "and a believing woman." Some of them interpreted the migration in His saying "who migrated with you" as referring to Islam, meaning: who embraced Islam with you. This indicates that it was not lawful for him to marry a non-Muslim woman. The marriage contract was valid in his case by way of gift (hibah), without a guardian (wali), without witnesses, and without a dowry. This was among his special privileges (khasa'is) in marriage, based on His saying: ﴿exclusively for you, not for the believers﴾, as with the allowance of more than four wives, and the obligation to give wives the choice, which was among his privileges with no one sharing it with him.

The scholars differed over whether a marriage is concluded with the wording of gift for the ordinary believers. Most of them held that it is concluded only with the wording of marriage (inkah) and wedlock (tazwij). This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, al-Zuhri, Mujahid, and 'Ata', and it was also the position of Rabi'ah, Malik, and al-Shafi'i.

Others held that it is concluded with the wording of gift and of transfer of ownership (tamlik). This is the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and the people of Kufah.

Those who say it is concluded only with the wording of inkah or tazwij differed regarding the marriage of the Prophet (ﷺ). A group held that it was concluded with the wording of gift, based on His saying: ﴿exclusively for you, not for the believers﴾.

Others held that it is concluded only with the wording of inkah or tazwij, as in the case of ordinary believers, based on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿if the Prophet wishes to marry her﴾. His privilege lay in waiving the dowry, not in the wording of the marriage contract.[2]

They differed concerning the woman who gave herself to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and whether any of his wives was of that kind.

Abdullah ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: no woman who gave herself to the Prophet (ﷺ) was ever among his wives; he had no wife except through a marriage contract or by right of ownership (milk al-yamin). [And His saying: ﴿if she gives herself﴾ is in the form of a conditional and its consequent.]

Others said: rather, there was a woman who was given to him as a gift, and they differed about her identity. Al-Sha'bi said: she was Zaynab bint Khuzaymah al-Hilaliyyah, who was called Umm al-Masakin.

Qatadah said: she was Maymunah bint al-Harith.

Ali ibn al-Husayn, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil said: she was Umm Sharik bint Jabir of Banu Asad.

Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: she was Khawlah bint Hakim of Banu Sulaym.[3]

**His saying, may He be exalted:** ﴿We have indeed known what We have enjoined upon them﴾, that is, what We have made obligatory upon the believers, ﴿concerning their wives﴾ of the rulings: that they should not marry more than four, and that they should marry only with a guardian (wali), witnesses, and a dowry (mahr). ﴿And what their right hands possess﴾, that is, what We have made obligatory among the rulings concerning ownership by right hand. ﴿So that there will be no discomfort upon you﴾. This refers back to the beginning of the verse, meaning: We have made lawful for you your wives, what your right hand possesses, and the woman given to you as a gift, so that there would be no hardship or constraint upon you.

﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

[1] Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, 9/74–76, who said: "This is a good hadith; we do not know it except through this route, from the hadith of al-Suddi." Also by al-Tabari, 22/20–21; authenticated by al-Hakim, 2/420, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him; and by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan, 7/54. Al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur, 6/628, added its attribution to Ibn Sa'd, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Rahawayh, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh.

[2] See: Ahkam al-Quran by al-Jassas, 5/236–238.

[3] See: Ahkam al-Quran by al-Jassas, 5/239.

﴿Turji﴾ means: you postpone (or defer), ﴿whom you will of them﴾, ﴿and you take into your presence whom you will﴾ means: you admit (or house) to yourself whom you will.

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of the verse. The most well-known opinion is that it concerns the division of nights among them (al-qasm). The equal treatment among them in the division was obligatory upon him, but when this verse was revealed, that obligation was lifted from him, and the choice regarding them became his.

Abu Razin and Ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed when some of the Mothers of the Believers became jealous of the Prophet ﷺ and some of them requested an increase in maintenance. So the Prophet ﷺ abandoned them for a month, until the verse of choice (ayat al-takhyir) was revealed. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to give them the choice between the world and the Hereafter, and that he release whoever chose the world and keep whoever chose Allah, His Messenger, and the Last Abode. (This was) on the condition that they remain Mothers of the Believers and never marry again, and on the condition that he may take into his presence whom he wills of them and defer whom he wills, so that they are content with him whether he divides (equally) among them or does not divide, or divides for some of them and not others, or favours some of them in maintenance and division. The matter in this is his, and he does as he wishes. This was among his special privileges (khasa'is). So they agreed to this and chose him on this condition. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 413, attributing it to the exegetes.]]

They differed as to whether he excluded any of them from the division. Some said: He did not exclude anyone; rather, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ—despite what Allah had granted him in this regard—continued to treat them equally in the division, except Sawda, who was content to forgo her right to the division and made her day for ʿA'isha.

It was said: He excluded some of them.

Jarir narrated from Mansur, from Abu Razin, who said: When the verse of choice was revealed, they feared that he would divorce them, so they said: "O Prophet of Allah, grant us from your wealth and yourself whatever you wish, and leave us in our state." Then this verse was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ deferred some of them and took others into his presence. Among those he took into his presence were ʿA'isha, Hafsa, Zaynab, and Umm Salama, and he divided equally among them. He deferred five of them: Umm Habiba, Maymuna, Sawda, Safiyya and Juwayriyya, and he divided for them as he wished. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 22/26, and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 414.]]

Mujahid said: "You defer whom you will of them" means: you set aside whom you will of them without divorce, and you return to yourself whom you will after setting aside, without renewing the contract.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: You divorce whom you will of them and keep whom you will.

al-Hasan said: You leave off marrying whom you will and marry whom you will from among the women of your community.

He also said: When the Prophet ﷺ proposed to a woman, no one else could propose to her until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ left her.

It was also said: You accept whom you will of the believing women who offer themselves to you, taking her to yourself, and you leave whom you will, not accepting her.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muhammad ibn Salam informed us, Ibn Fudayl informed us, Hisham informed us, from his father, who said: Khawla bint Hakim was among those women who offered themselves to the Prophet ﷺ. ʿA'isha said: "Is a woman not ashamed to offer herself to a man?" Then when the verse was revealed: ﴿You defer whom you will of them﴾, I said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see your Lord only hastening to fulfil your desire." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Nikah, chapter: Can a woman give herself to someone, 9/164; and Muslim in Radaʿ, chapter: The permissibility of a woman giving up her turn to her co-wife, no. 1464, 2/1085-1086.]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And whomever you seek of those you have set aside﴾ means: whom you desire and wish to take to yourself from those you have set aside from the division, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, meaning no sin upon you. Allah permitted him to leave off the division among them, to the extent that he would defer whom he wills of them in her turn and be intimate with whom he wills of them outside her turn, and return to his bed whoever he had set aside, as a preference for him over all other men. ﴿That is more suitable that their eyes be comforted and they not grieve﴾, meaning: the choice I have given you regarding their companionship is closer to their contentment, more pleasing to their souls, and less likely to grieve them when they know that this is from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And they will be pleased with what you give them, all of them﴾, meaning given to them, of deferment, setting aside, and taking in. ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ concerning the matter of women and inclination toward some of them. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing, Forbearing﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 52:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry] women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives﴾. Abu 'Amr and Ya'qub read "lā taḥillu" with a ta' (feminine), while the others read it with a ya' (masculine). "After this" means: after these nine [wives] whom you gave the choice, and they chose you. That is because when the Prophet (ﷺ) gave them the choice and they chose Allah and His Messenger, Allah thanked them for that and forbade him women other than them, and forbade him to divorce them or to exchange them for others. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah [[See Fath al-Bari: 8 / 526.]].

They differed over whether women were made lawful for him after this.

'A'ishah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until women other than them were made lawful for him [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir: 9 / 78-79, who said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Also by al-Nasa'i in al-Nikah, chapter: What Allah the Mighty and Majestic made obligatory upon His Messenger and forbade to His creation: 6 / 56; al-Darimi in al-Nikah, chapter on the saying of Allah the Exalted: "It is not lawful for you women after this": 2 / 153; Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Dham'an, no. (2126), p. (523); al-Hakim authenticated it: 2 / 437 and al-Dhahabi agreed; al-Bayhaqi: 7 / 54; and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 6 / 41, 180. See also: Fath al-Bari 8 / 526; al-Talkhis al-Habir: 3 / 123.]].

Anas said: He died upon the prohibition.

'Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: The meaning of the verse is: "It is not lawful for you women except those whom We have made lawful for you," which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives﴾ [the verse], then He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this﴾, except those whom We made lawful for you by the description mentioned earlier.

It was said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: If the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) died, would it have been lawful for him to marry? He said: What would prevent him from that? It was said: His saying, exalted is He: "It is not lawful for you women after this." He said: Allah only made lawful for him a kind of women, when He said: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives﴾, then He said: ﴿It is not lawful for you women after this﴾.

Abu Salih said: He was commanded not to marry a Bedouin woman or an Arab woman, and he might marry, if he wished, from the women of his own people, from the daughters of his paternal uncles, paternal aunts, maternal uncles and maternal aunts, three hundred [women].

Mujahid said: Its meaning is: the Jewish women and the Christian women are not lawful for you after the Muslim women, nor to exchange them [the Muslim women] for others. He means: you may not exchange the Muslim women for other women from the Jews and the Christians. He says: the Mother of the Believers may not be a Jewish or a Christian woman. ﴿Except what your right hand possesses﴾: Allah made lawful for him what his right hand possessed of the scripturaries (kitabiyyat), that he might take them as concubines.

It is related from al-Dahhak: that is, "nor to exchange them for other wives, nor to exchange your wives who are in your presence for other wives, by divorcing them and marrying others." So He forbade him to divorce the women who were with him, since He made them the Mothers of the Believers, and forbade them to others once they chose him. As for marrying other women, he was not prevented from it.

Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾: The Arabs in the Jahiliyyah used to exchange their wives with one another. A man would say to another man: "Swap with me your wife, and I will swap mine with you; you give me your wife and I give you my wife." So Allah revealed: ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾, meaning: you may not exchange your wives with another man by giving him your wife and taking his wife [[Al-Tabari mentioned these sayings: 22 / 29-33, with preferences to be consulted.]]. ﴿Except what your right hand possesses﴾: there is no harm in exchanging your slave-women for whatever you wish; as for free women, no.

It is related from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: 'Uyaynah ibn Hisn entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) without permission, while 'A'ishah was with him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "O 'Uyaynah, where is the seeking of permission?" He said: O Messenger of Allah, I have not sought permission from a man of Mudar since I reached maturity. Then he said: "Who is this red-cheeked one beside you?" He said: This is 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers. 'Uyaynah said: Shall I not divorce for you the best of creation? The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has forbidden that." When he left, 'A'ishah said: Who is this, O Messenger of Allah? He said: "This is a foolish, compliant man, and he is, as you see, the chief of his people." [[Narrated by al-Daraqutni in al-Nikah: 3 / 218-219; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6 / 638 attributed it to al-Bazzar and Ibn Mardawayh. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma': 7 / 92: "Narrated by al-Bazzar, and in its chain is Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Farwah, who is matruk (abandoned)." Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: "The hadith of Abu Hurayrah concerning nikah al-badal is very weak."]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Although her beauty pleases you﴾: that is, you may not divorce any of your wives and marry another in her place, even if her beauty pleases you.

Ibn 'Abbas said: That refers to Asma' bint 'Umays al-Khath'amiyyah, the wife of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib. When Ja'far was martyred, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to propose to her, but he was forbidden from that [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7 / 244.]].

﴿Except what your right hand possesses﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: After these, he possessed Mariyah.

﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, Watchful﴾: Hafiz (Guardian).

In the verse there is evidence for the permissibility of looking at a woman whom one wishes to marry. It is related from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you proposes to a woman, if he is able to look at what will draw him to marrying her, let him do so" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Nikah, chapter: A man looking at a woman when he intends to marry her: 3 / 25-26; al-Tahawi in Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar: 2 / 8; al-Bayhaqi: 7 / 84; al-Hakim: 2 / 165, who said: "Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it"; Imam Ahmad: 3 / 334; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9 / 17. See also: Nasb al-Rayah: 241; al-Talkhis al-Habir: 3 / 147; Irwa' al-Ghalil: 6 / 200.]].

Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni informed us; Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Sharik al-Shafi'i informed us; 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us; Abu Bakr al-Jurbadhi said: Ahmad ibn Harb informed us; Abu Mu'awiyah informed us, from 'Asim, that is Ibn Sulayman, from Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: I proposed to a woman, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Did you look at her?" I said: No. He said: "Then look at her, for it is more likely to create harmony between you two" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Nikah, chapter: What has come concerning looking at the woman to be proposed to: 4 / 206, who said: "This is a hasan hadith"; al-Nasa'i in al-Nikah, chapter: Permission to look before marriage: 6 / 69-70; Ibn Majah in al-Nikah, chapter: Looking at a woman when one wishes to marry her: 1 / 600, and Ibn Hibban authenticated it in Mawarid al-Dham'an, no. (1236), p. 303; al-Hakim: 2 / 165 on the condition of the two Shaykhs, and al-Dhahabi agreed; Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 4 / 355; al-Darimi in al-Nikah, chapter: Looking at the woman at the time of proposal: 2 / 59; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 7 / 84-85; Imam Ahmad: 4 / 246; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 9 / 17. See also: al-Talkhis al-Habir: 3 / 146-252; Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah no. (96): 1 / 150-152.]].

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us; Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us; Bishr ibn Musa informed us; al-Humaydi informed us; Yazid ibn Kaysan informed us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man wished to marry a woman from the Ansar, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Look at her, for there is something in the eyes of the women of the Ansar" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Nikah, chapter: Looking at the face and hands of a woman by one who wishes to marry her, no. (1424): 2 / 1040.]]. Al-Humaydi said: meaning, the smallness (of their eyes).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 53:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you﴾ and so on. Most of the exegetes said: this verse was revealed concerning the wedding feast (walima) of Zaynab bint Jahsh, when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ consummated the marriage with her.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Yahya ibn Bukayr informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Anas ibn Malik informed me that he was ten years old when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Madina. He said: Umm Hani used to urge me to serve the Prophet ﷺ, so I served him for ten years. The Prophet ﷺ died when I was twenty years old, and I was the most knowledgeable of people about the matter of the hijab when it was revealed. The first thing revealed about it was at the building of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with Zaynab bint Jahsh. The Prophet ﷺ had become a bridegroom with her, so he invited the people, and they ate the food and then left, but a group of them remained with the Prophet ﷺ and prolonged their stay. The Prophet ﷺ stood up and went out, and I went out with him so that they would leave. The Prophet ﷺ walked and I walked until he came to the room of Aisha. Then he thought they had left, so he returned and I returned with him, until when he entered upon Zaynab, behold, they were sitting and had not left. So the Prophet ﷺ returned, and I returned with him, until when he reached the threshold of Aisha's room and thought they had left, he returned and I returned with him, and behold, they had left. Then the Prophet ﷺ placed the curtain between me and him, and the hijab was revealed.

Abu Uthman, whose name is al-Ja'd, said, from Anas: He (meaning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ) entered the house and let down the curtain while I was in the room, and he was reciting: ﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you﴾ up to his saying: ﴿And Allah is not ashamed of the truth﴾.

It is related from Ibn Abbas that it was revealed concerning some of the Muslims who would watch for the Messenger of Allah's ﷺ food, entering upon him before the meal was ready, then eating and not leaving. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would be troubled by them, so it was revealed.

﴿O you who believe, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you﴾ means: unless you are invited, ﴿to a meal﴾, and then permission is given to you and you eat it, ﴿not waiting for its preparation﴾, meaning not waiting for it to be cooked and reach its time of readiness. It is said: "anā al-ḥamīm" when its heat has reached its end, and "ināʾ" (إِنَى) means it has become due, with the hamza kasra and shortened; when you open it you lengthen it and say "al-inā'" (الإِنَاءُ). There are two dialects: inā yaʾnā and ān yaīnu, like ḥān yaḥīnu.

﴿But when you are invited, enter, and when you have eaten﴾, meaning, when you have eaten the food, ﴿disperse﴾, meaning scatter and leave his house, ﴿and do not linger for conversation﴾, meaning do not seek companionable talk. They used to sit after the meal talking at length, so they were forbidden from this.

﴿Indeed, that was troubling to the Prophet, and he is shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth﴾, meaning He does not abandon disciplining you and making the truth clear out of shyness.

﴿And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾, meaning from behind a curtain. After the verse of hijab, it was not permitted for anyone to look at a woman of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whether she was veiled or unveiled. ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾ from doubt.

Concerning the occasion of revelation of the verse of hijab, there is what Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Yahya ibn Bukayr informed us: al-Layth informed us, "Uqayl narrated to me," from Ibn Shihab, from Urwa, from Aisha, that the wives of the Prophet ﷺ used to go out at night when they relieved themselves, to al-Manasi', which is a wide open area. Umar used to say to the Prophet ﷺ: "Veil your wives," but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not do so. Then Sawda bint Zam'a, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, went out one night after the evening prayer, and she was a tall woman. Umar called out to her: "Surely we have recognised you, O Sawda," eager that the hijab be revealed. So Allah the Exalted revealed the verse of hijab.

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: Abd al-Rahim ibn Munib informed us: Yazid ibn Harun informed us: Humayd informed us, from Anas, who said: Umar said: "My Lord agreed with me in three matters. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, if only you took the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer?' So Allah revealed: 'And take the Station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer.' And I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the righteous and the wicked enter upon you, so if only you commanded the Mothers of the Believers to observe hijab?' So Allah revealed the verse of hijab." He said: "And some of what the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had done to hurt him reached me. I entered upon them and admonished them one by one. I said: 'By Allah, either you will desist, or Allah will surely replace him with wives better than you,' until I came to Zaynab, and she said: 'O Umar, was there not in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what would admonish his wives, that you should admonish them?' So I left, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: 'It may be that if he divorces you, his Lord will substitute for him wives better than you' [al-Tahrim: 5], to the end of the verse."

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after him, ever﴾. It means: it is not for you to harm him in anything at all. It was revealed concerning a man from among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ who said: "If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dies, I will surely marry Aisha."

Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: he was Talha ibn Ubayd Allah, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic informed him that this was forbidden, and said: ﴿Indeed, that was in the sight of Allah a great (sin)﴾, meaning a great sin.

Ma'mar related from al-Zuhri that al-Aliya bint Zabyan, whom the Prophet ﷺ divorced, married a man and bore him a child, and that was before the wives of the Prophet ﷺ were made forbidden to people.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 54:

﴿Whether you disclose something or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things.﴾ It was revealed concerning the one who harboured the intention of marrying ʿĀʾishah after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [[Narrated by Ibn Jarir: 22/40. al-Suyuti, in al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/644, attributed it to al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Saʿd.]].

It is also said: a man from among the Companions said, "Why are we prevented from entering upon the daughters of our paternal uncles?" So this verse was revealed.

When the verse of the hijab was revealed, the fathers, the sons, and the relatives said, "We too speak to them from behind the screen?" So Allah revealed: [[See: al-Tabari: 22/41-42.]].

﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, their sons, their brothers, the sons of their brothers, or the sons of their sisters﴾. That is, there is no sin upon them for not veiling from these people. ﴿Nor their women﴾. It was said: he meant Muslim women, so it is not permissible for non-Muslim women (al-kitabiyyat, women of the People of the Book) to enter upon them. It was also said: it is general, covering both Muslim women and women of the Book. He only said "nor their women" because they are of their own kind. ﴿Nor those whom their right hands possess﴾.

They differed over whether a woman's slave is a mahram (a person she may appear before without veil) for her or not.

Some people said he is a mahram for her, based on the words of the Mighty and Majestic: "nor those whom their right hands possess."

Others said: he is like a stranger, and the verse refers to female slaves (imaa') only, not male slaves (abid).

﴿And fear Allah﴾, lest anyone other than these see you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things,﴾ of the deeds of the servants, ﴿Witness﴾.

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: he meant that Allah shows mercy to the Prophet, and the angels supplicate for him. It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "yusalluna" means "they seek blessing (yatabarrakun)."

It was said: blessing (salah) from Allah means mercy, and from the angels means seeking forgiveness.

﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him﴾, that is, supplicate for him with mercy, ﴿and greet him with greeting﴾, that is, salute him with the greeting of Islam.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: the blessing of Allah is His praise of him before the angels, and the blessing of the angels is supplication.

I said: "Yes, give it to me." He said: "We asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and we said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how is the blessing upon you, the People of the House?' He said: 'Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim and upon the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.'" [[Related by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, chapter: "Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet..." (the verse), 8/532, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 3/190.]]

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Say: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, his wives and his offspring, as You sent blessings upon Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad, his wives and his offspring, as You blessed the family of Ibrahim; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious." [[Related by al-Bukhari in Da'awat, chapter: Does one send blessings upon anyone other than the Prophet ﷺ? 11/169; Muslim in Salat, chapter: Sending blessings upon the Prophet after the tashahhud, no. ﴿There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, their sons, their brothers, the sons of their brothers, or the sons of their sisters﴾. They differed over whether a woman's slave is a mahram (a person she may appear before without veil) for her or not.

Some people said he is a mahram for her, based on the words of the Mighty and Majestic: "nor those whom their right hands possess."

Others said: he is like a stranger, and the verse refers to female slaves (imaa') only, not male slaves (abid).

﴿And fear Allah﴾, lest anyone other than these see you. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things,﴾ of the deeds of the servants, ﴿Witness﴾.

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: he meant that Allah shows mercy to the Prophet, and the angels supplicate for him. It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "yusalluna" means "they seek blessing (yatabarrakun)."
