Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 57:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Indeed, those who abuse Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: They are the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists. As for the Jews, they said, "'Uzayr is the son of Allah," and "The Hand of Allah is chained," and they said, "Allah is poor." As for the Christians, they said, "The Messiah is the son of Allah," and "He is the third of three." As for the polytheists, they said, "The angels are the daughters of Allah," and "The idols are His partners."

And it has been related to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah, glorified and exalted be He, says: My servant has insulted Me by saying, 'Allah has taken a son,' whereas I am the One, the Eternal Refuge, who has not begotten nor been begotten, and there is none comparable to Me." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the commentary on "Say, He is Allah, the One" (Qul huwa Allahu Ahad): 8/739, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said the Prophet (ﷺ) said: Allah the Exalted said: The son of Adam has denied Me, and he had no right to do so; and he has insulted Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying, "He will not restore me as He originated me," and... As for his insulting Me, it is his saying, "Allah has taken a son," whereas I am the One, the Eternal Refuge, who has not begotten nor been begotten, and there is none comparable to Me.]]

And it has been related to us from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The son of Adam harms Me; he curses time, while I am Time. In My hand is the affair; I turn the night and the day.﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the commentary of Surat al-Jathiya: 8/574, and Muslim in the Book of Words (al-Alfaz), chapter: the prohibition of cursing time, no. 2246, 4/1762.]]

It has also been said: the meaning of "abuse Allah" is that they deviate concerning His names and attributes.

'Ikrima said: They are the makers of images (pictures).

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muhammad ibn al-ʿAla' informed us, Ibn Fudayl informed us, from ʿUmara, from Abu Zur'a, who heard Abu Hurayra say: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Allah the Exalted said: Who is more unjust than one who sets out to create as I create? Let them create an atom, or let them create a grain or a barleycorn." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tawhid, chapter on the saying of Allah the Exalted: "Allah created you and what you do" 13/528, and Muslim in the Book of Clothing and Adornment, chapter: the prohibition of making pictures of living beings, no. 2111, 3/1671, and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 12/129.]]

Some of them said: "Abuse Allah" means: they abuse the friends of Allah, as in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And ask the town﴾ [Yusuf: 82], meaning: ask the people of the town.

And it has been related to us from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I have declared war against him; and whoever humiliates a friend of Mine, has challenged Me to battle.﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Softening of Hearts (al-Riqaq), chapter: humility, 11/340-341.]]

The meaning of harm (adha) is opposing the command of Allah the Exalted and committing His disobedience; it is mentioned according to what people commonly understand among themselves, whereas Allah, mighty and majestic, is far exalted above any harm reaching Him from anyone. As for harming the Messenger, Ibn 'Abbas said: it is that he was wounded in his face and his front tooth (rubaʿiyya) was broken. It was also said: he was called a poet, a sorcerer, a teacher, and a madman.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 58–59:

﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women without their having earned [it]﴾ — meaning, without their knowing anything that would make harming them obligatory. Mujahid said: they fall upon them and accuse them without any offence. ﴿Then they have certainly borne a slander and a manifest sin.﴾

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning ʿAli ibn Abi Talib [and that is because some of the hypocrites (munafiqun) used to harm him and revile him] [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 420. What is between the brackets we have supplemented from it. See also al-Qurtubi: 14/420.]].

It was also said: it was revealed concerning the matter of ʿA'ishah [[Refer to the earlier discussion in the tafsir of Surat al-Nur, verse 11 and what follows.]].

al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning the fornicators who used to walk along the roads of Madinah, following women when they went out at night to attend to their needs. They would make a gesture at a woman, and if she remained silent they would follow her, but if she rebuked them they would desist from her. They would seek only slave women, but they could not tell a free woman from a slave woman, because the dress of all of them was the same: free and slave women went out in a long shift (dir') and a veil (khimar). So the women complained of this to their husbands, who mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed: ﴿And those who harm believing men and believing women﴾ [[Mentioned by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 420, and he said: the proof of the soundness of this is the words of Allah, the Exalted: "O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers..." (verse). **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 33, verses 67–69:**

﴿They will say, "Our Lord, we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they led us astray from the way."﴾ Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqub read "سَادَاتِنَا" (sādātinā) with a kasra on the tāʾ and an alif before it, as the plural of a plural (jamʿ al-jamʿ). The others read it with a fatha on the tāʾ and no alif before it. ﴿And our elders (kubarāʾanā), and they led us astray from the way.﴾

﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment from the Fire﴾, meaning double the punishment of others. ﴿And curse them with a great curse.﴾ ʿĀṣim read "كَبِيرًا" (kabīran) with the letter bāʾ. Al-Kalbi said: that is, a great punishment. The others read it with the letter thāʾ ("كَثِيرًا", kathīran), in line with God's words: ﴿Upon them is the curse of God, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together﴾ [al-Baqarah: 161]. This supports the meaning of multiplicity, that is, time after time.

His saying, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa, but God cleared him of what they said﴾, meaning God purified him of what they said. ﴿And he was honourable with God﴾: noble and possessing standing. It is said: "wajuha al-rajul yūjahu wajāhatan fahuwa wajīh" when a man has standing and rank.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: he was favoured by God; he never asked God for anything except that He gave it to him.

Al-Hasan said: his supplication was always answered.

It was also said: he was beloved and accepted.

They differed concerning what Musa was harmed with:

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us, Rawh ibn ʿUbadah informed us, ʿAwf informed us, from al-Hasan, Muhammad, and Khilas, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Musa was a shy man, very modest, and none of his skin was seen out of modesty. So those among the Children of Israel who harmed him said: 'He conceals himself in this way only because of a defect in his skin: either leprosy, or a swelling of the testicles, or some other ailment.' God wished to clear him of what they said. One day he was alone, so he placed his garments on a rock and bathed. When he finished, he approached his garments to take them, but the rock ran off with his garment. Musa took his staff and went after the rock, saying: 'My garment, O rock! My garment, O rock!' until he came to an assembly of the Children of Israel, who saw him naked, the most beautiful of God's creation, and God cleared him of what they said. The rock stopped, he took his garment, put it on, and began striking the rock with his staff. By God, there are marks on the rock from the striking, three or four or five times." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya': 6/436.] This is the meaning of His saying, exalted and majestic: "O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa, but God cleared him of what they said, and he was honourable with God."

Others said: their harming of him was that when Harun died in the wilderness (al-tih), they claimed that Musa had killed him. God commanded the angels, and they carried him past the Children of Israel, who then knew that he had not killed him, so God cleared him of what they said. [See al-Tabari: 22/52; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/666. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath 8/538: "Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated in his Musnad," and al-Tabari and Ibn Abi Hatim with a strong chain from Ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿAli, who said: "Musa and Harun ascended the mountain, and Harun died. The Children of Israel said to Musa: 'You killed him; he was gentler to us than you and more beloved.' So they harmed him with that. God commanded the angels, and they carried him and passed by the assemblies of the Children of Israel, and they knew of his death."]

Abu al-ʿAliyah said: it was that Qarun hired a prostitute to throw herself at Musa before the assembly, but God protected her and cleared Musa of that, and destroyed Qarun. [See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/441–442; Zad al-Masir: 6/426.]

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Abu al-Walid informed us, Shuʿbah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, who said: I heard Abu Wa'il say: I heard ʿAbd Allah say: The Prophet (ﷺ) distributed a portion, and a man said: "This is a distribution by which the face of God was not sought." I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and he became angry, until I saw the anger in his face. Then he said: "May God have mercy on Musa; he was harmed with more than this and he was patient." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, chapter: "Patience upon harm": 10/511; and Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter: "Giving to those whose hearts are to be reconciled to Islam," no. 1062, 2/739; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/239.]

My garment, O rock!' until he came to an assembly of the Children of Israel, who saw him naked, the most beautiful of God's creation, and God cleared him of what they said. The rock stopped, he took his garment, put it on, and began striking the rock with his staff. By God, there are marks on the rock from the striking, three or four or five times." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya': 6/436.] This is the meaning of His saying, exalted and majestic: "O you who believe, do not be like those who harmed Musa, but God cleared him of what they said, and he was honourable with God."

Others said: their harming of him was that when Harun died in the wilderness (al-tih), they claimed that Musa had killed him. God commanded the angels, and they carried him past the Children of Israel, who then knew that he had not killed him, so God cleared him of what they said. [See al-Tabari: 22/52; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/666. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath 8/538: "Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated in his Musnad," and al-Tabari and Ibn Abi Hatim with a strong chain from Ibn ʿAbbas, from ʿAli, who said: "Musa and Harun ascended the mountain, and Harun died. The Children of Israel said to Musa: 'You killed him; he was gentler to us than you and more beloved.' So they harmed him with that. God commanded the angels, and they carried him and passed by the assemblies of the Children of Israel, and they knew of his death."]

Abu al-ʿAliyah said: it was that Qarun hired a prostitute to throw herself at Musa before the assembly, but God protected her and cleared Musa of that, and destroyed Qarun. [See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/441–442; Zad al-Masir: 6/426.]

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Abu al-Walid informed us, Shuʿbah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, who said: I heard Abu Wa'il say: I heard ʿAbd Allah say: The Prophet (ﷺ) distributed a portion, and a man said: "This is a distribution by which the face of God was not sought." I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and he became angry, until I saw the anger in his face. Then he said: "May God have mercy on Musa; he was harmed with more than this and he was patient." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, chapter: "Patience upon harm": 10/511; and Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter: "Giving to those whose hearts are to be reconciled to Islam," no. 1062, 2/739; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/239.]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 33, verses 67–69:**

﴿They will say, "Our Lord, we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they led us astray from the way."﴾ Ibn ʿĀmir and Yaʿqub read "سَادَاتِنَا" (sādātinā) with a kasra on the tāʾ and an alif before it, as the plural of a plural (jamʿ al-jamʿ). The others read it with a fatha on the tāʾ and no alif before it. ﴿And our elders (kubarāʾanā), and they led us astray from the way.﴾

﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment from the Fire﴾, meaning double the punishment of others. ﴿And curse them with a great curse.﴾ ʿĀṣim read "كَبِيرًا" (kabīran) with the letter bāʾ. Al-Kalbi said: that is, a great punishment. The others read it with the letter thāʾ ("كَثِيرًا", kathīran), in line with God's words: ﴿Upon them is the curse of God, and of the angels, and of mankind, all together﴾ [al-Baqarah: 161]. This supports the meaning of multiplicity, that is, time after time.

It is said: "wajuha al-rajul yūjahu wajāhatan fahuwa wajīh" when a man has standing and rank.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: he was favoured by God; he never asked God for anything except that He gave it to him.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 70–71:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Correct (sawaban)." Qatadah said: "Just (adlan)." Al-Hasan said: "Truthful (sidqan)." It was also said: "Upright (mustaqiman)." 'Ikrimah said: it is the statement "There is no god but Allah" (qawl La ilaha illa Allah).

﴿He will amend for you your deeds﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He will accept your good deeds. Muqatil said: He will purify your deeds. ﴿And forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great attainment﴾, meaning: he has gained all good.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 33, verse 72:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾ – the verse. He meant by the trust (amanah) obedience and the obligations (fara'id) that Allah imposed upon His servants. He offered it to the heavens, the earth and the mountains on the condition that if they fulfilled it He would reward them, and if they neglected it He would punish them. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Mas'ud said: The trust is performing the prayers, paying the zakah, fasting Ramadan, performing the Hajj to the House, truthfulness in speech, repaying debts, and justice in measure and weight; and greater than all of these are deposits (al-wada'i').

Mujahid said: The trust is the obligations and the repayment of debts.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: It is what they were commanded to do and forbidden from doing.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is fasting, the ghusl from janabah (ritual impurity), and what is concealed of the sacred laws (shara'i').

'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As said: The first thing Allah created in man was his private part (farj), and He said: "This is a trust I have deposited with you." So the private part is a trust, the ear is a trust, the eye is a trust, the hand is a trust, the foot is a trust, and there is no faith for one who has no trustworthiness.

Some of them said: It is the trusts of people and the fulfilment of covenants. It is incumbent upon every believer that he not deceive a believer or a covenant-partner (mu'ahad) in anything, small or great. This is the narration of al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas. So Allah offered this trust to the very entities (a'yan) of the heavens, the earth and the mountains. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, a group of the Tabi'un, and most of the early scholars (al-salaf). He said to them: "Will you bear this trust with what is in it?" They said: "And what is in it?" He said: "If you do good, you will be rewarded, and if you disobey, you will be punished." They said: "No, O Lord, we are subjected to Your command; we do not want reward or punishment." They said this out of fear, awe and reverence for the religion of Allah, lest they fail to uphold it, not out of disobedience or opposition. The offering to them was a matter of choice, not compulsion; had He compelled them, they would not have refused to bear it. All inanimate things are humbly subject to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, obedient and prostrating before Him, as He said, may His remembrance be exalted, to the heavens and the earth: "Come willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly" [Fussilat: 11], and He said of the stones: "And indeed, among them is that which falls down out of fear of Allah" [al-Baqarah: 74], and Almighty Allah said: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures﴾ [al-Hajj: 18] – the verse.

Some of the people of knowledge said: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, placed in them intellect and understanding when He offered the trust to them, so that they comprehended the address and responded with what they responded.

Some of them said: The meaning of the offering to the heavens and the earth is the offering to the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth; He offered it to those in them among the angels.

It was also said: It means to its people entirely, not to their very entities, like His saying: "And ask the town" [Yusuf: 82], meaning the people of the town. The first view is more correct, and it is the saying of the scholars.

﴿But they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it﴾, i.e., they feared from the trust that they would not discharge it, so that punishment would befall them. ﴿And man bore it﴾, meaning Adam, peace be upon him. Allah said to Adam: "Indeed, I offered the trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains, and they could not bear it. Will you take it with what is in it?" He said: "O Lord, and what is in it?" He said: "If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished." So Adam bore it, and said: "Between my ear and my shoulder." Allah, the Exalted, said: "As for when you have borne it, I will help you. Make a screen for your sight, so that when you fear looking at what is not lawful for you, you lower its screen. Make a lock for your tongue, so that when you are overcome, you close it. And make a garment for your private part, so that you do not uncover it in what I have forbidden you."

Mujahid said: The time between his bearing it and his leaving the Garden was only the period between midday (zuhr) and afternoon ('asr). [[See: Ibn Kathir: 3/523-524.]]

Al-Naqqash related with his chain from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: The trust was likened to a rock lying [on the ground], and the heavens, the earth and the mountains were called to it, but they did not draw near to it and said: "We cannot bear it." Adam came without being called, shook the rock and said: "If I were commanded to carry it, I would carry it." They said to him: "Carry it." So he carried it up to his knees, then set it down, and said: "By Allah, if I wished to add to it, I would have added." They said to him: "Carry it," so he carried it up to his waist, then set it down, and said: "By Allah, if I wished to add to it, I would have added." They said to him: "Carry it," so he carried it until he placed it on his shoulder. He then wished to set it down, but Allah said: "Stay where you are, for it is upon your neck and the necks of your offspring until the Day of Resurrection."

﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: a wrongdoer to himself, ignorant of the command of Allah and of what he had taken on of the trust.

Al-Kalbi said: a wrongdoer when he disobeyed his Lord, ignorant, not knowing the punishment for abandoning the trust. Muqatil said: a wrongdoer to himself, ignorant of the consequence of what he undertook.

Al-Zajjaj and others among the scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) mentioned, regarding His saying "and man bore it," two opinions. They said: Allah entrusted Adam and his children with something, and entrusted the heavens, the earth and the mountains with something. So the trust with regard to the children of Adam is what we have mentioned concerning obedience and carrying out the obligations, while the trust with regard to the heavens, the earth and the mountains is submission and obedience to that for which they were created. It was also said: His saying ﴿But they refused to bear it﴾ means they discharged the trust (addaw al-amanah). It is said: "So-and-so did not bear the trust," meaning he did not betray in it; and "man bore it" means he betrayed in it. It is said: "So-and-so bore the trust," meaning he sinned in it by betrayal.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they will surely bear their burdens﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 13]. ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer, ignorant.﴾ It is related from al-Hasan, according to this interpretation, that he said: "And man bore it" means the disbeliever and the hypocrite; they both bore the trust, i.e., they betrayed. The saying of the early scholars is what we have mentioned.

**Al-Baghawi's commentary on the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:** ﴿So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women, and that Allah may turn in mercy to the believing men and the believing women. And Allah is ever Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾

Muqatil said: "He will punish them for betraying the trust and breaking the covenant. ﴿And Allah will turn to the believing men and the believing women, and Allah is ever Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾ He guides them and shows mercy to them for having fulfilled the trust."

Ibn Qutaybah said: "That is, We presented the trust so that the hypocrisy of the hypocrite and the polytheism of the polytheist would become manifest, and Allah would punish them both. And the faith of the believer would become manifest, and Allah would turn to him, that is, return to him with mercy and forgiveness if he fell short in some of the acts of obedience."
